head: Security
title: Security
text: - Admin switch chat.android, off. Once released it works for every profile; only the admin blocks single profiles (People and devices → Blocked functions). Never guests. - The app has no key of its own: it uses its page's login (cookie). Signing out in the page ends it. - The app only loads pages of its own Spark (same address and port), everything else opens in the browser; https only, system certificates. Microphone only for the own Spark page. - #ask= only puts shared text into the text field, nothing is ever sent by itself; both jumps only work in the app. - The APK only comes from GitHub's download addresses with matching size and SHA-256. The download link carries a one-time token (only its hash in memory, 30 minutes, at most 5 downloads); without a valid link 404. - Update in the app: its own admin switch chat.android_update (off), blockable per profile; GET /api/android/apk only with the profile's browser login (no device key), rate limit, hands out only the APK the Spark checked when fetching it. The app follows no redirect and trusts only its own address; Android installs over the installed app only when the signing key matches. The page hands the app nothing: the button

head: Security
title: Security
text: is the fixed link sparkapp:update the app catches. Log: android: app update … sent to … or … refused … reason …. - Notes stay in memory only (24 hours, at most 30 per profile) and only go to the profile's own login. - Spark as assistant: its own admin switch chat.android_assist (off), blockable per profile, never guests. The Spark checks every question of the sheet itself (device "android"); without the release it answers 403 and logs android: assistant refused for … reason …. The app learns the release only from /api/profile/android and shows or hides widget, tile and shortcuts by it. The microphone runs only while the sheet is open and the question lasts (at most 30 seconds); on the lock screen only after unlocking. The widget shows numbers only, never titles or names of appointments and messages. Waiting questions stay in the app only (at most 10, one day). - Shared files go through the Spark's normal ways (/api/chat/image, /api/profile/docs) with their rights, size and rate limits; the app reads only content addresses (content://), no file paths. - Last state: admin switch chat.app_cache (on in the basic set), blockable per profile. The page keeps only inside the app (mark "Spa

head: Security
title: Security
text: rkAndroid/") and only while /api/profile/settings says "app_keep"; when the Spark says no it deletes everything. The copy lies in the app's page storage (in the app's encrypted storage, apart per profile), never keys, codes, admin pages or files. Signing out and another profile delete it. A browser keeps nothing this way (that is "Read history offline" with a trusted browser). - Fingerprint for admins: its own admin switch chat.android_lock (off); it applies only to a login with an admin role. A phone without any screen lock has nothing to check: the app says so and opens.

head: New version
title: New version
text: Raise name and code in android/version.properties and push to main: the action builds, signs and publishes android-v<name>; the Spark fetches it and the apps say so.

head: APIs (OpenAI-style)
title: APIs (OpenAI-style)
text: Both services answer GET /health with status and counters. GET /v1/voices (TTS) lists the voices and GET /v1/models the loaded model.

head: APIs (OpenAI-style)
title: APIs (OpenAI-style)
text: Speech recognition accepts anything ffmpeg can read (wav, mp3, webm, mp4, ogg …) and long recordings. language is a code (de) or a name (German); without it the model detects the language. response_format is json, text or verbose_json (with language and duration, without timestamps). With -F stream=true the text arrives in pieces as Server-Sent Events in OpenAI format (transcription.chunk, then [DONE]).

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: With "stream": true (and "response_format": "pcm", the default then) the answer arrives as Server-Sent Events as soon as the first sounds are generated:

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: audio is PCM, 16 bit, mono, 24 kHz. Errors arrive as speech.audio.error. This is vllm-omni's format, passed through unchanged.

head: Streaming speech
title: Steadier delivery
text: Steadier delivery: Qwen samples with temperature 0.9 and top_p 1.0 by default, so tempo and emphasis vary from sentence to sentence. The server therefore applies temperature 0.7, top_p 0.9 and seed 42 (Settings → Speech output). Requests can override them with the same fields, top-level or inside extra_params. In Open WebUI, set response splitting to paragraphs: each part is generated separately, and longer parts sound more coherent. Set the default language to a fixed language instead of auto.

head: Streaming speech
title: Laughing and mood swings
text: Laughing and mood swings: the model reads emojis, "haha", *laughs* and markdown as cues and laughs or changes tone. The server removes them before synthesis (Settings → Speech output → clean text, on by default).

head: Streaming speech
title: Overacting
text: Overacting: exclamation marks and interjections ("Oh", "Wow") make the voice act out excitement. With "speak calmly" (on by default) the server turns "!" into "." and drops such interjections at the start of a sentence. The default voice-chat prompt also asks the LLM for plain, calm everyday language.

head: Streaming speech
title: Numbers
text: Numbers: the server writes numbers out before synthesis, because the model guesses otherwise. Dates, times, money, percent and decimals become words ("on 2026-10-06 at 9:30, $49.90" → "on October sixth, twenty twenty-six at nine thirty, forty-nine dollars ninety"), phone numbers become pairs. Settings → Speech output → reading numbers: as words (default), in pairs, digit by digit or unchanged. Works for German and English.

head: Streaming speech
title: Speaking style
text: Speaking style: "instructions": "calm and friendly, rather slow" in the request. Without it, the default instruction from Settings → Speech output applies. Only the 1.7B models (CustomVoice, VoiceDesign) follow instructions; the 0.6B models ignore them (per the Qwen model card).

head: Streaming speech
title: VoiceDesign
text: VoiceDesign (voice from a description): "task_type": "VoiceDesign" and "instructions": "deep, calm male voice". This needs its own model: enable "VoiceDesign zusätzlich bereitstellen" in Settings → Speech output. It starts a second engine with the same memory footprint again.

head: Streaming speech
title: Streaming speech
text: In the panel under Status → Checks, "streamed" plays audio while it is generated and shows the time to first audio.

head: General
title: General
text: The services behave like the OpenAI audio API: TTS returns mp3 by default (also wav, flac, opus, pcm), STT understands response_format=text, and the language may be an ISO code like de. OpenAI voice names like alloy fall back to the default voice. If an API key is set in the panel, apps must send Authorization: Bearer <key>.

head: Open WebUI
title: Open WebUI
text: If Open WebUI runs in Docker on the same Spark, use the LAN IP or host.docker.internal instead of SPARK (container started with --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway). The panel shows these values ready to copy under People and devices → Apps and interfaces.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: An agent such as Hermes Agent (Nous Research) or OpenClaw can use the Spark's speech recognition and speech output. The agent runs on another computer and only gets audio and text to read out, no access to the assistant's profiles, memory or tools. The panel shows ready-made snippets under People and devices → Apps and interfaces.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: OpenClaw: tts.provider: "openai" with tts.providers.openai.baseUrl = http://SPARK:31002/v1 (plus apiKey, model, speakerVoice, responseFormat: "mp3"), and for voice messages an entry in tools.media.models with provider: "openai", baseUrl = http://SPARK:31001/v1 and capabilities: ["audio"]; store the key as an OpenAI API key profile.

head: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
title: AI agents: Hermes Agent and OpenClaw
text: Do not install the agent on the Spark itself: it runs commands and could reach settings and keys. Without an API key anyone on the home network can use the speech services.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Spark as an MCP server
text: Other programs use the Spark over the Model Context Protocol (Streamable HTTP, the panel's address /mcp, e.g. http://SPARK:31080/mcp). Off by default.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Switching on
text: Switching on: admin: Features → *Spark as MCP server*. This works for every profile; only the admin blocks single profiles (People and devices → Blocked functions). Setup in the profile: Me → *Services over MCP* → "Connect a program with a key": name, tools, "Create key". The key is shown once; enter it in the program as the header Authorization: Bearer <key>.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Rules (fixed, no switch)
text: Rules (fixed, no switch): - Each access belongs to one profile and can only use the tools the profile gave it and may use itself right now. Never to the outside: mail, memory, earlier conversations, secrets, settings. - "Home network only" (default): the key works only for requests straight from the LAN, without proxy headers and not from a listed reverse proxy. - ask_spark: the question counts as outside text. Nothing is switched, saved, learned, sent or proposed; nothing of it lands in the conversations. - Acting: a program only leaves a proposal. The profile gets a notification and decides under Me → Spark as MCP server ("Yes, do it" with the code window, or "No"). A proposal waits 15 minutes. - Limits: 60 calls per minute and access (ask_spark 10), 2 at once per access, 6 overall; speech runs with the stage "last", people at the Spark go first. Without use an access ends after 90 days. - The journal shows each request as mcp-server: with program, tool and time, never the content. - Status → Live (since V01.0.334) shows each tool call as its own request "MCP-Client" with tool and target (speech as hearing or speaking, a proposal as "Bestätigung anfragen" → push, a confirmed acti

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Rules (fixed, no switch)
text: on as its own request); the access's name shows only with the profile's consent ("My name in the request log"), contents never. ask_spark shows like a conversation.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: From outside (OAuth)
text: From outside (OAuth): admin: *MCP server from outside* below the switch. An access "from outside" needs the profile's second sign-in step and a fresh code. Programs like claude.ai sign in with OAuth 2.1 (dynamic registration, PKCE S256, /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server): add a custom MCP connector with https://your-proxy/mcp in the program, it sends you to the panel, there you see a warning, pick the tools and confirm with your code. Access tokens last 1 hour, refresh tokens 30 days and are swapped with every use. Everything such a program reads goes to its provider.

head: Spark as an MCP server
title: Examples
text: Examples: Open WebUI: Settings → External tools → "+", type MCP (Streamable HTTP). n8n: node "MCP Client Tool". Programs without a header field: npx mcp-remote http://SPARK:31080/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <key>".

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Own MCP services per profile
text: Since V01.0.363 (plan plaene/eigene-mcp-dienste.md) every profile can connect its own MCP services (Streamable HTTP), besides the ones the admin connects for everybody. Only that profile sees and uses them.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Switching on
text: Switching on: Admin: Features → Jobs → Services over MCP → *Own MCP services for profiles* (chat.mcp_own), below it *… also in background jobs* (chat.mcp_own_jobs) and *… with sign-in (OAuth)* (chat.mcp_own_oauth); all off. Once released it works for every profile; only the admin blocks single profiles. Setup in the profile: Me → *My MCP services*, enter name, address and key and "Connect service". The profile needs no agent level for this.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Rules (fixed)
text: Rules (fixed): - At most 5 services per profile, each with at most 30 tools. Every tool is "Off" until the profile sets it to "Read" or "Act after yes". If the service changes a tool's description or inputs, it is "Off" again after "Fetch tools again". - Never for guests, never for other profiles, never for a foreign voice at a speaker (only when speech recognition surely heard the profile's own voice), over Telegram only with "private data". - Connecting a service, a new address, a new key: only in the profile's own browser login with a fresh code (second sign-in step, when set up). A new address always needs a new key; all tools are "Off" again then. Keys and sign-in data are kept encrypted (vault), never sent back, never logged. - Connections through the guard (netguard.USER): public addresses with https; home network addresses (also http) only when the admin allows them under Security; the Spark's own services (ports 30000–31099) never. - "Read": the answer is outside text (framed, the assistant switches and saves nothing more in that answer, never learned). "Act after yes": only a proposal; carried out after a plain "Yes" in the next message from the same device and conversati

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Rules (fixed)
text: on, for 15 minutes, never after outside text, never in background jobs, not during Notaus stage 2 or "Mein Notaus". - Limits: 30 seconds per call, at most 2 MB read, 8000 characters to the model, arguments at most 4000 characters, 10 calls per minute and 2 at once per profile. - Background jobs (with the admin switch and the box ticked at the service): reading tools only, only in jobs with private data. - Sign-in (OAuth): if the service wants a sign-in, leave the key empty and tap "Sign in at the service". The Spark reads the service's sign-in addresses (protected resource metadata, authorization server metadata), registers there as a program (dynamic registration, PKCE S256, resource), the browser signs in at the service and comes back through /api/mymcp/back (this address changes nothing, it hands code and state to the signed-in page, 10 minutes, once). Access and refresh token are kept encrypted; the Spark renews the access before it ends.

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Admin
text: Admin: People and devices → Apps and interfaces → *Profiles' own MCP services*: profile, name, address (host only), number of released tools, last fetched, never a key. "Block" applies at once and also when the profile connects the service again; "Remove" deletes it with its key. Optionally a list of allowed hosts (empty: every public one; an entry also allows its subdomains).

head: Own MCP services per profile
title: Visible
text: Visible: Status → Live shows each call as a step to the target "MCP-Dienste" and under events "MCP: service · host · ok or error · duration", plus connected, removed, signed in, blocked; never question, arguments or answer, never the profile's name. Me → My status shows one row per service (answers, sign-in needed, blocked). The guard's decisions show under Live as always.

head: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
title: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
text: Since V01.0.552 (Synology plan S7, guide only, no code in the Spark). If you would rather offer your files through an MCP program of your own on the Synology than through knowledge folders, docs/vorlagen/nas-mcp has a hardened template for Container Manager: a file server (@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem behind supergateway, Streamable HTTP) with a doorman (nginx) in front that only lets /mcp through with the right key.

head: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
title: Honestly first
text: Honestly first: knowledge folders (Me → Storage) are the better way for almost everyone: no third-party program, the Spark reads by itself, everything through the Wächter and in Live. An MCP container is third-party software on your NAS with access to the folder you give it. It is as safe as its dependencies, and you have to build updates yourself. Only use it when you know exactly why.

head: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
title: What the template fixes
text: What the template fixes: - Base images only by digest (node:22-alpine@sha256:…, nginx-unprivileged@sha256:…), fixed package versions, npm ci at build time instead of npm install at every start, without install scripts. - The folder read-only (/volume1/dokumente:/data:ro), plus read_only: true, user: "1000:1000", cap_drop: [ALL], security_opt: no-new-privileges, memory and process limits. - The file server sits only in the internal network (internal: true): no port, no internet. Only the doorman faces outward, and only on 127.0.0.1:8765. - Reachable only through the NAS's reverse proxy with HTTPS and a valid certificate (the Spark checks it and refuses a self-signed one). The doorman requires Authorization: Bearer <key> and does not pass the key on.

head: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
title: Setup
text: Setup: 1. Copy the four files to the NAS (e.g. /volume1/docker/nas-mcp). Run npm install --package-lock-only once (another computer will do) so package-lock.json pins the exact versions. 2. Enter both digests (the commands are in the files), adjust the folder in compose.yaml, replace SCHLUESSEL in nginx.conf with a long random value (openssl rand -hex 32). 3. Container Manager → Project → Create, choose the path, take compose.yaml, build and start. 4. DSM → Control Panel → Login Portal → Advanced → Reverse Proxy → Create: source HTTPS with its own port or name, destination HTTP localhost:8765. Assign a certificate under Security → Certificate. 5. Spark: the admin turns on Features → Jobs → Services over MCP → *Own MCP services for profiles* and, since the NAS is in the home network, Settings → Security → *Allow home network addresses*. 6. Profile: Me → *My MCP services*: name "NAS files", address https://<NAS>:<port>/mcp, the key, "Connect service". Under "Release tools" set only the reading tools (read_text_file, list_directory, search_files, get_file_info …) to "Read"; everything that writes, moves or creates stays "Off" (the folder is mounted read-only anyway).

head: Advanced: MCP server on the NAS
title: Off
text: Off: remove the service in the Spark (the key is deleted), stop the project on the NAS and delete the reverse proxy rule. A new key: change it in nginx.conf, restart the doorman, enter the service again in the Spark with the new key.

head: "Hey Siri, ask Spark"
title: "Hey Siri, ask Spark"
text: An iPhone shortcut sends the dictated question to POST /api/siri/ask (header X-Speech-Device with a device key of your profile, body {"text": "..."}) and lets Siri speak the answer field. Works without the page open, also on Apple Watch, AirPods and CarPlay; follow-ups within 10 minutes keep the context, and each day's questions are kept as a conversation of the profile. Step by step under People and devices → Apps and interfaces and in Features → Guides.

head: iPhone app "Spark"
title: iPhone app "Spark"
text: Own iPhone app with the Spark voice and "Hey Siri, Frag Spark", paired by QR code, its own key per iPhone that may only ask and listen. Building, pairing and security: iphone-app.md.

head: Chats between profiles (for the iPhone app)
title: Chats between profiles (for the iPhone app)
text: Since V01.0.488 messages between profiles go through chats only; /api/messages… no longer exists. With the profile's browser login or the iPhone app's key (header X-Speech-Device), only when the admin switched on "Chats" and the profile "Chats with others"; other device keys get 403. - GET /api/chats: enabled, on, chats (each id, kind, title, unread, mute, last, the group "Alle" with fixed), contacts (id, name, call), all (takes part in "Alle"), speakers (for announcements), max_text. - POST /api/chats/open {"to": "<profile id>"} returns the id of the chat for two; POST /api/chats/send {"id", "text"} writes into it (into "Alle" at most 5 an hour). - POST /api/chats/announce {"speakers": [id], "text"}: an announcement on picked speakers (admin switch "Announcements on speakers"). - Browser only: GET/PUT /api/chats/who {"allow"?, "block"?} ("Who may write to me") and PUT /api/chats/call {"call"} (own call name, unique). Admin: GET /api/admin/profiles?q=&show=&sort=&page=&per= (at most 100 per page), GET /api/admin/profiles/<id>, PUT /api/admin/profiles/<id>/call.

head: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: Between Sparks (open, a signature instead of a login): GET /.well-known/spark-verbund returns {"v": 1, "key": "<Ed25519, base64>", "inbox": "/api/verbund/in"}, only while "Chats with other Sparks" is on. POST /api/verbund/in takes JSON up to 32 KB with the headers X-Spark-From: <sender's domain> and X-Spark-Sig: <base64>; signed is spark-verbund v1\n<receiver's domain>\n<body>. Body: v, t (Unix time, ±600 s), n (32 hex characters, once), type (pair, ask, yes, msg, read, edit, back, react, for groups gadd, gmsg, gleave, gremove, gname, gmembers), from/to (the part before the @), by type name, id, text, reply, emoji, secret. The answer is always {"ok": true}, refusals 400/403/409/413/429 without a reason. For the profile (browser or iPhone app, switches as above): GET /api/verbund (own address, QR, contacts with state in/out/ok/block), POST /api/verbund/ask {"addr"}, POST /api/verbund/answer {"id", "act": "ok"|"no"|"block"|"unblock"}, POST /api/verbund/remove {"id"}, POST /api/verbund/open {"id"} (chat id). Admin: GET /api/admin/verbund, POST /api/admin/verbund/pair and /connect {"code"} (second step's code), POST /api/admin/verbund/peer {"domain", "act": "allow"|"block"|"remove"}.

head: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: Files (V01.0.568, switch "Photos and files to other Sparks"): POST /api/verbund/blob with the content as body, X-Spark-From, X-Spark-Blob (base64url of {"v": 1, "t", "n", "sha", "size"}) and X-Spark-Sig (signature as for messages over that head); then msg with "media": {"kind": "photo"|"file"|"voice", "sha", "size", "name"?}. Answers: 200, 400 (form, time, size, hash), 401 (no known, allowed Spark, or off), 403 (signature), 409 (repeated), 429 (daily limit).

head: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
title: Chats with other Sparks (V01.0.496)
text: Groups (V01.0.568, switch "Groups with other Sparks"): the group belongs to the Spark it was created on; gid is its chat id there. From it: gadd to one person (from is the admin, who must be an accepted contact of that person; name, members as a list of {"addr", "name"}), gmsg with id, text, reply, by (the author's address) and byname, once per Spark, gremove to one person, gname with name, gmembers with members. To it, with an empty to: gmsg (from is the member, id, text, reply) and gleave. The home Spark checks membership and passes a message on to all other Sparks, never back to the one it came from. Text only for now, at most 10 other Sparks per group.

head: Calls (V01.0.556)
title: Calls (V01.0.556)
text: Only in the profile's own browser (the Android app is one; never with a device key), admin switch "Calls (voice and video)", sound and picture go over WebRTC straight between the devices. dev is a random id of the page (12 hex characters), call the call's (16 hex characters). GET /api/anrufe/ice returns servers (empty without "Calls when away", else STUN/TURN with an access for one hour). POST /api/anrufe/start {"id", "video", "dev"} → {"call", "state": "ring"|"busy"|"missed", "servers"}; POST /api/anrufe/answer {"call", "dev"}; POST /api/anrufe/signal {"call", "dev", "data": {"sdp": {"type", "sdp"}} | {"ice": {…}}} (16 KB); POST /api/anrufe/end {"call", "dev", "why": "hangup"|"reject"} → {"line"}. News come over GET /api/chats/stream as call, call_ok, call_taken, call_sig (with to: only that device takes it) and call_end. Calls by the assistant (rufen.py): GET /api/chats has ruf (null or {"id", "name", "video", "secs"}: a call the assistant keeps for the profile); DELETE /api/anrufe/bereit → {"ok"} removes it ("Nicht jetzt"). In the answer stream of POST /api/chat after the yes {"type": "anruf", "id", "name", "video"} (the device starts the call) or on Android {"type": "waehlen",

head: Calls (V01.0.556)
title: Calls (V01.0.556)
text: "number"} (open the phone app).

head: Calendar apps (CalDAV, since V01.0.840)
title: Calendar apps (CalDAV, since V01.0.840)
text: The Spark is itself a CalDAV server for a profile's Spark calendars, so the iPhone's calendar app, Thunderbird or DAVx5 show and change them directly. Admin: Features → My day → "Calendar server for calendar apps" (off). The profile makes an app password under Calendar → Settings → "For calendar apps" (in its own browser login or in the iPhone app, with its code); it is shown once, only its hash is kept, "Delete access" ends it at once. In the app: server https://<address>/caldav/ (or just the address, /.well-known/caldav redirects), the user is the profile ID, the password the app password. Only the own Spark calendars are reachable, never iCloud or other accounts and never another profile. Wrong passwords lock like a PIN. Security: Ways in.

head: Contacts apps (CardDAV, since V01.0.897)
title: Contacts apps (CardDAV, since V01.0.897)
text: The Spark is also a CardDAV server for a profile's address book "On the Spark", so the iPhone's Contacts app, Thunderbird or DAVx5 show and change it directly. Admin: Features → Mail and contacts → "Contacts for contacts apps" (off; needs "Contacts" and "Calendar server for calendar apps"). Setup on the iPhone: Settings → Apps → Contacts → Accounts → Other → CardDAV account, server = the Spark's address with /carddav/, user = profile id, password = the calendar server's app password. The door is the same as for /caldav/ (wrong guesses lock like a PIN, rate limit "caldav", other sites' web pages refused, My emergency stop). Only the own address book, never iCloud address books and never another profile; one vCard per card with a name or company, at most 256 KB and 2000 cards; writing only with "Edit contacts", otherwise read-only.

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: The watch app "Spark" (app/pebble/speech-spark.pbw, source in pebble/) brings the voice chat to Pebble Time 2 and Core 2 Duo, with the answer as text and through the watch speaker. On Pebble Round 2 the answer is text only. It needs a watch firmware with the speaker API (from about v4.9.170).

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: 1. Pairing with a setup code (new in V01.0.230, off): the admin switches on *Features → Pair the Pebble watch* (works for every profile), the profile picks "Pair a Pebble" under *Me → Pebble watch* and copies the line (valid 10 minutes, once). The watch gets its own key, which only reaches /api/watch/ and is locked at once when the admin switches the feature off or blocks the profile. Without pairing it still works: add a device "Pebble" under People and devices and copy its key. 2. On the paired phone, download http://SPARK:31080/pebble/speech-spark.pbw and open it with the Pebble app. Easier: *Me → Pebble watch* shows a QR code for it to scan with the phone camera. When the Spark has a newer watch app, "Neue Uhr-App" shows under an answer at most once a day; reinstalling keeps the pairing. 3. In the Pebble app, open the settings of "Spark": paste the setup code, or enter the Spark address (http://SPARK:31080) and device key. Settings and "Start App" stay grey while the Pebble app does not see the watch as connected (tab Devices). 4. On the watch: SELECT asks (dictation through the phone), SELECT again stops the speech, long SELECT starts a new conversation. A small face at the to

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: p shows whether Spark listens, thinks or speaks; its mouth follows the speech. In the Pebble app: Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Volume caps how loud the app can get.

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: The phone must reach the Spark, at home over Wi-Fi, on the road through a VPN such as Tailscale or the address on the road (below). The app uses HTTP because the Pebble app does not trust the self-signed certificate. On the Spark, POST /api/watch/ask and GET /api/watch/poll serve it: the answer is made like in the voice chat (kept short), the audio is compressed for the small speaker (quiet syllables lifted, peaks softly limited) and goes to the watch as 8 kHz IMA ADPCM. Watch and phone retry lost messages; after 30 s without a message the watch gives up. At the end the phone sends the times to POST /api/watch/report; *Status → Logs* then shows one line watch: zeit … per answer in the area "Watch" (dictation, first text, first sound, done, retries, outcome). The watch shows the same face as the panel (robot, comic or comic woman), taken over with the next answer.

head: Pebble watch
title: More on the watch (watch app 2.0, package 1 of `pebble-ideen/plan.md`)
text: More on the watch (watch app 2.0, package 1 of pebble-ideen/plan.md): three sub-switches under *Features → Pebble watch*, all off; released, they apply to every profile, never to guests.

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: - *Home and on the road*: when pairing, *Me → Pebble watch* has the field "Address on the road" (only https://name[:port], e.g. the reverse proxy). The pairing line carries it as &aussen=…. When the home address does not answer within 4 seconds, the phone takes the second one and keeps it for 5 minutes; the watch then shows "unterwegs". Without https nothing goes over the internet. - *Watch: follow-ups to tap*: at the end of an answer DOWN opens up to 3 short follow-up questions; tapping one asks it as if spoken. The model only suggests text (task "Uhr-Nachfragen", at most 6 seconds); the panel keeps only short questions without yes/no, links, long numbers or deleting, buying, sending. After an answer from mail, web or outside text, after a proposal, an error or Notaus there are none. When the Spark proposes something ("Soll ich …?"), the watch shows ✓ and ✕; ✓ sends "Ja", ✕ "Nein" as a normal answer, decided in the panel as always. - *Watch: quick commands*: up to 12 own sentences per profile (at most 60 characters each) under *Me → Pebble watch*. Long UP on the watch shows the list, SELECT sends one as a question. - *Watch: reminders and timers on the wrist* (needs *Timers and re

head: Pebble watch
title: Pebble watch
text: minders* too): the next 8 reminders of the next 30 days sit on the watch as wake-ups and ring without the phone (yellow window, three vibrations). UP closes, SELECT "later" (10 minutes), DOWN ends a series. A timer shows a ring; UP adds a minute, long DOWN stops it. Long DOWN shows the list. The watch reports what it rang (POST /api/watch/reminder), so a reminder rings only once for the profile; push waits 90 seconds for the watch when the watch holds it. My day: today's appointments, reminders, weather, unread messages. My week: questions and new notes of the last 7 days, appointments and reminders of the next 7 days. Fixed sentences from the own data, never the language model, never mail or message text; each part only when its function is on for the profile. - *Watch: notes for admins* (needs the service watch): when a service does not answer, the watchface of the admins who get the notes shows a red bar with the same fixed sentence as the banner and vibrates once. - *Watch: quick notes* (needs memory): "Merken" in the list, say a sentence; it goes through POST /ap

DOWN at the end: "Okay", "Bin unterwegs", "Melde mich gleich", "Danke!" or "Diktieren …"; sending goes through POST /api/watch/chat, which checks every chat rule again. Private chats do not show: they only take messages sealed on the device. - *Watch: reply suggestions*: when the last message came from somebody else, the language model suggests up to 3 short replies (task "Uhr-Antworten", at most 6 seconds). The messages go as content between <<< >>>, never as an instruction; the panel keeps only sentences up to 40 characters without links, numbers, money, codes or PIN. Only what you tap is sent. - *Watch: remote*: under *Me → Pebble watch* tick up to 12 devices of your own Home Assistant; "Fernbedienung" in the list shows them with fixed buttons (TV and music: on, off, play/pause, next, louder, quieter; blinds: up, down; lights and switches: toggle, on, off), plus the own speakers (louder, quieter). POST /api/watch/fern switches only devices on the own list that Home Assistant still r

title: Terminal client (spark-tui)
text: spark-tui (app/tui/spark-tui.py, one Python file) brings the chat with your history, *Today* and your jobs, plans and routines into a terminal, e.g. on the ClockworkPi uConsole or over SSH (new in V01.0.646, off).

head: Terminal client (spark-tui)
title: Terminal client (spark-tui)
text: 1. The admin switches on *Functions → Terminal client* (applies to every profile, the admin blocks single ones; never guests). 2. *Me → Terminal* shows a line that fetches the program, checks the checksum (sha256sum -c with the value from the page) and sets it up as the command ~/.local/bin/spark-tui (from V01.0.661; Raspberry Pi OS has ~/.local/bin in the path after the next login). The window needs Textual in its own environment (python3 -m venv ~/.local/share/spark-tui && ~/.local/share/spark-tui/bin/pip install textual, Raspberry Pi OS and Debian refuse pip outside an environment; spark-tui finds it by itself), spark-tui frage "…" works without it. 3. "Get a pairing line" (with confirmation code) gives a line ~/.local/bin/spark-tui koppeln 'https://…#tui=…&fp=…', valid for 10 minutes and once. In the home network the terminal pins the panel's certificate (fp, SHA-256) and sends nothing if it does not match. If you fetch the line over the outside address (reverse proxy with a real certificate), it has no fp and the certificate is checked as in the browser. spark-tui adresse-dazu https://… adds a second address; the terminal uses the first one that answers. Only https works. 4. T

title: Terminal client (spark-tui)
text: he terminal keeps its key in ~/.config/spark-tui/geraet.json (readable only by you). The key is called "Terminal · name", reaches only chat, conversations, Today, the function list and the job pages, and gets 503 while the function is off or the profile is blocked. Jobs follow the profile's agent level. Remove it under *Me → Terminal* or under People and devices.

head: Terminal client (spark-tui)
title: Terminal client (spark-tui)
text: Window: conversations, jobs and Today on the left (below 100 columns only the chat), the chat on the right. F2 conversations, F3 jobs (n new job; in a job d as document, x cancel, Del delete), F4 reload, F5 calendar (the week as text, ← → pages, t today; since V01.0.807), Ctrl+N new conversation, Esc stops the answer, F10 quit. spark-tui kalender (or --woche 1 for next week) prints the week's appointments like the page Calendar, read only. spark-tui status shows address, profile and what the terminal may do. When the Spark has a newer version, the window's head line says "Neue Version …: spark-tui update"; spark-tui update fetches it over the paired connection and replaces the program only when the checksum matches the one the Spark names (from V01.0.665). Questions show up in the request history with input "Terminal", *Status → Live* shows the number of open terminals, *Status → Logs* has the terminal: … lines in the area "Apps". The question goes into a three-line field that grows up to six lines (since V01.0.829): Enter sends, Ctrl+J (or Shift+Enter where the terminal tells them apart) makes a new line; the same for a new job.

head: Terminal client (spark-tui)
title: Terminal client (spark-tui)
text: Calendar and e-mail without the window (V01.0.830, Dominik 2026-10-19 "a"): spark-tui neu 'Morgen 15 Uhr Zahnarzt' shows what the Spark reads from the line (title, day, time, place; fixed rules like "Quick add" on the Calendar page), asks "Eintragen? [j/N]" and only then saves into your first own calendar (--ja without asking). spark-tui mails lists the newest mails by day (number, * unread, time, sender, subject), spark-tui mail 3 shows the third as plain text; it stays unread. Changing, ordering and sending stay in the panel and the app. Text from calendars and mail is shown with printable characters only, never control characters.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
title: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
text: The "Spark" app is the iPhone front end for a voice assistant you run yourself on your own computer ("your Spark"). The app only works together with your Spark.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: In short
title: In short
text: - The app talks only to your own Spark. There is no developer server. - The developer receives no data: no usage statistics, no ads, no tracking, no crash reports through own services. - Whoever runs the Spark is responsible for the data stored on it.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: What goes where
title: What goes where
text: The connection to your Spark is encrypted (https). The pairing key is kept in the iPhone's keychain.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: What stays on the iPhone
title: What stays on the iPhone
text: - Wake word: "Hey Spark" is recognised on the iPhone only; nothing goes to Apple or your Spark until you speak. - Camera and photos: the iPhone reads the text itself. Images never leave the iPhone. - Contacts: only to find the number for "Call …". Contacts are not sent to your Spark. - Reminders: after your "yes" the app writes entries into the Reminders app. It reads nothing there for your Spark. - Questions while offline: at most 10 typed questions wait on the iPhone for up to one day.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Notifications through Apple
title: Notifications through Apple
text: If you turn notifications on, your Spark sends only the fixed sentence "Neue Nachricht vom Spark" and a random number through Apple's push service. The iPhone then fetches the actual text directly from your Spark. Apple does not see the content.

file: Privacy policy of the iPhone app "Spark"
head: Deleting
title: Deleting
text: "Unpair" in the app deletes the pairing key, waiting questions and the reminder mapping on the iPhone. Data on your Spark is deleted in your Spark's panel. Deleting the app removes all of its data from the iPhone.

head: Architecture and data flow
title: Architecture and data flow
text: This page describes how the Spark is built: which parts exist, which way a request takes and where which data lies. The panel shows the same to click through under Status → Architecture (admins only). There the picture uses the whole width with the detail below it; "⛶ Full screen" lays the overview or the data flow over the whole screen, with ＋/− to zoom and Escape to close. How to build is set by the coding guideline.

head: Architecture and data flow
title: Architecture and data flow
text: The sections between the markers <!-- technik:… --> are generated from the code (app/panel/technik.py, plus speicher.AREAS/LOCAL and backup.STATE_FILES/STATE_LOCAL). python3 app/panel/hilfe.py --docs writes them again. A self-test (test_technik) turns red when a module, a file or a step is missing or the docs were not written again. Only the text outside the markers is kept by hand.

head: Overview
title: Overview
text: Devices and programs only talk to the panel. The panel checks every request, asks the language model, calls tools through the guard and writes into the folders under /var/lib/speech-spark. Speech recognition, speech output, pictures and the language model are services of their own.

head: Overview
title: Overview
text: The picture is split into zones so you can see where a part lives: at the top the devices, which can be at home or on the way (small marks „home“ and „on the way“; they come in directly at :31080/:31443 or through the reverse proxy), in the middle the DGX Spark with panel, models and storage, at the bottom what goes out, split into home network and internet and only through the guard or fixed ways. With the Spark split the panel zone runs with the storage on its own computer, the models stay on the DGX and are reached through the TLS-Tor (box „Spark split“). In the panel the lines stay pale until you click a box; then only its ways light up. Places, zones and lines are in technik.py (ZONEN, LINIEN); test_technik checks that no box covers another, every box lies in its zone and every line runs at right angles from box to box.

head: Processes and ports
title: Model computer (V01.0.606, plan "Splitting the Spark" stage B1)
text: Model computer (V01.0.606, plan "Splitting the Spark" stage B1): the panel reaches speech recognition, speech output, pictures and the LLM-Tor through one address only: common.model_url(art, path) with the setting models.host. The default is 127.0.0.1, and then everything runs on one Spark over http://127.0.0.1:<port> as before. With another computer there (a name or IP, never a path or http://), every request goes over https and the API key is a must (admin.validate); a broken entry stays on the Spark. The LLM-Tor on the model computer gets the key like the own one (llm.own_tor), and the guard (netguard.model_addresses) treats the model computer's ports 30000–31099 like its own: no MCP, calendar or Home Assistant address can point at them. The model computer is set only by the split install (stage B6); the pairing pins the certificate (B3). Self-test test_modell_rechner.

head: Processes and ports
title: TLS-Tor (V01.0.607, stage B2)
text: TLS-Tor (V01.0.607, stage B2): when the panel runs on another computer, the services on the DGX listen only on 127.0.0.1, and app/tlstor.py opens the same ports on api.tls_listen with TLS 1.3 and the certificate in /etc/speech-spark/tls, only for the addresses in api.tls_from. The panel trusts exactly the pinned certificate (models.cert); common._pin_models gives it to every httpx connection to the model computer that brings no transport of its own. Self-test test_teilen.

head: Processes and ports
title: Wärter (V01.0.609, stage B4a)
text: Wärter (V01.0.609, stage B4a): on the model computer app/tarswart.py (127.0.0.1:31007, behind the TLS-Tor) runs a fixed list of commands: status and einheit start|stop|restart <part>. The panel talks to it through steuer.py (unit_state, active_seconds, systemctl, gpu); on the all-in-one install steuer.py calls systemctl and nvidia-smi itself as before. Signed with HMAC-SHA256 and the Wärter key from the pairing. Self-test test_waerter. Since V01.0.610 also einstellen (speech settings from the panel, common.model_settings) and logs <part> <n>. Since V01.0.612 the status reports the model choice (common.MODEL_CHOICE), which the panel takes over; plus modelle, wechseln <kind> <id|zurueck>, eigen_dazu and eigen_weg for Status → Models (modelle.wechsel_anfragen is the one source for both ways). The qwen38 lanes (common.qwen38_lanes) now live in common. The status also reports the model computer's Wartungspause (common.WARTUNG_FILE, parts and times only) and per unit when it started (eintritt, for the automatic); weiter ends it. wartung.state merges it with the own pause (steuer.cached, never a request on the question path); Live box "Model computer" from steuer.for_live. Since V01.0.614

head: Processes and ports
title: Wärter (V01.0.609, stage B4a)
text: update starts the model computer's own update; the status carries commit and update, the panel computer's update.sh waits for it through speech-spark teilen modelle-update. PREFIX and installed_version now live in common. Emergency mode: steuer.weg (30 s without an answer) makes wartung.paused true for every part, wartung.quiet not; own sentence wartung.NOTBETRIEB and speaker files notbetrieb-satz-*.pcm. Pairing (V01.0.616, B6a): teilen.py warten|koppeln on port 31008 only while a code is shown; key scrypt(code, SHA-256 of the certificate), proof and answer with HMAC-SHA256; speech-spark teilen code|koppeln writes the result with cfg_put (the one place that changes the config in the shell) and STATE/waerter.key. Install (V01.0.617, B6b): install.sh --mode api --teilen (marker $ETC/teilen, services on 127.0.0.1, door certificate common.TOR_CERT, units speech-spark-tlstor, -waerter, -teilen-fw, both in restart-map) and --mode panel --modelle (PANEL_ONLY: no model, no engine, pairing before the units); steuer.rundlauf checks the way afterwards. Moving (V01.0.618, B6c): panel/umziehen.py packen|auspacken (move backup through stdin/stdout, system._check_config), teilen.warten(umzug=…)/

head: Processes and ports
title: Wärter (V01.0.609, stage B4a)
text: koppeln(umzug_ordner, einspielen) with a signed "fertig"; speech-spark umziehen --code|--von, zurueckholen --von; only speech-spark teilen zertifikat makes the door's certificate. Emergency mode with Parakeet (V01.0.620, B5c): panel/notbetrieb.py with chat.notbetrieb_asr; in emergency mode common.model_url("asr") goes to speech-spark-notasr (asr_proxy.py with SPEECH_SPARK_NOTASR=1, 127.0.0.1:common.NOTASR_PORT, loads when needed, unloads after common.NOTASR_IDLE); before the fixed sentence chat.py asks notbetrieb.antwort (Home Assistant through chat._ha_panel, the time, reminder_list); esp32.pause_clip(en, text) plays files from STATE/notbetrieb-saetze/ for it (notbetrieb.ton, made by notbetrieb.make_clips in wartung.clips_tick).

head: Processes and ports
title: Processes and ports
text: All services run as the system user speech and log into the journald namespace speech-spark. The panel starts its background jobs itself (panel.py: samples, stability, inbox tidy, reading documents, reMarkable sync, learning from conversations). Background work waits while someone speaks (vorrang.py).

head: Data flow of a request
title: Data flow of a request
text: The way of a spoken question in the browser, from input to storage:

head: Data flow of a request
title: Data flow of a request
text: - Telegram, Siri and the watch send text (or a voice message) to their own endpoint. The panel stores the history itself (verlauf.keep), not the device. - ESP32 speakers and Home Assistant Assist talk to esp32.py and wyoming.py. A stranger's voice at a shared speaker gets guest rights only. - MCP programs ask through /mcp (mcpserver.py) with their own token, stored only as a hash. - Guests get only question and answer from the language model, without tools, personal data or history on the Spark.

head: Data flow of a request
title: Data flow of a request
text: Everywhere: everything from outside (web, mail, documents, tool results, model output) is data, never a command. The panel decides by fixed rules.

head: Building blocks
title: Building blocks
text: Every module under app/panel/ and app/ belongs to exactly one group. A new module without an entry in technik.MODULE turns test_technik red. The English lines are the first sentence of each module's docstring.

head: Building blocks
title: Building blocks
text: Every request passes here first: size, origin, kill switch, login, profile and releases.

head: Conversation
title: Conversation
text: Prepares a request, asks the language model in rounds and checks what is said.

head: Switch and tool names
title: Switch and tool names
text: Fixed rules for which tools the model sees for a question. Never gives more than the rights.

head: Knowledge and documents
title: Knowledge and documents
text: Own documents, memory, earlier conversations, Kiwix and Wikipedia, created documents.

head: Connections
title: Connections
text: Home Assistant, tasks, For you, weather, reMarkable, MCP and what the Spark does by itself.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: The own pages E-mail, Calendar and Contacts, fetching from the provider, the sealed supply and the doors for calendar and contacts apps.

head: Devices and channels
title: Devices and channels
text: Apps, Telegram, watch, speakers, room mode, chats and the history on all devices.

title: Operation
text: Live overview, logs, watchers, backup, update, help and the admin pages.

head: Speech services
title: Speech services
text: Speech recognition and speech output as their own services, ahead of everything else.

title: Spark split
text: Panel on its own computer, models on the DGX: pairing, TLS-Tor, Wärter and the move.

head: Data storage
title: Data storage
text: All files belong to the user speech (folders 0700, files 0600) and are written atomically (.tmp, then renamed). "Backup" means the file is in the backup under Settings → Backup. "Own storage" means a profile can copy the file encrypted to its own storage.

head: Keys and encryption
title: Keys and encryption
text: - state/secret.key seals every password and token (Fernet, vault.py). The chats' key is derived from it too (HKDF, AES-256-GCM). It goes only into a move backup, sealed with the admin's password (state/move-keys.json, scrypt). A normal backup restored on another Spark therefore loses chats and every sealed account. - users/secret and state/admin-session.key sign logins and never go into a backup. After a move everyone signs in again. - The voiceprint users/ID/voice.json is sealed like a password (speakers.py), in the backup too. An older open file is sealed the first time it is read. After a backup restored on another Spark the profile records its voice anew. - The offsite backup (offsite.py) and the own storage (speicher.py) are encrypted as a whole (scrypt + AES-GCM, AES-256-GCM in chunks of 1 MiB).

head: Caches in memory
title: Caches in memory
text: These caches are lost on a restart and hold nothing that cannot be fetched again: calendar 300 s, mail 120 s, bus and train 60 s, weather 900 s, parcels 600 s, Wikipedia and Kiwix 24 h, picture questions 600 s (results also in state/vision.json), answers for the watch 600 s, the document search vectors per profile, the voices of speech output.

head: Logs
title: Logs
text: All services write into the journald namespace speech-spark (persistent, at most logs.max_mb = 500 MB, logs.keep_days = 14 days). Lines hold only fixed words and numbers, a profile only through profiles.log_name. The request trace (state/traces.jsonl, 48 h) runs only while the admin switch logs.trace is on.

head: The boxes in detail
title: The boxes in detail
text: Every box of the picture has its own page (Status → Architecture, click a box, then „In detail“): what it does and why, its way as a picture with numbered steps, rules, numbers, where to set it and see it, and its code. The texts live in app/panel/technik_knoten.py; numbers and lists of callers are read from the code. A click on a bubble frames its text and makes both blink briefly (on a phone it opens as a card under the bubble), with a mouse pointing is enough. A click on the text, a rule, a number or a code line marks the bubble the other way round; if it is out of sight, it shows up small under the clicked line, with „Show in the way“, and the page stays put. While an example plays, the list beside follows. In this file, „(step N)“ links lead to the step. In the data flow, a clicked box picks its step of the request's way.

head: The boxes in detail
title: The boxes in detail
text: The page in the browser (static/js/chat.js) is the device: it records the question, sends the sound to speech recognition, sends the text to /api/chat and plays text and sound from one single stream. A profile's conversations live on the Spark, every open page keeps them in step.

head: The boxes in detail
title: Why
text: Why: All the computing happens on the Spark; the page stays thin. Browser, phone browser and the Android app (a WebView) take the same way, so login, limits and rules apply in exactly one place, and a conversation looks the same on every device. The page stays calm: saving never reloads it, when it must reload (new version, update finished) it comes back to the same place, and during an update one window alone shows the progress.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. „Speak“ tapped: startListening gets the microphone and remembers how it opened: by hand, after an answer (follow-up), hands-free or by talking over the answer. A microphone the page opened by itself later only takes a known voice. 2. Secure connection?: Browsers only hand out the microphone on a secure page. Without https the page shows a note with the panel's https address and records nothing. 3. Record, find the end of the sentence: MediaRecorder records, a level meter listens for silence. About every second the recording so far goes to speech recognition and shows as a pale bubble. If the sentence ends with a full stop, question or exclamation mark, the question is done at once; if it ends on „and“, „because“, „uhm“ or a comma, the page waits a little longer. 4. Sound to /api/test/asr: The page turns the recording into a plain mono WAV (else the original goes). The Spark checks the rate limit (240 per minute for a profile, guests at most 3 at once), reads at most 50 MB and sends the sound to speech recognition, for the Dungeon Master in the car with the round's names first. Alongside it measures on the CPU how much of it is voice and whose voice it is. 5. Silence, own or fore

head: Way
title: Way
text: ign voice?: Fixed rules, no model: a „yes“ out of silence or a click (stille.check), the Spark's own voice from another device (echo.check) and, with a microphone the page opened itself, a foreign voice like the TV (fremdstimme.check) are no question. The answer is then empty text with the reason. When the page or the iPhone app only paused the answer for a barge-in (hold), zwischenruf.decide adds with fixed words: on (nothing, ignored, „mhm“), stop („stop“) or question (anything else); without a decision after 4 s it plays on. 6. Question to /api/chat: The page sends the last messages of the open conversation, its id, voice, speed and, when the voice was recognized, a signed one-time token. The Spark checks the rate limit (120 per minute for a profile, guests at most 4 at once), lets background work wait (vorrang) and tells the profile's other open pages „answering“ (only the kind of device). 7. Text and sound in one stream: The answer comes as events: pieces of text, pieces of sound, search, sources, questions back, errors. The text is redrawn at most once per frame. The sound plays in its own audio context at the speech output's rate; every piece ends with a short fade so the se

head: Way
title: Way
text: ams do not click. 8. Someone talking over it?: While the answer plays, the microphone keeps listening. If the level stays clearly above the own output and the room (TV) for a moment, the answer stops and the recording already running becomes the next question. 9. Error in the stream?: An error shows under the answer in plain words; the admin also sees the technical detail, guests only the kind of error. If only speech output failed, the answer stays as text. 10. Store the conversation: For a profile the page sends only the new messages (PUT /api/profile/convos with „add“). The Spark appends them to its copy under a lock, so another device overwrites nothing, and keeps at most 50 conversations of 60 messages each. 11. Sync with other devices: When the page comes to the front again, and regularly in between, it asks what changed since last time; a conversation deleted elsewhere closes. With instant sync every visible page keeps an event stream open that only reports „conversation changed“ and „answering“, never contents (at most 8 per profile, 30 minutes each); a hidden page closes it to save the battery and asks again on coming back. 12. Ready: The page waits until the answer is spo

head: Apps
title: Apps
text: The iPhone app gets its own device key of the profile when it is paired and uses the same endpoints as the browser with it. The key only opens a fixed list of paths. The Android app has no key of its own: it shows the panel in a WebView and signs in like a browser.

head: Apps
title: Why
text: Why: A phone gets lost or passed on. That is why an app key can only ask and listen, never change the account, devices or security, and it stops working at once when the device is removed in the panel or the app is switched off.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Ask for pairing: Only the profile's own browser login may pair, never a device key. If the profile has a second sign-in step it needs a code for this, because a new way into the profile is made. 2. App allowed and room left?: The app must be switched on by the admin and not blocked for the profile, and the profile may have at most 5 iPhones. The panel address must start with https and have no path. 3. One-time link as QR code: kopplung.py makes a random code (144 bits); only its hash is kept in memory. A profile has at most 3 open codes, the Spark at most 20. The link spark-app://pair opens the app with address and code. 4. Code valid?: The app sends the code. The Spark checks the rate limit (10 per minute and address), compares the hash in constant time and deletes the code at the first hit. An expired or used code never fits. If it is no link code, pruefzugang.py checks a typed review code for Apple's review (12 signs, 14 days, at most 5 iPhones, only with the review access on); wrong review codes lock the address like wrong PINs. 5. Own device key: profiles.add_device makes the key and stores only its SHA-256 hash in profiles.json. The app gets it exactly once and keeps it in

head: Way
title: Way
text: the keychain. 6. Every request with the key: profiles.current looks up the key's hash in the device list. A device key comes before the cookie; the profile always comes from the key, never from what the app writes. 7. Path allowed for the app?: An app key only works for the 70 paths in profiles.APP_PATHS (chat, speech recognition, conversations, reminders, chats, calls …), a few read patterns, the panel areas (admin switch iPhone app with panel) and "My things" (iphone.THINGS, each part only with the release of its own function). Everything else it sees without a profile. 8. App off right now or My kill switch?: If the app is switched off by the admin or blocked for the profile, or the profile has My kill switch on, this request has no profile. The app gets „not now“ (503), keeps its pairing and works again as soon as the switch is back. 9. Like a browser of the profile: The app asks through the same endpoints as the page, with the same limits. What it may do on top (smart home, CarPlay, listening, documents, pictures) the Spark tells it in /api/iphone/hello; the app only shows it and follows it. Calls between profiles ring through a VoIP push from Apple that carries only the call

head: Way
title: Way
text: 's random number; the app asks the Spark who calls. For private chats the app makes its own key in the Secure Enclave; the Spark only gets the public half. The Android app's sheet over other apps asks as device „android“ only while „Android: Spark as assistant“ is released (android.assist_gate). Whether the app may keep the pages' last state, hello says with „keep“ (appmerken.keep); on no it deletes it. With „barge_hold“ it only pauses the answer for a barge-in (zwischenruf.py). With „Notes to the device in use“ the app and the pages only say every minute whether they are in use right now (POST /api/zustellung/da, the companion with its idle time); zustellung.pick then sends a note to the device with the last input within the last 120 seconds, else to the phone app at once. If nobody saw it, zustellung.follow sends it once to the phone after 5 minutes; a tapped note says „seen“, and with the answer „zu“ pages and the iPhone take done ones away. Every note stays on the Spark for 24 hours with a random number (mitteilungen.keep, in memory only); only the number goes along. Tapped, it shows as a card above the conversation, with the one button mitteilungen.ziel picks by fixed rules (O

head: Way
title: Way
text: pen, chat, mail, code, way); only the own profile gets it back. 10. Account, devices or security?: Endpoints that change the profile's connections, devices or security only take the own browser login (core.browser_profile). They refuse a device key, except in an area the profile opened for the app; secrets need a fresh code there as well. 11. Removing works at once: When the iPhone is removed in the panel, its hash leaves the device list. The app's next request finds no profile any more.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Pair an iPhone and ask: The app has its key and asks like the browser. · Old QR code: Refused: the code was used or has expired. · App wants to change the PIN: Refused: that only works in the own browser. · Admin switches the app off: Not now: the pairing stays for later.

head: Telegram, Siri, watch
title: Telegram, Siri, watch
text: Telegram, the Siri shortcut and the Pebble watch ask short questions without a browser. Each channel turns them into a request to /api/chat like a device, collects the answer from the stream and hands it back in its own form. The panel itself keeps the history in the profile.

head: Telegram, Siri, watch
title: Why
text: Why: The channels should decide nothing of their own: the same rights, locks and limits as in the browser apply, because everything runs through the same chat. What a channel brings on top (forwarded texts of others, Telegram's servers) is settled by fixed rules first.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Question through a channel: Telegram: the panel asks Telegram for new messages itself (long polling), no open port is needed. Siri: a shortcut sends the dictated text with a device key to /api/siri/ask. Watch: the phone sends the question with the watch key to /api/watch/ask. 2. Telegram: chat linked?: Groups and channels are never answered. A chat belongs to a profile once it sent „/start CODE“ with a code from Me → Telegram (valid 10 minutes, at most 5 wrong codes per chat and hour). A stranger's chat gets one fixed sentence at most once a day. 3. Blocked or My kill switch?: The profile's My kill switch, a block by the admin or a channel switched off end the question. Telegram then answers with a fixed sentence; Siri and the watch find no profile for their key. 4. Forwarded?: A message forwarded in Telegram comes from someone else. It is never taken as an order and does not trigger commands like /notaus either. 5. Voice message to text: A Telegram voice message is loaded with a size limit, turned into WAV by ffmpeg (length capped) and read by the Spark's speech recognition. With Siri the iPhone dictates, with the watch the phone. 6. Short history: For follow-ups the last eight

head: Way
title: Way
text: messages go along while the last question is no older than 30 minutes (Telegram) or 10 minutes (Siri). The watch sends its history itself; the panel recognizes answers made from outside text in it again (watch.mark_of). 7. Request to /api/chat: The channel calls the chat inside the panel. For Telegram the panel puts the profile into the request, which no request from outside can do; Siri and the watch carry their key. Rights, switch, limits and request history are the same as in the browser. 8. Collect the answer: From the stream, pieces of text and retractions count. If the answer came from mail or outside text it is marked so, so the next question starts locked. A question back from the panel becomes buttons in Telegram that come back like a typed answer; without one, the example sentences of „You can also say“ become reply buttons. 9. Output per channel: Telegram gets plain text and, if the profile wants it, a voice message in its voice. Siri gets speakable text without passwords and codes. The watch fetches text and sound (packed for its small speaker, 6000 bytes per fetch) through /api/watch/poll, only for the profile that asked (a foreign job number gives 404); at most 8 wat

head: Way
title: Way
text: ch answers run at once. The companion gets text without Markdown and also the answer with Markdown (at most 60000 characters) when it hides no fewer secrets. With its switches the watch also gets up to 3 follow-ups to tap (the model only suggests, watch.follow_clean keeps short questions without yes, no, links or numbers; never after mail, web or a proposal; when the answer ends with a question, its buttons from ablauf.asks are the follow-ups), a proposal as ✓ and ✕, and through /api/watch/sync the quick commands and the next 8 reminders, which it rings itself as wake-ups; push waits for it first. The Spark watchface fetches the next appointment, reminder, weather, a hint and for admins an outage through /api/watch/blick every 15 minutes; /api/watch/brief builds My day and My week from fixed sentences, /api/watch/merken keeps a dictated sentence in memory (with the place to about 100 m only with its own switch). /api/watch/chats and /api/watch/chat show the latest chats (no private ones) and send a tapped or dictated reply through chats.send; up to 3 suggestions of the model pass the fixed check pebblewatch.reply_clean. /api/watch/fern switches only devices on the own list with fix

head: Way
title: Way
text: ed buttons (never with a smart home code word), /api/watch/gesundheit keeps steps, pulse and sleep sealed in the profile, never for the model. 10. Black out the code word: Before storing, the smart home code word is replaced by [Codewort]. In Telegram the bot deletes the message with the code word or asks the person to delete it. 11. In the profile's history: verlauf.keep puts question and answer into the channel's conversation of the day („Telegram“, „Siri“, „Uhr“ with the date). With „One conversation for all channels“ they go into the day's main conversation, marked with their channel.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: Telegram voice message: Answered and kept in the day's „Telegram“ conversation. · A stranger writes to the bot: One fixed sentence, nothing else. · Forwarded mail with an order: Not carried out: someone else's words are no order. · Siri with My kill switch: No answer: the key finds no profile.

head: Speakers, phone
title: Speakers, phone
text: Own speakers are ESP32 boards with the open XiaoZhi firmware. They listen for their wake word, send the sound to the Spark over a WebSocket connection and play the answer. Every speaker is a device key of its profile. Home Assistant Assist only uses the Spark's speech recognition and voice over Wyoming.

head: Speakers, phone
title: Why
text: Why: A speaker stands in the room, anyone can talk to it. That is why personal things only go to the voice that is surely recognized as the profile's (or says the code word), and a board gets its key only once and only at the address that showed the code.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. Board starts: At every start the board asks with its id, MAC address and firmware version which server and which firmware to use. If speakers are off in Features, it gets nothing (403). 2. Board known?: An unknown board gets a six-digit code for its display (valid 10 minutes, at most 3 per address and 30 in all). The profile types it in under Me → Speakers. 3. Same board?: Once a MAC address is on record for a board id, it must fit. A copied id from another board gets no key and no firmware. 4. Answer of the start check: The board gets the time and the WebSocket address. The key comes exactly once, right after the code was typed in, and only to the address that showed the code. A newer firmware is only offered over https, over http only with the admin's switch. 5. Connection allowed?: When connecting the Spark checks: kill switch stage 3 off, the key belongs to a speaker (not a watch or another device), speakers on in Features and not blocked for the profile. Then it looks again every 2.0 seconds and ends the connection when something changed. 6. Listen: After the wake word the board sends Opus sound. The Spark finds the end of the sentence itself (0.7 seconds of silence after s

head: Way
title: Way
text: peech) and takes at most 30 seconds per question. 7. Recognize and check the voice: Speech recognition makes text of it. At the same time speakers.verify checks whether it is the profile's voice, when speaker ID is on and the profile has taught its voice. 8. Nothing, stop or own voice?: No text, a stop word or the Spark's own voice from another device (echo.check) get no answer. The board waits for its wake word again. 9. Personal without a sure voice?: With the speaker code word: an unsure voice asking for personal things is asked for the code word, the question waits. After 3 wrong tries the speaker does not ask for 30 minutes. Without a sure voice there are only general things. A sure voice in a short question asking nothing personal gets the owner's rights as without the code word. 10. Like a device to /api/chat: The Spark calls the chat with the speaker's key; the profile's voice, memory and room apply. Whose voice it was only the panel itself puts into the request; if it was not surely the profile's, the question counts like a guest's. 11. Sound back: The answer goes to the board as Opus at 24000 Hz at playback pace, the text without Markdown for a display. Other devices in t

head: Way
title: Way
text: he house know the Spark is speaking right now (echo.said). 12. In the speaker's history: Question and answer go into the speaker's conversation of the day, the code word blacked out. A voice that was not surely the profile's is marked as outside text: the next question starts locked, and nothing about the profile is learned from it.

head: Way
title: Examples
text: Examples: The owner asks for appointments: Voice recognized: personal answer, kept in the day's conversation. · New board: Code on the display until the profile types it in. · Copied board id: Refused: the MAC address does not fit. · A guest asks for mail: Code word asked; without the right one nothing personal. · Maintenance pause of the speech output: Answer on the display, the short maintenance sentence from a file to hear (else a tone); with the speech recognition paused the speaker says the sentence right after the wake word. · Emergency mode with Parakeet: Model computer gone: Parakeet on the panel computer hears, a fixed command (“lights on”, “what time is it?”) runs without a model; to hear are sentences and building blocks made before (notbetrieb.ton).

head: Home Assistant Assist (Wyoming)
title: Home Assistant Assist (Wyoming)
text: - Its own server listens on the Wyoming port (default 31003) while the switch is on. Wyoming has no password; that is why it only answers addresses from the admin's list, with an empty list nobody. - Home Assistant only gets „sound in, text out“ and „text in, sound out“, no language model, no profile, nothing personal. At most 8 connections at once; lengths are checked before reading; only sound formats a microphone sends. „describe“ answers at once with the voice list from memory (read again every 10 minutes), because Home Assistant waits only 1 second. - Refused addresses show on Status → Live under input and as a suggestion for the list.

head: Calling the Spark (phone)
title: Calling the Spark (phone)
text: - The Spark signs in at the telephone system in the home network as an IP phone (SIP over UDP, port 31060, digest sign-in, renewed every 10 minutes). It takes messages only from the system's address, at most 4096 bytes and 100 per second; sound (RTP) only from the address in its SDP, which has to be in the home network. The sound out goes from a thread of its own at a 20 ms beat, independent of the panel's event loop; speech starts only once 10 packets are ready or the sentence is complete, after every gap it waits for more (at most 40). The log line at the end names gaps, late packets and the time spent encoding per second of sound. - A call runs like a question at a speaker: end of sentence with the same level check, speech recognition, voice check, chat with the profile (set only by the panel), answer back in G.722 or G.711. A profile's handset gets personal things only with a sure voice; at the shared phone the voice picks the profile. After 20 seconds of silence „Noch etwas?“, after another 10 it hangs up; at most 15 minutes. A goodbye („Tschüss“, „Danke, das war's“, „Ich lege auf“, also in the middle of an answer) and right after „Noch etwas?“ a „Nein danke“ end the call: „Ts

head: Calling the Spark (phone)
title: Calling the Spark (phone)
text: chüss!“, then the Spark hangs up itself (fixed word lists BYE_WORDS and NO_MORE, never the model). When the phone hangs up, its BYE ends the call at once; if none arrives (router, line), the Spark hangs up after 8 seconds without any sound packet, unless the phone put the call on hold. - From outside: an own number waiting for its code under Me → Phone types it (4 digits, 15 minutes, 3 tries), then it hangs up. With „Anrufe von außen“ a confirmed number picks its profile, but personal things only with a sure voice or the PIN, because numbers can be forged; with guests also unknown numbers as a guest, at most 20 a day. Logs and Live never name a number from outside. - The phone PIN (digits, then #) stands for the voice for the rest of the call: on a handset for its profile, at the shared phone for the profile it belongs to. 3 wrong ones in 15 minutes lock it at that phone for 30 minutes. Stored as a salted hash in the vault; never spoken, shown or logged. - The Spark calls (switch „Der Spark ruft an“): wake-up call and reminder a profile orders itself (tool anruf_planen, only time, kind and text, never a number), the call back and the alarm. It only calls the assigned handset or, wi

head: Calling the Spark (phone)
title: Calling the Spark (phone)
text: th „also confirmed own numbers“, the profile's confirmed number; at most 5 calls per profile and day, never during „Nicht stören“; not answered once more after 5 minutes, then a note. It reads a reminder only once voice or PIN fit. Call back: whoever calls from outside with an unsure voice and says „Ruf mich zurück“ is called at the stored confirmed number, so a forged number never reaches the forger. - Alarm on outages: if a service is gone 10 minutes or longer, the Spark calls the admin, at most once in 60 minutes. Never between 10 pm and 7 am (dienstwacht.NIGHT, always for calls), in the admin's quiet hours or during „Nicht stören“; if the service is still gone afterwards, the call comes then.

head: MCP programs
title: MCP programs
text: Other programs (Claude, n8n, Open WebUI, Home Assistant) use the Spark over the Model Context Protocol at /mcp. Every connection belongs to one profile and has its own key and its own tool list. Reading works directly, acting only as a proposal the profile confirms.

head: MCP programs
title: Why
text: Why: What a program sends is outside text and never a command. That is why the panel decides with fixed lists which tool may run, and nothing changes without the person's yes in the own browser.

head: Way
title: Way
text: 1. A program sends a request: Every request is one JSON-RPC message. If the MCP server is off by the admin, the endpoint does not exist (404). 2. From another web page?: If a browser sends an Origin, it must be the panel's. So no other page can use the endpoint through DNS rebinding. 3. Key valid?: The bearer key is a fixed key or an OAuth access token (valid 60 minutes). Only hashes are stored. A connection ends after 90 days without use. 4. Home network key from outside?: A „lokal“ key only works when the peer is a private address, no proxy header is in the request and it is none of the listed reverse proxies. „extern“ only works with the admin's switch. 5. My kill switch or profile blocked?: The profile's My kill switch closes every MCP access (503); if the admin blocked the MCP server for the profile, there is nothing (403). 6. Rate limit and size: Every connection may send 60 requests per minute; a request is at most 16 MB. Many refused requests from outside count for „Emergency stop by itself“. 7. Tool allowed?: Only tools from the fixed list (15), only those given to this connection, and only when the profile may use the function right now, checked again on every call. Mail,

head: Way
title: Way
text: memory, earlier conversations, settings and code are never among them (31 names in mcpserver.NEVER). 8. Too many at once?: At most 2 calls of one connection and 6 of all connections run at once. 9. Speech and reading: Speech recognition (at most 10 MB) and speech output (at most 2000 characters) run at the level „hinten“, so people at the Spark always go first. The reading tools only read this profile's data. 10. Ask the Spark, read only: ask_spark (10 per minute) runs as one turn of the assistant for the profile, but only with this connection's reading tools. The question counts as outside text from the start: nothing is switched, stored, learned or sent, no memory, nothing of it in the history. Passwords and codes are removed from the answer. 11. Should something change?: Smart home, reminder and appointment are only proposed (at most 10 open). The profile gets a notice and decides under Me → Spark as MCP server within 15 minutes; only then the panel carries it out. With the kill switch or a smart home code word set, an MCP program switches nothing. 12. Answer to the program: The answer is cut to 12000 characters. The journal only gets which program, which tool, whether it worke

head: Way
title: Way
text: d and how long, never question or answer.
