head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: Stage M0: The Spark makes music itself with ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT licence), without the internet. The model only comes with the installation on the model computer: sudo ./install.sh --musik 2b (2B turbo with the 1.7B planner, recommended), 2b-klein (0.6B planner, less memory) or xl (XL turbo, sounds better, needs more); the first install asks, the default is none. The engine is acestep.cpp (ace-server, pinned to one commit, built for the GB10 with CUDA, no torch and no Docker); the GGUF files are pinned by revision and SHA-256 (musikmodell.py). The service speech-spark-musik (musik_server.py, only 127.0.0.1:31004, with a split install through the TLS-Tor, API key) loads the engine only for a song (127.0.0.1:31014, after checking the free memory) and stops it after 10 minutes without a song; the picture and music services share bedarf.py for it. A song takes two steps: the small planner sets structure and audio codes, then the sound model turns them into an MP3 (192 kbit/s). The service sets every field itself, takes only an MP3 back and writes its own ID3 mark into it ("KI-erzeugt mit ACE-Step 1.5"). The admin measures: State → Checks → "Test music" makes two fixed samples for every in

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: Heavy jobs: one model at a time (V01.0.776, plan plaene/schwere-auftraege.md, Dominik 2026-10-18 "only one model loaded at a time, never both"): Painting pictures, changing pictures and making music share one place on the model computer: only the picture model or the music model is loaded, never both. A fixed rule without a switch, like Speech first. All jobs stand in one queue in the panel (schwer.py), "Bild testen" and "Test music" too. The order is by arrival, but while the loaded kind still waits it goes first, at most 3 times in a row while the other kind waits; so the panel seldom reloads and nobody is left behind. When another kind is next, the panel first ends the loaded model (/v1/bild/stop or /v1/musik/stop), else it stays loaded until its idle time as before. The services hold the rule themselves: whoever starts its engine first takes the lock state/bedarf.lock on the model computer; when the other service holds it, it answers 503 "belegt" (counter refused_place in /health). Too little memory no longer ends a job at once: it keeps its place, tries again every 30 seconds and only gives up after 10 minutes. Who waits behind others gets a fixed sentence from the panel, e.g.

head: Voice chat
title: Timers and reminders
text: Timers and reminders: "remind me about the oven in 10 minutes" or "remind me tomorrow at 8 about the appointment". Pending reminders show as small chips below the toggles (✕ cancels); "which timers are running?" and "cancel the oven timer" work by voice too. When one is due, the page chimes, shows it in the conversation and speaks it; if the tab is in the background, a browser notification appears as well. This works while the page is open. Reminders need a profile; they are kept on the Spark. Guests have none. Since V01.0.176 a profile's reminder rings only once: the first device that plays it (an open page, the iPhone app or push) takes it on the Spark, all others stay silent. While a page of the profile is open, push waits 20 seconds so the reminder does not ring there and arrive as a notification too. A reminder that was more than 10 minutes overdue when the page opens shows quietly in the conversation ("Missed"). The iPhone app without Apple push rings with its own alarms; if it is closed then, it reports that the next time it opens. At the same moment as an open page it can then still ring twice; with Apple push it does not. Can be turned off under Features.

This needs https with a valid certificate (e.g. behind a reverse proxy); on an iPhone first add the page to the home screen ("Share → Add to Home Screen"). The Spark only sends to the browsers' push services (Apple, Google, Mozilla, Microsoft), encrypted. Since V01.0.181 every notification (reminder, "speaking up" note, morning briefing, agent report) arrives once: on the device the profile used last (an open page, the iPhone app or Telegram, at most 12 hours back), else the iPhone app, else Telegram, else the browser set up last. Private notes go over Telegram only when the profile allowed personal data there.

head: Voice chat
title: Daily briefing and calendar
text: Daily briefing and calendar: say "good morning" or "what's on today?" and the assistant reads out today's and tomorrow's appointments, today's reminders and a few lines on your own topics (e.g. "weather Berlin", via your SearXNG). "What do I have on Friday?" works too. Each profile connects one or more calendars (up to 8) on the page Calendar, tab Settings; an appointment found in two calendars is read out once. Each one is a CalDAV address with user and app password (iCloud: https://caldav.icloud.com with the Apple ID and an app-specific password from appleid.apple.com; Nextcloud: …/remote.php/dav; Radicale …), or a subscription link with webcal://, webcals:// or https:// (Google: "secret address in iCal format", a public iCloud calendar). New appointments: "put dentist on Tuesday 10 am in my calendar" makes the assistant read out a proposal; only when you answer with a plain yes in the same conversation does the panel itself write it to the first CalDAV calendar (optionally with an alarm). Subscription links stay read only. The password stays on the Spark and is never shown again. Guests get no calendar. Can be turned off under Features.

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: Calendar fast: cache and background refresh (V01.0.817, Dominik 2026-10-19 "calendar slow, caching for entries and background refresh"): The Spark keeps the appointments of each calendar month by month in the panel's memory (calendars.py), never on disk. Page, assistant, briefing and "On its own" read the same months; a month is fetched once even when several ask at the same time. Where an address's calendars are (CalDAV discovery, several requests at iCloud) is kept for 6 hours; after that every fetch goes straight to the calendars. The page waits at most 8 seconds: whatever is still loading then keeps loading in the background and lands in the cache, and the page asks again by itself after 3 seconds (at most 5 times). Before, the fetch was cancelled after 8 seconds and nothing was kept, hence "3 of 3 calendars slow" on every opening. A month older than 5 minutes is shown on the page at once and fetched anew behind it (up to 24 hours old); the assistant waits for a fresh one. Every 5 minutes the panel fetches this and the next month anew for every profile that read its appointments in the last 24 hours. When an appointment or a setting changes, the cache is dropped at once, and a

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: Calendar without panel stalls (V01.0.838, Dominik 2026-10-19, the panel stood still for 6-8 seconds): working out the appointments from the calendar texts (expanding repetitions) is pure Python and ran anew for every look, every minute check and every refresh, for every calendar at once; two such runs held the panel so often that pages hung for seconds. Now the Spark works out each appointment once per calendar month and keeps the result in memory (at most 30,000 entries, never on disk); only a changed appointment or a new month is computed again. All of it runs in one background thread at low priority, never two at once, and lets the panel go after every appointment.

title: Reading e-mail
text: Reading e-mail: "Any new mail?", "What does Anna write?", "Read me the mail from the bank". Each profile connects up to 4 mailboxes over IMAP in the "Me" window, tab E-mail: iCloud (imap.mail.me.com, your iCloud mail address and a new app-specific password from appleid.apple.com), Gmail (imap.gmail.com, app password, needs 2-step verification), GMX and web.de (allow IMAP in their settings first) or any other IMAP server with TLS. The assistant only reads the inbox of the last 30 days and changes nothing: the mailbox is opened read only, no mail is sent, deleted, moved or marked as read. It summarizes mails and reads them out word for word only when asked; the daily briefing names the unread ones. Mail text is treated as someone else's words: once the assistant read a mail in an answer, in that answer it cannot switch smart home devices, change memory, cancel reminders, search the web or enter appointments, so a crafted mail cannot trigger anything; answers made from mails are not learned into memory. head: Voice chat
title: Companion: updates, look, coffee (V01.0.347)
text: Companion: updates, look, coffee (V01.0.347): The programs now look like the panel: the Spark face as icon in taskbar and menu bar (dot bottom right: green reachable, grey not reachable, red kill switch, accent colour when a new version is there), a window on clicking the icon with all parts that are on and their hotkeys, light and dark look following the system. Updates: the Spark fetches new versions itself from the GitHub releases begleiter-windows and begleiter-mac (once a day and only when a device of that kind is paired; Features → Spark companion → "Fetch new version now" at once) and checks size and SHA-256 against the version's begleiter.json. The program learns from its check that a new version is there, downloads it only from the paired Spark, checks size and SHA-256 again and installs only after your click on "Update"; a damaged file is deleted and the old version keeps running. In the Companion app: Settings → About shows the version, "Check for updates" and the switch "Download updates automatically, ask before installing". The first version with updates has to be installed by hand once. The program and Me → Companion carry the link "☕ Support Spark" (buymeacoffee.com

title: Companion deeper in the computer (V01.0.353)
text: Companion deeper in the computer (V01.0.353): eight more parts, all off, turned on per device under Me → Companion: - Right-click on files: "With Spark" in Explorer (Windows 11: "Show more options") and under Services in Finder: summarize, translate, explain (PDF, Office, text, mail, pictures; at most 20 MB, the first 40,000 characters are read) or add to knowledge (needs own documents). - Ask about the screen: Ctrl+Alt+B (⌥⌘B), drag a region, optionally a question, then explain, read out the text or translate. The language model reads the picture; it is kept nowhere. - Know the app: the writing help learns the kind of program (mail, Word, Excel, chat, browser …) and fits tone and form; program names and window titles do not go to the Spark. - Draft a reply: Ctrl+Alt+M (⌥⌘M) for the open mail in Outlook (classic, Windows) or Apple Mail: the answer is a draft in the reply window; nothing is ever sent. In the new Outlook it is on the clipboard. - Spark-Wissen folder: what lands in the folder (default: Spark-Wissen in the user folder) goes into the own documents; a changed file replaces its older version, at most 50 a day. text: Companion: seven more parts (V01.0.375): all off, turned on per device under Me → Companion. Read aloud (Ctrl+Alt+L, ⌥⌘L): marked text in your Spark voice, at most 5000 characters. From the phone to the PC: text (into the clipboard), a link (opened only after asking, only http/https) or a file (at most 20 MB, into "Downloads/Vom Spark") from the panel ("Send to the PC" at the device) or by voice ("Send the link to my PC"); waits up to 24 hours. Appointments in the companion: the next 24 hours with a note 10 minutes before, "Remind me in 20 min" on notes. Recognise do not disturb: while another program uses the microphone or camera or a presentation runs, notes and announcements on your own speakers wait; a summary "Während du beschäftigt warst" follows. Notaus, security notes and reminders always come. Write along in meetings (own admin switch "Write along in meetings", off): only on a click, with a red bar; the microphone and the computer's sound go to speech recognition, the transcript stays in memory only (at most 3 hours). Afterwards a summary and tasks; with "Ausgewählte auf die Liste" chosen tasks go onto a list ("Tasks" by default, selectable; with the date from "due" and th

head: Voice chat
title: Companion update looks right away (V01.0.377)
text: Companion update looks right away (V01.0.377): "Check for updates" in the program and every program start make the Spark look at GitHub at once (at most every 5 minutes per kind of computer); before, it looked once a day. The Mac names the failing step when it refuses an update.

head: Voice chat
title: Companion with the chosen face (V01.0.395)
text: Companion with the chosen face (V01.0.395): the companion shows the face picked under Settings → Defaults (robot, comic or comic woman) in every window and the icon; a change arrives with the next check. In the companion the comic face is a still picture.

head: Voice chat
title: Acting on the PC right at the companion (V01.0.397)
text: Acting on the PC right at the companion (V01.0.397): asked in Ask Spark on the computer itself ("open Safari with Google"), the computer need not be named; a verb of doing (open, start, play, louder, quieter, lock, show) is enough. The question at the computer stays.

head: Voice chat
title: Acting on the PC from a speaker or the phone (V01.0.419)
text: Acting on the PC from a speaker or the phone (V01.0.419): a clear order naming the computer ("Open heise.de on my Mac") is now reliably sent to the computer from there too; the question still comes at the computer. When it cannot go (no computer paired, "Act on the PC" off at the device or for the profile), the Spark says exactly that instead of trying other tools. Speech recognition may write "Mac" as "Mäc".

head: Voice chat
title: Remote control of the computer, stage 1: more fixed orders (V01.0.739)
text: Remote control of the computer, stage 1: more fixed orders (V01.0.739): "Act on the PC" can now also bring a released program to the front ("Switch to Outlook"), close, minimize, maximize or full-screen the front window, press fixed keys (next, previous, space, enter, Esc, Tab, undo, redo, copy, paste, save, reload, find), type your own words ("Type on the PC: be right there"), open a folder (Documents, Downloads, Desktop, Pictures, Music, Videos, Recent), put the computer to sleep or turn the screen off and run a shortcut. Shortcuts (Mac: from the Shortcuts app; Windows: scripts, links, programs) are released only at the computer itself (companion → "Am PC handeln einstellen"); the Spark knows only their names. There are no free key combinations. Only what you said yourself in this sentence is typed; if the model adds words, the panel refuses. The computer asks as before; in the window you can pick "Without asking from now on" for a kind (not for pages, typing and showing a text). You set and undo that only at the computer, Me → Companion only shows it. Requests now arrive at once: the companion waits for them with an open request instead of looking every 10 seconds.

head: Voice chat
title: Remote control of the computer, stage 2: show and operate the screen (V01.0.739)
text: Remote control of the computer, stage 2: show and operate the screen (V01.0.739): Under Me → Companion tap "View screen" or "Operate" for the device and you see the main screen of your own PC or Mac in the panel or in the iPhone or Android app. The computer asks every time: Decline (preselected), View only or Allow (only when operating was asked for). After "Allow" a tap or click on the picture is a click on the computer, dragging moves the mouse, the wheel scrolls, "Right click" makes the next tap a right click; text and fixed keys (Esc, Tab, Enter, Backspace, arrows, Copy, Paste, Undo) come through the bar below the picture. There is no Windows key, Cmd-Space, Alt+Tab or Ctrl+Alt+Del. While it runs the computer shows a red frame and a bar on top with "Beenden" (End); ending also works in the companion menu (Windows), with My emergency stop and in the panel. Up to four pictures a second, at most 1600 pixels wide; the Spark keeps only the newest picture in memory and forgets it at the end. No recording, no history. At most 30 minutes; when nobody watches any more or the computer stops sending, the session ends after 30 seconds. Own admin switch (Features → Show and operate the scre

head: Voice chat
title: Remote control of the computer, stage 3: Spark operates the computer (V01.0.739)
text: Remote control of the computer, stage 3: Spark operates the computer (V01.0.739): "Spark, write to Anna in Outlook that I'll be there at three" – the Spark does the task on your own PC or Mac step by step: it sees the screen, proposes exactly one step (click, double click, right click, scroll, a fixed key or typing text), and the computer shows it with the target marked in red and asks: Stop (preselected), Skip or Allow. Only after "Allow" does the step happen; 60 seconds without an answer count as Stop. Protection against injected orders: the task is fixed from the first sentence and must be in your own words; text on the screen is only content for the Spark. Only text from your task is typed, anything else is shown as a warning above the step. Only a program released under "Act on the PC" may be in front; terminal, settings, login windows, password managers and the Companion itself are always blocked. If something on the screen looks like an order to the Spark, it pauses and asks (No / Continue). At most 30 steps and 5 minutes; Stop, "End" in the bar and My emergency stop end it at once. The result comes as a notice in fixed words ("On the computer: done (4 steps)"); pictures and

title: Remote control of the computer, stage 3: Spark operates the computer (V01.0.739)
text: screen text never go to memory, history or chat. Own admin switch (Features → Spark operates the computer), off until switched on; on the device both "Act on the PC" and "Show and operate the screen" must be on. Needs a language model that sees pictures.

head: Voice chat
title: Describe the screen (V01.0.741)
text: Describe the screen (V01.0.741): "What do you see on my Mac right now?" or "What is open on my PC?" – the computer asks (Decline preselected, 60 seconds without an answer count as Decline), takes one single picture after "Allow", and the Spark describes it in a few sentences. Text on the screen stays content, never an order; it never names passwords, codes or account numbers, and in the same answer it changes nothing afterwards. If a protected program is in front (login, password manager, settings, terminal), it describes nothing. You only see and hear the description: in the history, on other devices and in memory there is only "Here was a description of your screen" instead. Switched on with Features → Spark operates the computer; on the device "Show and operate the screen" must be on. If something is off, the Spark says exactly what is missing.

head: Voice chat
title: Follow-up requests to the computer (V01.0.752)
text: Follow-up requests to the computer (V01.0.752): After "What is running on my Mac?", "Bring the Terminal to the front." or "Again" is enough without naming the computer again: if one of your two messages before named it, the request goes to it (a fixed rule, only with an order word or "again"). "… in den Vordergrund" or "… nach vorne" brings a released program to the front, and the Spark must really ask at the computer for it. After a screen description the next request is no longer locked.

head: Voice chat
title: Office add-ins from the companion (V01.0.433)
text: Office add-ins from the companion (V01.0.433): new part "Office add-ins" (per device, off; needs the writing help). Then "Office-Add-ins einrichten …" in the companion; it asks first. Outlook classic (Windows): a "Spark" button in the ribbon (main window and reading: draft a reply, translate; composing: improve text, translate), also with iCloud or IMAP accounts. The button only sends one fixed word to the running companion, which works as with its hotkeys; nothing is ever sent. Word and Excel (Windows and Mac): the companion registers the Office add-in itself. For that open the panel once at its https address, save under Me → Companion; the admin must have released "In other programs" of the writing help. New Outlook, Outlook for Mac and on the web: the companion shows the file and opens the page "Add from file"; adding it is done by the person (Microsoft allows nothing else, only for Microsoft 365, Exchange or Outlook.com). Part off: everything is removed again.

head: Voice chat
title: Outlook classic hung at start (V01.0.537)
text: Outlook classic hung at start (V01.0.537): with the Spark add-in, Outlook classic stopped at "Loading add-ins". The cause was the self-declared Office interface: the custom parameters were not passed as a SAFEARRAY like in Office. The interface is now declared exactly as Microsoft does, and nothing in the add-in can disturb Outlook with an error. If affected: switch the part "Office add-ins" off in the companion and on again after the update. The setup dialog now names this way out too.

head: Voice chat
title: Blocked Spark add-in (V01.0.545)
text: Blocked Spark add-in (V01.0.545): after a hang Outlook moves an add-in to "Disabled items", and its tick under COM add-ins stays empty. "Office-Add-ins einrichten …" now lifts that block, for Spark only (Resiliency\DisabledItems and CrashingAddinList); other add-ins stay as Outlook set them.

Tabs without content are left out, with only one there is no bar. The window is at most as high as the free screen and only the tab scrolls (one bar); all tabs have the same height so nothing jumps when switching. head: Voice chat
title: Notes with "OK" (V01.0.663)
text: Notes with "OK" (V01.0.663): in the Windows companion's tray window every note has the button "OK" first. It takes the note away without opening anything, and the window stays open so further notes can be confirmed right away. On the Mac notes are macOS notifications and go away as usual with "Close". Needs the new companion build.

head: Voice chat
title: Microphone open/closed (V01.0.549)
text: Microphone open/closed (V01.0.549): the companion (Windows: right-click menu and tray window, Mac: menu bar window) has the switch "Mikrofon schließen" or "Mikrofon öffnen" as soon as a part with the microphone is on (dictation, Ask Spark, wake word, meeting). Closed really means closed: the wake word stops, a running recording is discarded and not sent, a meeting ends, and no button opens the microphone until you open it again. The state stays after a restart. The icon in the taskbar or menu bar then shows a struck-through microphone. Under Me → Companion every connected device shows "Mikrofon offen" or "Mikrofon zu"; Status → Live only counts the devices with the microphone closed. Only this state goes to the Spark, never sound. Needs the new companion build.

head: Voice chat
title: "Draft a reply" no longer hangs (V01.0.545)
text: "Draft a reply" no longer hangs (V01.0.545): when Outlook asks something while creating the reply (e.g. "Download external content?"), the companion waits for it. That question used to sit behind the companion window, so everything looked frozen. Now the companion brings Outlook to the front, no longer stays on top of it and shows "Outlook öffnet den Entwurf … bitte dort antworten". While the Spark writes, the seconds count up, and "Abbrechen" stops it.

head: Voice chat
title: Speaking into the companion windows (V01.0.466)
text: Speaking into the companion windows (V01.0.466): with the part "Dictation" on, every free text field in the companion windows has a mic button: "Draft a reply" (notes and mail text), "Improve text" (wish, source text, result), "Ask about the screen" (question) and, as before, "Ask Spark". First click starts, the second (■) stops the recording (at most 60 seconds); the Spark recognizes the text, it goes to the cursor or the end and is never run. So the Outlook classic buttons "Draft a reply" and "Improve text" can be used by voice too. Never in code word or password fields. The Office add-ins in Word, Excel and new Outlook have no mic button. Button labels never break inside a word; if the Mac panel is too narrow, "Spark unterstützen" moves to its own line.

head: Voice chat
title: Companion tidied up (V01.0.729, Dominik 2026-10-17)
text: Companion tidied up (V01.0.729, Dominik 2026-10-17): the window on clicking the face is reordered: at the top a greeting, device and state as a dot, on the right a gear (settings) and ✕ or power; below the field "Frag Spark …" (Enter asks, the microphone asks by voice), the commands as tiles with their hotkey and sections like in the panel: next up, notes (Windows), home and "this computer" or "this Mac" with switches for microphone and wake word and, when "act on the PC" is on, the row "act on the PC … set up" (a running screen session can also be ended there on the PC). At the bottom "Open panel" and "Notaus …". The settings have a side menu like the panel (overview with the state and the parts switched on in the panel, Ask Spark, hotkeys, start of the day, knowledge folder, below "device" with pairing and About and update; on the Mac also permissions); pages of parts that are off are left out. The coffee button is only in About and update now, quietly. Parts, rights and data are unchanged.

head: Voice chat
title: Room mode
text: Room mode (Features → Home → "Room mode", off by default; profiles only): the switch "Raum" below the face lets the assistant listen to the conversation in the room at this device for a chosen time (15 minutes to 4 hours, it ends by itself); an orange dot shows it. In a pause it helps when a fixed cue came up: an open question (with web search, nothing when in doubt), an appointment ("Shall I enter it?"), "cold", "too warm" or "too dark" (the room's real temperature from Home Assistant, offering to change the heating by one degree or switch on the light) and things to buy (Home Assistant shopping list). It changes something only after a "yes", for the smart home with the code word when one is set. In the "Me" window under "Room mode" each device sets the duration, how much it may say (questions only, also hints, also comments), each kind on its own, the device's room in Home Assistant and "text only" (silently in the conversation instead of spoken). What it hears stays in the panel's memory for five minutes and is never stored; room mode uses neither memory, mail nor earlier conversations. Everyone in the room should know it is listening. Since V01.0.95 it also offers a timer ("The

head: Voice chat
title: Room mode
text: pizza needs 12 more minutes") and a reminder ("I must not forget to call grandma"), both only after a "yes", and calculates unit questions ("How much is 180 degrees in Fahrenheit?"). A question that points back ("When did he die?") is completed from the last sentences, only with words that were said. With a taught voice and speaker identification on, only the profile's own voice can say "yes". A soft tone comes before it speaks; "Stopp" ends the sentence, "Nicht jetzt" keeps it quiet for 15 minutes, "Raummodus aus" (also "Hör auf zuzuhören") switches it off, from any voice. Since V01.0.126 the profile's quiet hours apply (Me → By itself, 22 to 7 by default): then everything appears as text only, never spoken. When the page is in the background or the phone locked for more than two minutes (the microphone hears nothing there anyway), room mode ends with its summary; closing the tab ends it at once. Since V01.0.128 it also runs on the own ESP32 speakers, all board variants: "Raummodus an" after the wake word or the switch "Room" under Me → Speakers (when the speaker sleeps, it starts at its next wake word), where duration, how much it may say and the room in Home Assistant are set p

head: Voice chat
title: Room mode
text: er speaker. The Spark keeps the connection open, cuts out every sentence, runs it through speech recognition and speaks in a pause after the soft tone; boards with a display show the sentence. It ends after its time, with "Raummodus aus", the switch, when the connection drops or when the admin or the profile switch it off; then the board waits for its wake word again. In quiet hours the speaker stays silent. Since V01.0.140 the speaker cuts long stretches of talk after at most 8 seconds and checks every sentence on its own, speaks after 1.5 seconds of quiet (counted from the last loud sound, not from the end of a piece), streams the speech, and each speaker has "detect more". Questions are now recognized without a question mark from the speech recognition ("Wie hoch ist die Zugspitze"), after "Sag mal" or "Weißt du, wann …" and with "Stimmt es, dass …"; questions about the people in the room ("Wo ist meine Brille") stay out. The answer is looked up while people still talk and is ready in the pause (in the browser too). "Also comments" is chattier: at most every two minutes, after three seconds of quiet, one casual sentence about the conversation. Since V01.0.142 Me → Speakers has "

head: Voice chat
title: Room mode
text: Stimme hier anlernen" (speaker identification on, browser login, with the second step when set up): the speaker asks for three sentences and keeps its own voiceprint for its microphone; a sentence counts for a profile when it fits any of its voiceprints (browser or speaker). Until somebody taught a voice through a speaker, it listens to everybody despite "only known voices" (log: "listens to everybody (no voice taught through it yet)"), because a voice taught in the browser is rarely recognized through the small board microphone. At most two speakers at once, because speech recognition runs all the time. While it speaks, the wake word interrupts it. Option "Genauer erkennen": the model looks for missed questions, appointments and shopping, counted only with a word-for-word quote. When room mode ends, the page shows what it said and did (not what it heard), not stored. Every decision writes a "room:" line to the log (why it spoke or stayed silent, never the heard text).

head: Voice chat
title: Ignoring TV voices
text: Ignoring TV voices (since V01.0.139; Features → Room mode → "Fernsehstimmen überhören", off by default): every device picks under Me → Room mode "Who it listens to" (speakers under Me → Speakers): *everybody* (as before, default), *only known voices while the TV is on* (recommended) or *always only known voices*. A voice is known when a profile taught it under Me → Speaker identification; speaker identification must be on. It then runs for every sentence in room mode, on the CPU next to speech recognition (about 0.1 s per sentence), with no extra GPU load. Whether the TV is on comes from Home Assistant at most every 30 seconds: a media player on, playing or buffering in the device's room, without a room set anywhere in the home; when Home Assistant does not answer, it listens to everybody as before. A sentence in a foreign voice triggers no question or suggestion and is dropped at once; the model never sees it, not with "Genauer erkennen" or comments either. Always counted: a sentence starting with "Spark" (also from visitors), "Stopp", "Nicht jetzt" and "Raummodus aus". A "yes" still counts only in the profile's voice. Very short sentences (under about one second of speech) are of

head: Voice chat
title: Ignoring TV voices
text: ten not recognized and count as foreign. With *Trial* (on at first) nothing is ignored, only counted: at the end the summary and the log say "Probelauf: Von 40 Sätzen hätte ich 12 als fremde Stimme überhört.", for speakers also under *Check*. Only this number is kept, never the text or whose voice it was; the log says "room: ignored (unknown voice)" or "(unknown voice, tv on)".

head: Voice chat
title: Where it listens right now
text: Where it listens right now (since V01.0.208; part of room mode, no switch of its own): the Spark keeps a list of every device in room mode, browser pages and speakers, in memory only and only with name, kind, since/until, "who it listens to" and trial, never anything heard. A page signs in when switched on and gives a sign of life every minute; without one for three minutes (tab closed, phone locked) it drops out. After a restart it signs in again with its next sign of life. It shows (1) as a green strip on top of every page ("Kitchen listens until 21:30", View opens Me → Room mode), (2) at the face as "Also the kitchen is listening", (3) under Me → Room mode → *Active now* with *+30 min* and *Stop* (speakers waiting for their next wake word with *Do not start*), (4) for the admin under Status → *Listening right now* with profile, device and time, *Stop* and *Stop all*, and as a mark "listening" and the filter "listening right now" under People and devices. A page in room mode shows "● Room" in the tab title and a red dot on its icon. Everybody who sees the list may end a room (it only means less listening); extending only in the profile's browser login, never beyond 4 hours from n

head: Voice chat
title: Where it listens right now
text: ow. A browser's name is set under Me → Room mode → *Name of this device* (else e.g. "iPad · Safari", with a device key its name). *Reminder tone* (per device, speakers under Me → Speakers, off): the soft tone every 15 minutes, never in quiet hours. *Note when a speaker starts listening* (profile, off): when somebody says "Raummodus an" at your speaker, a note goes to the device used last, at most once an hour per speaker, never in quiet hours. *Recently*: the last 20 times within 14 days with device, time, how it ended and how many sentences were heard, said and ignored, never text (users/<profile>/room-history.json, in the backup). Home Assistant (admin: Features → Room mode → *Room mode for Home Assistant*, off): under Me → Room mode → Home Assistant the profile makes a key of its own (with the second step when set up; a new one replaces the old). It may only GET /api/room/active (count, first device, until when) and POST /api/room/end ({"all": true}), nothing else; the page shows the ready text for configuration.yaml once (REST sensor "Spark Raum-Modus", command spark_raummodus_aus). The log only says "room: listed …", "room: … ended (panel|iphone|ha|admin)" and "room: page … ga

title: Where it listens right now

head: Voice chat
title: Starting from afar
text: Starting from afar (since V01.0.213; admin: Features → Room mode → *Start room mode from afar*, off; then for every profile): "Raummodus im Wohnzimmer an" (also "Kannst du den Raummodus für den Lautsprecher im Wohnzimmer aktivieren?", "… für 60 Minuten") in the panel, the iPhone app or at another speaker. The panel recognizes the sentence by fixed rules (roomfar.py); the language model gets no tools in that answer, Home Assistant is not asked and no code word is wanted. Only the profile's own speakers, found by name or by the room entered under Me → Speakers; when several fit, the answer names them. The speaker must be connected right now (it does not start later by itself; the switch "Room" is for that). Only a plain "Ja" in the next message of the same conversation (15 minutes) starts it; the speaker says "Raum-Modus an, gestartet von der iPhone-App" (or the panel, the kitchen speaker). Duration from the sentence (rounded to 15/30/60/120/240 minutes), else the speaker's own. Not via Telegram or Siri, never for guests or a voice recognized as someone else. "Raummodus im Wohnzimmer aus" / "Raummodus überall aus" ends without a question (history: "ended from another device"). With t

head: Voice chat
title: Starting from afar
text: he switch off there is a fixed answer naming the switch. "Starte den Raummodus" without a place stays the device's own room mode. Log: "room: start at speaker … asked from …", "room: on at speaker … (remote from …)".

head: Voice chat
title: Speaking up by itself
text: Speaking up by itself (Features → My day → "Speaking up by itself", off by default; profiles only): once released it is on from the start for every profile; in the "Me" window under "By itself" each profile sets why the assistant speaks unasked, each kind on its own, or switches it off entirely: appointments ahead ("In 20 minutes: dentist. Shall I remind you again at 9:55?", a "yes" sets the reminder), its own smart home rules ("Whirlpool above 37.5", "bathroom window is open and rain is on", "washing machine power below 5 for 3 minutes"; read only, never switching), a short greeting with the next appointment or reminder when the conversation is opened after three hours or more, at most one follow-up a day on a plan mentioned yesterday, new mail from chosen senders (sender and subject only) and a weather note for tomorrow via web search. Plus quiet hours, a daily limit and learning from feedback: "nicht jetzt" means two hours of quiet, "das interessiert mich nicht" halves how often that kind may speak (can be reset). The panel decides when, by fixed rules from real data; where the model words something (follow-up, weather), its answer only counts when it quotes the data. With the c

head: Voice chat
title: Speaking up by itself
text: onversation open the note is spoken, otherwise it arrives as a push notification. Since V01.0.179 only the first device of the profile says it (page or iPhone app), the others stay silent, just like reminders (V01.0.176). Every note is in the log with its reason. Since V01.0.385 the follow-up is a fixed sentence with the person's own words ("Gestern hast du zu mir gesagt: „…“. Hat das geklappt?"); the model only points at a sentence, and the panel takes it only when it is an own plan in the first person (no question, no request to the assistant, no pasted text, no question about a mail or web page, nothing from briefing, jobs or meetings). Asked about a note ("what do you mean?", "where is that from?"), the model gets its basis from the panel and must not make up another source; for mail notes only "sender and subject read", never mail text. Logs → Requests show it as "von selbst: Grundlage", Live shows a refused pick as an event. Since V01.0.810 the mail rows (important mail, mailbox tidying, parcel comes today) sit under E-mail → Settings and appointments ahead under Calendar → Settings; Me → By itself keeps the main switch, quiet hours, the daily limit and the other kinds.

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant tells the Spark
text: Home Assistant tells the Spark (since V01.0.314, plan plaene/home-assistant-meldungen.md): the smart home rules under "By itself" can do more. Each rule can speak *at most every N minutes* (e.g. a motion sensor at most every 10 minutes), for "changes" *on*, *off* or both, and have an extra condition: *only when I am away* (the person in Home Assistant with your profile name or the one chosen under "Me in Home Assistant"), *only when nobody is home*, *only at night* or *only during the day* (by sun.sun, else 9 pm to 6 am). Plus five parts, each with its own admin switch under Features → Speaking up by itself, all off at first, never for guests. Once released they work for every profile; what speaks up by itself is on from the start and can be switched off one by one under Me → By itself: *Instant notes from Home Assistant*: the Spark keeps a WebSocket connection to your Home Assistant (the same address and token, only the devices of your rules, subscribe_entities); a change arrives in about a second, also a motion sensor that triggers only briefly. If the connection drops, the Spark checks every minute again. *House notes on speakers*: a rule also says its own sentence on chosen spe

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant tells the Spark
text: akers that take announcements from you, e.g. "Someone rang the bell."; only its own sentence without names, never for person devices and never with a camera picture, not in the speaker's quiet hours, at most 20 an hour. *Home Assistant tells the Spark*: a list of event names with a fixed sentence (e.g. klingel → "Es hat geklingelt.") and a key of its own; Home Assistant calls rest_command.spark_melden with event: klingel (POST /api/ha/event). Only names from the list count, nothing else from the request is read or said; at most 30 a minute, a pause per event (default 1 minute). *Smart home rule by voice*: "Sag mir Bescheid, wenn jemand an der Haustür ist", "Melde dich, wenn Anna heimkommt": the panel recognizes the sentence by fixed words, finds the device and asks "Soll ich mich melden, wenn …?"; only a "yes" in the same conversation adds the rule. *Describe a camera picture*: a rule can name a camera from Home Assistant; when it applies, the local language model describes the still in a few words. The picture is never stored, the description is outside text and goes to your devices only, at most 30 an hour. Log lines start with "hamelden:". Status → Live shows the live connection

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant tells the Spark
text: (under channels) and each note, event and described camera picture in fixed words, without device names, sentences or camera words. You don't have to type devices for a rule (since V01.0.317): the field suggests all devices from Home Assistant, "Zuletzt geändert" shows the last changed ones, and with "Gerät erkennen" you trigger the sensor within 40 seconds (motion, door, bell); whatever changes shows up to tap. The panel only compares the change time Home Assistant reports itself. Rules can be edited (since V01.0.319): "Edit" brings a rule back into the form, "Check and save" checks it like a new one and replaces it in the same place; it then starts fresh (speaks only after it was false once). Since V01.0.334 each fired rule and event shows on Status → Live as a request of "Home Assistant" (rule or event) with camera picture, note (Web Push, Apple Push, Android app, Telegram or the open page) and speaker announcement; everything else the Spark says by itself as a request of "Von selbst" (e.g. greeting, reminder, task). Never the sentence.

head: Voice chat
title: Natural turn-taking
text: Natural turn-taking (on by default, conversation settings): during a short pause the recording is transcribed already. A finished sentence ends the turn at once and its transcript becomes the question, so the answer starts noticeably sooner; after "and …", "because …", "um" or a comma the assistant waits up to 2 s for you to go on.

head: Voice chat
title: New conversation every day
text: New conversation every day (on by default, conversation settings → Display): the first question of a new day starts a new conversation; earlier ones stay in the history and can be picked and continued.

head: Voice chat
title: Speaker identification
text: Speaker identification (off by default, Features): each profile reads three short sentences in the "Me" window. When the assistant then clearly recognizes a voice, it answers for that profile, with its memory, documents, reminders and voice, even on a guest device. The conversation shows "🎙 name" below the question. When someone other than the logged-in profile speaks at a device, the assistant gets only that one question (not the device's conversation), and the exchange stays out of the logged-in profile's history and memory. When the voice is unclear, nothing changes. Recognition runs on the Spark's CPU (Resemblyzer model, Apache 2.0) and needs no GPU memory. Strictness is adjustable. A voice is not a password: someone who sounds very similar or plays a recording can get into a profile.

head: Voice chat
title: Profiles and memory
text: Profiles and memory: under People and devices the admin creates profiles with a name and PIN. In the chat you log in with the "Guest" button at the top of the conversation by typing name and PIN. Logged in, the assistant remembers things for good when you tell it to ("remember that I'm vegetarian") or when they will be useful later, and forgets them on request; the Me lists what it knows, for deleting. Memory and conversations belong to the profile and live on the Spark, so the same history shows on every device you are logged in on: which profile is asking is decided only by the login (cookie) or the device key, never by the model, and guests get no memory. Speakers and your own programs get a device key under People and devices that belongs to one profile, and send it as the header X-Speech-Device to /api/chat. A new PIN logs out every browser of that profile; deleting a profile removes its memory and devices. The data lives on the Spark under /var/lib/speech-spark/users, one folder per profile.

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant
text: Home Assistant (Funktionen → "Home Assistant", off by default): each profile connects its own Home Assistant in the "Me" window under "Smart home" with the address (e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123) and a long-lived access token (Home Assistant: your profile → Security; best for a separate non-admin user). Then "turn on the living room light" or "how warm is it in the bathroom?" work in the conversation. Commands go to Home Assistant's own Assist (/api/conversation/process), so only entities exposed to Assist (in Home Assistant: Settings → Voice assistants → Expose) can be switched. Devices Assist does not know are switched directly through their service (e.g. switch.turn_on), except locks, alarm systems and updates. With a code word ("Me" window → Smart home) the assistant switches only when the code word is in the same message ("lights off, code word sunflower"); without it, it asks. The panel checks this itself, not the language model; the model and the stored conversations see only "[Codewort]", it is stored encrypted and compared with some tolerance for speech recognition (a letter or two off, "Apollo 13" = "Apollo dreizehn"). Questions need no code word. Also (ideas from

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant
text: ha-mcp): history ("how warm was it in the bathroom yesterday?"), several devices at once ("all lights in the living room off", each checked; an unknown room never switches the whole home), typo-tolerant device search and to-do lists such as the shopping list (read, add, tick off; changes need the code word). Questions about values, states, zones and where someone is are read directly (/api/states) instead: the assistant sees every device, sensor, zone and person the token's user may see, exposed or not. Home Assistant tells rooms (areas) only to an admin token; without admin rights devices are found by their names only. Only that profile can use its Home Assistant: guests never, and a voice recognized by speaker identification at someone else's device neither. The token is checked before saving, stays on the Spark (users/<id>/homeassistant.json, mode 0600) and is never sent back to the browser. When several devices fit a switching command, the device whose name, room or device class fits wins over one that only fits by its kind ("TV in the living room" is the TV there, not the Apple TV box next to it). If it stays unclear, the Spark switches nothing and names the fitting devices; t

head: Voice chat
title: Home Assistant
text: he model then gets no switching tool (since V01.0.461).

head: Voice chat
title: Ask instead of guessing
text: Ask instead of guessing (Funktionen → "Rückfrage statt Raten", off by default; released for every profile): when several devices fit a switching command, the Spark switches nothing at random but asks: "Several fit: Samsung, Samsung The Frame or TV. Which one do you mean?". In the chat the devices are buttons below it, plus "None of these". When it cannot find the device exactly it asks "I can't find that exactly. Do you mean …?"; "None of these" or "show all" brings the whole device list with a search field, grouped by room (never locks, alarm panels or remotes). The answer may be typed, spoken or tapped: name, room or number ("the second"). It only counts in the same conversation, on the same device and for two minutes; the code word of the command covers the choice but is never stored or spoken. When the Spark itself picked one of several devices, "No, the Apple TV" corrects it: the wrongly switched device goes back to its old state, the right one is switched. Fixed rules in the panel decide, never the language model. (since V01.0.470)

head: Voice chat
title: Remember the choice
text: Remember the choice (sub-switch, off by default): after a choice or a correction the Spark asks "Shall I remember that "TV in the living room" is Samsung?" (buttons "Yes, remember" and "No"). Only a yes stores it. From then on the same sentence switches that device at once; the code word is still needed. All mappings are under Me → Memory → "Mappings": change words, other target, delete, or assign your own from the device list with "Give own names". They live in the profile's zuordnungen.json and go with the memory into your own storage and the backup. The live page shows numbers only (open questions, asked today, chosen, corrected, remembered, used), the log fixed words only ("klaeren: frage ha 3 kandidaten"), never devices or sentences. (since V01.0.470)

head: Voice chat
title: Asking back for bus and train, weather and messages too
text: Asking back for bus and train, weather and messages too (same switch): "to the station" fits several stops and names none exactly, so the Spark asks with buttons instead of taking the first; the same for place names in different regions ("Karlsbad" in Germany and Czechia) in the weather and for lists in Home Assistant ("Einkauf" fits "Einkaufsliste" and "Einkauf Baumarkt"; for a change the code word of the request covers the choice). The choice runs the same request with the chosen target; after a yes the word stands for it from then on (Me → Memory → Mappings, areas "Bus and train", "Places (weather)" and "Lists"). With "Do you mean Quirin Meier or Quirin Müller?" the names are buttons below. In Telegram the choices come as a keyboard under the answer; a tap sends the name like a typed answer. In the apps and at a speaker the spoken or typed answer does it (name, room or number). A calendar named for an appointment that does not exist is never silently replaced by the first one any more: the Spark enters nothing and names the calendars there are. (since V01.0.470)

head: Voice chat
title: Searching conversations
text: Searching conversations: the magnifier next to the conversation list (on phones in the menu) searches all earlier conversations, a profile's with a profile, the browser's as a guest. A click opens the conversation at that spot.

head: Voice chat
title: Earlier conversations
text: Earlier conversations (Funktionen → "Frühere Gespräche", on by default; profiles only): the assistant can look up what you talked about before ("what did you tell me about the grill last week?", "what did we talk about yesterday?"), searching only your own profile's saved conversations. Conversations that have been quiet for ten minutes are also read once in the background, while nobody is talking, and up to three lasting facts per conversation go into the profile's memory, marked "automatic" in the "Me" window, where they can be deleted. Each profile can switch this learning off in the conversation settings ("Learn from conversations"). Once a week (or with "Propose cleanup") the assistant proposes merging duplicate entries and removing outdated ones; nothing changes until you accept the proposal under Me → Memory. With notifications on, a note is sent.

head: Voice chat
title: Pronunciation
text: Pronunciation: Settings → Speech output → Pronunciation takes one rule per line, e.g. DGX = De Ge Ix. It applies to whole words and to all speech output, Open WebUI included.

head: Voice chat
title: Barge-in
text: Barge-in: while the assistant speaks, the microphone keeps listening. Talking for about a quarter of a second interrupts the answer, and what you said becomes the next question. This relies on the browser's echo cancellation; if the assistant interrupts itself on loud speakers, use headphones or untick "barge in" below the chat. With "Barge-in: pause first" (see below) the answer only pauses, and a "mhm" lets it play on.

head: Voice chat
title: Read answers aloud (since V01.0.409)
text: Read answers aloud (since V01.0.409): if you do not want speech output, switch it off. For one device, the "Vorlesen" switch below the face (on a phone the speaker icon at the top right of the chat) is enough; it applies to this browser or the Android app only. For all devices of the profile: conversation settings → answer → "Read answers aloud". The Spark then answers as text only, does not call the speech output at all (saves the GPU) and plays no instant acknowledgement either; notes, messages and reminders come with a chime and text but are not read aloud. Speakers without a screen and CarPlay keep speaking, there is nothing to read there. "Read again" on an answer still works. The Spark-Begleiter does not read "Frag Spark" answers aloud either while "Read answers aloud" is off.

head: Voice chat
title: Your own voice
text: Your own voice: under Voices you can record a reference straight from the microphone (read the suggested text, about 10 seconds); the panel fills in the transcript with the speech recognition. Cloning needs a Base model (Settings → Speech output → model …-Base), then pick the new voice as the default voice. The default voice is a list that fits the chosen model: CustomVoice shows the built-in speakers, Base your own voices, with VoiceDesign it is locked (the voice comes from the speaking style); a saved name missing from the list stays as "(not in the list)". A German reference gives much steadier German than the built-in speakers, which are not native German speakers. Under Voices, one or all of your own voices can be exported as a ZIP (reference audio and transcript) and imported again on this or another Spark; on a name clash the import renames, replaces or skips.

head: Voice chat
title: Required tools and answer check (V01.0.117)
text: Required tools and answer check (V01.0.117): questions about appointments, mail, reminders, timers, weather, parcels, transit, lists, match results and news have to go through the matching tool (one table NEED_TOOLS in chat.py, also used by the quality test). While the model chooses the tool, the "tool choice" temperature (0.1) applies, the normal one afterwards. The answer check (Settings → Language model, on by default) lets no sentence through for such questions that names a time, date, score or amount that is in no tool result, the question or the conversation so far; instead the assistant says once "Genauere Angaben dazu habe ich nicht." If the model answers without looking anything up, the answer is dropped and the model is asked once more. Both show up in the tool log as "Antwort-Prüfung". General questions without a tool are not checked. Optional: the admin allows "think while choosing tools" (off); then it works for every profile, never for guests. Since V01.0.404 a round with thinking holds its text until the thinking is over: when the server does not hand the thinking over apart (reasoning_content) but as text up to a lone </think> (Qwen gets the opening <think> in the p

head: Voice chat
title: Required tools and answer check (V01.0.117)
text: rompt), everything before it is never shown, spoken or kept; a lone </think> is never shown (before, the answer came twice with </think> between). Since V01.0.455 no sentence of an answer comes twice: when the model writes the answer before a tool call (also one it only writes as text) and again after the result, the next round shows each sentence only once it is complete and leaves out sentences already said, in the chat and in the voice; Logs → Requests then show "Repetition left out" with the count.

head: Voice chat
title: Check deeds and stop error loops (V01.0.477)
text: Check deeds and stop error loops (V01.0.477): two protection rules, on by default like the answer check (Settings → Language model, chat.action_check, chat.loop_stop, reason in features.DEFAULT_ON), without a switch per profile (taten.py, fixed rules, no model). Check deeds: every tool that changes something has a kind (taten.KIND: geraet, erinnerung, termin, mail_entwurf, dokument, remarkable, nachricht, merken, aufgabe, musik and more). Per answer the panel keeps which kind worked (the same failure words as Logs → Requests; "NOT saved yet" counts as a proposal, not as a deed). When a finished sentence claims a deed ("is on now", "I have entered it", "has been sent", "I'll remember", a bare "Done." while something that changes things was offered) and none of the kinds it names worked, it is neither shown nor spoken. At the end comes one fixed sentence: "That did not work: TV." (the tool ran and failed) or "I did not do that." (it did not run); nothing while a proposal is open. No second try. When a tool of that kind works later in the same answer ("I'm making the song." before musik_machen), the held sentence is left out silently (since V01.0.700). In doubt the sentence is said (i

head: Voice chat
title: Check deeds and stop error loops (V01.0.477)
text: t names several deeds and one of them worked). Stop error loops: when the same tool fails twice with the same details (or three times with any), it is not offered again for the rest of the answer, the model hears why, a further call is not run. Visible in Logs → Requests ("Taten-Prüfung", "Schleife gestoppt"), in the journal (chat: action check: held back kind=… reason=…, chat: loop stop: tool=… fails=…) and on the Live page ("Taten-Prüfung": held back and stopped today, numbers only). The settings assistant's rule set will use the same interface taten.check(text, acts, offered) (a fixed "built-in" rule).

head: Voice chat
title: Three red questions in the quality test (V01.0.574)
text: Three red questions in the quality test (V01.0.574): (1) Announced deed: a sentence that only announces a tool call or a deed ("I'm calling the timer tool …", "I'll set a timer …", taten.announces) is neither shown nor spoken while no tool has worked in this answer. When a tool call follows, it is left out silently; when none follows, the panel says "I did not do that." at the end. Check deeds now also applies when no tool at all was offered (then every claimed deed is false). Journal: chat: action check: held back kind=ankuendigung …, chat: action check: announcement left out, a tool ran. (2) Remember only what there is to remember: a message that only asks (one sentence with a question mark, no "remember", nothing the person says about themselves like "I am …"; chat.just_asks) is not offered memory_save (chat.offer_memory, in the quality test as well), so "Do you know my brother's name?" never saves a made-up fact; journal chat: memory_save not offered - the message only asks. (3) Account balance: there is no bank tool, so every honest answer is right ("no access", "no tool", "check your banking app"). Since the fix after V01.0.597 the quality test checks no wording here, only fa

head: Voice chat
title: Three red questions in the quality test (V01.0.574)
text: cts: an amount in figures or words (quality.MONEY) or an unsuitable tool fails. The two cases without calendar and mail access still accept every "no access" answer (quality.NO_ACCESS).

head: Voice chat
title: Appointments only fresh from the calendar (V01.0.348)
text: Appointments only fresh from the calendar (V01.0.348): "Guten Morgen" on its own (also with "Spark", "wie geht's") counts as asking for the day: the switch files it under the calendar and the first round has to call daily_briefing (without the briefing: calendar_events). Before another request ("Guten Morgen, turn on the light") it does not. The same for the briefing by name, also as one word (V01.0.847): "Morgenbriefing", "Gib mir mein Tagesbriefing", "Was ist mein Morgenbriefing?" go to the calendar and call daily_briefing; only "Was ist das Morgenbriefing?" or "Wie stelle ich es ein?" asks about the function (Spark help). Every calendar result marks appointments that have already ended with "(already over)"; briefing and daily overview do not name them as coming up. Once an answer has read the calendar, the answer check takes times, dates and quoted appointment titles only from the question, the instructions and this answer's results, no longer from earlier answers in the conversation, so yesterday's appointments never come back as today's (tool log: "Termin aus früherer Antwort").

head: Voice chat
title: Learning from corrections (V01.0.118)
text: Learning from corrections (V01.0.118): admin switch Features → Conversation → "Learning from corrections", off; released for every profile, never guests or another voice. When a message right after an answer starts like a correction ("Nein, …", "Das stimmt nicht", "Du sollst …", at least three words), the model words a short sentence on the side (fixes.py) and the assistant ends with "Soll ich mir merken: …?". It is stored only after a plain yes from the same conversation within 15 minutes. Never proposed: sentences about code words, PINs, passwords, rules, security, confirmations, locks or alarms, world knowledge (scores, amounts) and links; after mail or outside text there is no proposal, and the earlier answer is then not sent along. The tool log shows a "Korrektur" entry; "Send the question to the admin as a test case" puts the corrected question into quality-cases.json (at most 30) and it runs with the quality test: all tools offered, each finds nothing, made-up figures count as a failure. The admin deletes them under Status → Checks → Quality test.

head: Voice chat
title: Memory check (V01.0.467)
text: Memory check (V01.0.467): admin switch Features → Memory check, off; released for every profile, never guests (gedaechtnis.py, plan gedaechtnis-pruefen/plan.md). Every entry keeps its evidence, also while the switch is off: where it came from (said remembered in a conversation, fix from a confirmed correction, auto learned from a quiet conversation, hand changed under Me, tidy from an accepted cleanup proposal), which conversation (own ones only, never to the model) and when it was last confirmed. Entries of older versions count as auto when they were learned, else as said. text: Exact calculations (rechnen.py, tool rechnen, Dominik 2026-10-22): A language model is bad at arithmetic, so the panel computes. The model only writes down the calculation or the dates, the panel computes with its own small calculator (split into tokens, then an own parser; never eval, exec, sympy or a foreign calculator) and returns its result as "Ergebnis vom Panel: …"; the model only says that figure. Date arithmetic by fixed rules: days until a day, days between two days, the weekday of a day, the date in n days (also "Christmas", "New Year", "24.12."). Hard limits: at most rechnen.MAX_CHARS (200) characters and rechnen.MAX_TOKENS (80) tokens, rechnen.MAX_DEPTH (12) nested brackets, powers up to rechnen.MAX_EXP (100), results up to 10¹⁵, dates up to 100 years; else "Fehler beim Rechnen" with a fixed reason. Offered only when the person's own words ask for a calculation (rechnen.WORDS), next to any Weiche group (werkzeug_abdeckung.BY_WORD). The answer check also c

head: Voice chat
title: Voice chat
text: Number words, required tool, paper and receipts (rechnen.digits, rechnen.wants, rechnen.check, Dominik 2026-10-22): Spoken number words become digits before computing ("sechs mal sechs" → 6 mal 6, "twenty-three point five" → 23.5, "two million"), German and English, with fixed word lists; an article only counts before "hundred", "thousand" or "million". head: The panel
title: The panel
text: The menu (since V01.0.145, design "Klar") is a sidebar on the left on computers and a bar at the bottom on phones (Assistant, Me, Status, Manage). At the very top Search (Ctrl K or ⌘ K, since V01.0.265) finds pages, switches, settings, Me, checks, logs and guides; a hit opens the place and marks it. Since V01.0.521 the button is in the menu for signed-in profiles too, phones have a magnifier at the top of the assistant (admin and profile), and the search box fits narrow screens and closes with ✕. A way in a hint or an answer like "Settings → Spark → Operation" or "Me → Documents" is a link that jumps right there (since V01.0.435). Below are Assistant and Me for yourself, then under *Manage Spark* the admin pages Status, Features (with *Guides*), People and devices (with *Apps and interfaces*) and Settings (since V01.0.265; "Integrate" is gone). Status, Features and People and devices have sub-pages; a number next to "Settings" counts unsaved pages. On a computer "Me" opens as a page right of the sidebar since V01.0.147 instead of a window; another menu entry closes it.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: - Assistent (assistant): voice chat with the language model (the own one behind the LLM-Tor or qwen38). Speak (or type); the answer comes back as text and streamed speech, sentence by sentence while the LLM is still writing. Hands-free mode listens again after each answer; the space bar or "Speak" interrupts. If nobody says anything for 8 seconds after an answer, the microphone goes off and the status line says so ("Heard nothing, microphone off"); only "Hey Spark" listens all the time. Follow-up without wake word (admin: Features → Follow-up without wake word, off by default; profile: Me → Conversation, off/4/6/8/10 seconds): after answering a spoken question (via "Hey Spark" or "Speak") the microphone stays open for the chosen time, so "And tomorrow?" works without the wake word; if nothing comes it goes off and "Hey Spark" keeps listening. Unlike hands-free only briefly and only after spoken questions; never after typed questions, never for guests, never in room mode. The ESP32 speakers do not have it (they listen for "Jarvis" on the chip). On an iPhone, iOS ends the microphone when the screen locks, the page goes to the background, a call comes in or Siri speaks. head: The panel
title: The panel
text: The panel is available in English and German; the button at the top right switches (default: the browser's language).

head: The panel
title: History on every device
text: History on every device (since V01.0.457): a profile's conversations live on the Spark. The panel, the Android app and the iPhone app send only the new messages after each answer, and the Spark appends them. When two devices ask in the same conversation (for example today's conversation on the computer and on the phone), both questions stay; before, the second device overwrote the first. An open page fetches what other devices added as soon as it is in front again and every 30 seconds (only changed ones, at most 120 requests per minute and profile). Only deleting replaces the Spark's copy. Questions from the Pebble watch are kept like Siri, Telegram and the companion as their own conversation per day ("Uhr 12.10."). Guests keep their history in their own browser only.

head: The panel
title: Instant history sync, one conversation for all channels, offline reading
text: Instant history sync, one conversation for all channels, offline reading (since V01.0.457, each function off until the admin switches it on under Features; then for every profile; never guests):

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: - *Instant history sync*: each open page keeps one event connection to the Spark (/api/profile/convos/stream, at most 8 per profile, renewed after 30 minutes). When a conversation changes on another device, the page fetches it at once; a deleted conversation closes. While another device answers in the open conversation, a pale "Phone is answering …" shows (only the kind of device, never the question). The live view shows only the number of these connections. - *One conversation for all channels*: Telegram, Siri, the companion, the watch and the own voice at a speaker write into today's main conversation (the newest of today that belongs to no channel alone; else "Heute DD.MM."), each message marked with its channel (white like the text in the own, blue bubble, V01.0.534). More context, but also more foreign context. A voice that is not surely the owner's stays in the speaker's conversation. - *Read history offline*: only a browser the profile trusts at the second sign-in step keeps a copy of the last 30 conversations and the page itself. Without a connection to the Spark the panel opens it for reading; questions without a connection (at most 10) go out once the Spark answers again.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: Every other browser stores nothing and deletes what it had the next time it opens; signing out always deletes.

head: The panel
title: The panel
text: Always, without a switch: what stood under an answer (sources, document passages, created documents) is kept with it and shows again on every device. The iPhone app fetches what is new when opened and during a conversation (needs a new TestFlight build).

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: Every function of the Spark with its switch, what it builds on, where you set it up and what it does (the first sentence of its guide under Features → Guides). hilfe.py --docs writes this list from features.py and the guides, so a new function stands here and in the help by itself.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Web search (Features → Conversation → "Web search"): When a question needs current information (news, opening hours, prices), the assistant searches the web itself and answers from the results.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Faster web search (Features → Conversation → "Faster web search"; builds on "Web search"): The web search no longer waits for the slowest page: each page gets at most 3 seconds, what is not there by then stays the short snippet from the result list.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Wikipedia straight away (Features → Conversation → "Wikipedia straight away"; Me → Conversation): For knowledge questions the Spark fetches the intro of the matching Wikipedia article and gives only that to the language model.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Own Kiwix archive (Features → Conversation → "Own Kiwix archive"; Me → Conversation): The Spark looks things up in your own kiwix-serve: knowledge questions first in its Wikipedia books, "Look in my archive …" in the full text of all chosen books, "Tell me more" reads up to three parts of an article.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Look locally first (Features → Conversation → "Look locally first"; Me → Conversation): For knowledge questions the Spark itself first looks in your documents (shared ones too), the Kiwix archive and earlier conversations, all at once, for at most 0.4 seconds (the Kiwix archive up to 0.9 seconds; per question it asks the Ge …

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Roles by voice (Features → Conversation → "Roles by voice"; Me → Conversation): You save up to 8 roles, such as "Butler" or "Explainer", and switch by voice.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Own conversation style (Features → Conversation → "Own conversation style"; Me → Conversation): Each profile says in its own words how the assistant should talk to it: form of address, tone, form, e.g.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Follow-up without wake word (Features → Conversation → "Follow-up without wake word"; Me → Conversation): After answering a spoken question the assistant keeps listening for a few seconds, so "And tomorrow?" or "Make it brighter" works without another "Hey Spark".

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Ignore my own voice (Features → Conversation → "Ignore my own voice"; Me → Conversation): Every device only filters its own echo.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Barge-in: pause first (Features → Conversation → "Barge-in: pause first"; Me → Conversation): Without this switch a quarter of a second of voice ends the answer, a cough or a "mhm" too.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Turn end by tone (Features → Conversation → "Turn end by tone"; Me → Conversation): Today a word list decides whether your sentence is finished: when it ends on "and", "because" or "um", the assistant waits longer.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Learning from corrections (Features → Conversation → "Learning from corrections"; builds on "Memory"; Me → Conversation): If you correct the assistant ("No, my brother is called Tim", "You should always check the calendar for appointments"), it turns this into a short sentence and asks: "Shall I remember …?" It is stored only after your "yes", in your memory.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Ask instead of guessing (Features → Conversation → "Ask instead of guessing"; Me → Conversation): If a command fits several devices ("Turn on the TV in the living room", with a TV and an Apple TV box there), the assistant does not guess: it asks "Which one do you mean?" and shows the fitting devices as buttons.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Remember the choice (Features → Conversation → "Remember the choice"; builds on "Ask instead of guessing"; Me → Conversation): After your choice the assistant asks: "Shall I remember that ‘TV in the living room’ is the Samsung?" After "yes" the same sentence switches that device straight away.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Show steps and approvals (Features → Conversation → "Show steps and approvals"): Below every answer a folded line shows which tools the assistant used, e.g.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Picture recognition (Features → Conversation → "Picture recognition"; Me → Conversation): You attach a photo and ask about it: "What plant is this?", "What does the sign say?", "What does the error message mean?".

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Exact calculations (Features → Conversation → "Exact calculations"): A language model is bad at arithmetic.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Help with the Spark (Features → Conversation → "Help with the Spark"; Me → Conversation): When you ask the assistant about the Spark itself ("What does targeted tool choice do?", "Where do I set the voice?"), it looks in the Spark's guides, switches and docs and answers from them, with the path in the panel and whether it is …

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Suggesting settings (Features → Conversation → "Suggesting settings"; builds on "Help with the Spark"; Me → Conversation): When a setting fits your question, the assistant shows a card below the answer: which switches, before and after.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Ask Spark on every page (Features → Conversation → "Ask Spark on every page"; builds on "Help with the Spark"; Me → Conversation): The face at the bottom right is the assistant on every page.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Suggesting functions (Features → Conversation → "Suggesting functions"; builds on "Help with the Spark"; Me → Conversation): When you ask for something that is still off for you ("What is on my calendar today?" with the calendar off), the assistant says so plainly and shows "Set up" below.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - You can also say (Features → Conversation → "You can also say"; builds on "Suggesting functions"; Me → What I can do): The assistant shows functions that are on for you but that you never used, each with a sentence you can say as it stands.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Tips while talking (Features → Conversation → "Tips while talking"; builds on "You can also say"; Me → Conversation): At a speaker, on the phone, in the car and at the watch there are no buttons.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Priority for people (Features → Conversation → "Priority for people"): When several people talk to the Spark at once, chosen profiles get their answer first.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Note when a service is missing (Features → Conversation → "Note when a service is missing"; builds on "Service watch"; Me → Conversation): When the service watch sees a service gone, the assistant says so at once when somebody needs it, e.g.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Instant history sync (Features → Conversation → "Instant history sync"; Me → Conversation): What you ask on one device shows up at once in the open panel on your other devices, without reloading; a deleted conversation disappears there at once.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - One conversation for all channels (Features → Conversation → "One conversation for all channels"; Me → Conversation): Telegram, Siri, the companion, the watch and your voice at a speaker write into today's main conversation instead of their own conversation per day.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Read history offline (Features → Conversation → "Read history offline"; Me → Conversation): A browser you trust at the second sign-in step ("trust this browser") keeps a copy of your last 30 conversations.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Settings assistant (Features → Conversation → "Settings assistant"): Whatever goes wrong becomes a case: a tool fails, an error, a question no rule recognizes that ends in the web search, a refusal ("I cannot"), the same question twice, a 👎 or "Wrongly sorted" on the Weiche.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Explain requests (Features → Conversation → "Explain requests"; builds on "Settings assistant"): Under Status → Logs → Requests a button explains a request in fixed sentences: which intent the Weiche saw, which tools ran, where it got stuck.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Ask the assistant for proposals (Features → Conversation → "Ask the assistant for proposals"; builds on "Settings assistant"; Me → Conversation): Admin profiles ask "What does the settings assistant propose?" and hear the open proposals.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Note on a new proposal (Features → Conversation → "Note on a new proposal"; builds on "Settings assistant"; Me → Conversation): When a new proposal comes, admin profiles get a short note with its title, at most three a day.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Prepare cases as reports (Features → Conversation → "Prepare cases as reports"; builds on "Settings assistant"): When nothing from the catalog helps, the case becomes a draft under Reporting problems, with fixed sentences and a preview before sending.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Autopilot for small changes (Features → Conversation → "Autopilot for small changes"; builds on "Settings assistant"): He takes stage A and B with a green test bench and at least two reports himself: one a day, at most three steps, back when it gets worse.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Ideas outside the catalog (Features → Conversation → "Ideas outside the catalog"; builds on "Settings assistant"): When the fixed catalog has nothing for a case, the local language model writes an idea: text, at most one setting with a jump link and steps to copy.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Analyse a case (Features → Conversation → "Analyse a case"; builds on "Settings assistant"): The local language model reads a case and picks a rule from fixed templates: must word, tool hint, extra tool for a group, word or test sentence for the Weiche.

head: All functions
title: All functions
