text: - Undo automatically (Features → Conversation → "Undo automatically"; builds on "Settings assistant"): The re-check looks at every taken change after its waiting time: when the case came back, a test sentence turned red or the 👍 share of its group fell by at least 15 points (from 10 ratings before and after), the result is "worse".

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Steps for the environment (Features → Conversation → "Steps for the environment"; builds on "Settings assistant"): When a service outside the Spark is the cause (search, wiki, NAS, network), the proposal shows steps to copy.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Proposals for my profile (Features → Conversation → "Proposals for my profile"; builds on "Settings assistant"; Me → Conversation): A profile's own 👎 lead to proposals for its settings, e.g.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - 👍/👎 under answers (Features → Conversation → "👍/👎 under answers"; builds on "Settings assistant"; Me → Conversation): Under every answer 👍 or 👎.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - "Why?" for every profile (Features → Conversation → ""Why?" for every profile"; builds on "Settings assistant"; Me → Conversation): When you ask "Why did you just search the web?" or "Why didn't you look it up?", the Spark explains the way of its last answer: how it understood the question and where it looked, in fixed plain sentences, without rules, tool names or se …

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Spark diary (Features → Conversation → "Spark diary"; Me → Conversation): The Spark notes what it did for you itself: devices switched, reminders set, mail drafts saved, documents made, files put on the reMarkable, messages sent.

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Status by voice (Features → Conversation → "Status by voice"): When you ask "Is everything running?", "Is Home Assistant reachable?", "When was the last backup?", "Is there an update?", "Is the emergency stop on?" or "Is my mailbox connected?", the Spark reads its own state and answers only from it …

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Undo by voice (Features → Conversation → "Undo by voice"): When you say "Undo that", the Spark proposes to take back its last deed for you: delete a reminder, remove a list entry, forget a note, take an appointment out again, switch a device back, set the volume back, the pause of notes, restore …

head: All functions
title: All functions
text: - Feedback when it is fixed (Features → Conversation → "Feedback when it is fixed"; builds on "👍/👎 under answers"; Me → Conversation): When a change helps after your 👎, the assistant tells you once.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Thinking while choosing tools (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Thinking while choosing tools"; Me → Conversation): The model thinks briefly before it picks a tool (calendar, mail, web search …).

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Targeted tool choice (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Targeted tool choice"; Me → Conversation): Fixed rules in the panel recognize from your own words what it is about (smart home, appointment, mail, web search, reminder, list, weather …).

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Fetch clear questions directly (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Fetch clear questions directly"; Me → Conversation): For short, clear questions the panel calls the matching tool itself, by fixed rules: "Do I have new mail?" (mail list), "Which reminders do I have?", "What is the weather like?" (today, at home), "Where is my parcel?" and "Which appointm …

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Names for listening (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Names for listening"): The speech recognition gets a short list of names with every recording: all profiles, the profile's contacts and the rooms and devices from its Home Assistant.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Answer simple things at once (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Answer simple things at once"): The panel answers a few simple questions itself with a fixed sentence, without the language model: the time ("What time is it?"), the date and weekday ("What day is it today?"), calculations with brackets, percent and roots ("What is 17 …

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Trim a large memory (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Trim a large memory"): When the Spark has remembered a lot for a profile (more than about 6000 characters), the language model only gets the newest facts as a fixed part plus at most five older ones that share words with the question.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Instant acknowledgement (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Instant acknowledgement"; builds on "Targeted tool choice"; Me → Conversation): Right after your question the Spark says in a short sentence what it is doing now, for example "Let me check your calendar." or "Let me search the web.".

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Tune the switch (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Tune the switch"; builds on "Targeted tool choice"): On Features → Routing, "Tune" starts a run: the language model proposes up to 6 words for groups that everyday sentences often miss.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Keep unclear questions anonymously (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Keep unclear questions anonymously"; builds on "Targeted tool choice"; Me → Conversation): Questions no rule of the switch recognizes are listed on Features → Routing under "unclear": without names, numbers, addresses and codes, never with profile, device or time.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Fetch ahead on a question back (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Fetch ahead on a question back"; builds on "Targeted tool choice"; Me → Conversation): When an answer ends with a question back ("For which day?"), the panel already fetches what the next answer will most likely need: the calendar of the next days, the newest mails, the weather at home or parcels.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Classification with probabilities (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Classification with probabilities"; Me → Conversation): The language model on the Spark answers fixed questions of the panel with probabilities instead of text (/v1/systemone of the LLM-Tor or of qwen38).

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Classification when tidying the inbox (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Classification when tidying the inbox"; builds on "Classification with probabilities"; Me → Conversation): Mails no fixed rule sorts while tidying get their category with a real probability.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Classification in the quality test (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Classification in the quality test"; builds on "Classification with probabilities"): The quality test (Status → Checks) gets a second opinion per question: how well the answer answers it (0 to 2) and how likely it makes something up.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Classification in the settings assistant (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Classification in the settings assistant"; builds on "Classification with probabilities"): The settings assistant picks the fitting proposal for a case from its fixed catalog.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Check answers in the background (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Check answers in the background"; builds on "Classification with probabilities"; Me → Conversation): After an answer for which tools ran, the panel asks in the background whether the answer names details that are in no result.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Recognize complaints (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Recognize complaints"; builds on "Classification with probabilities"; Me → Conversation): When somebody says "still does not work" or "it is still on" right after a deed, the panel recognizes it from a fixed word list, otherwise with the classification from 80 %.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model"): A small, fast language model (Qwen3 4B) on the model computer takes simple work off the big language model: fixed questions with a fixed answer list (classification) for routing, the Dungeon Master and mail.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model for routing (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model for routing"; builds on "Helper model"): Questions no fixed rule of the switch recognizes are sorted into a tool group by the helper model first, also when measuring the threshold.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model for the Dungeon Master (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model for the Dungeon Master"; builds on "Helper model"): The dungeon judge (after every turn: must the narration be rewritten?) and the classification in the narrator test bench ask the helper model first.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model for mail (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model for mail"; builds on "Helper model"): Sorting mail when tidying the inbox and recognizing important mail ask the helper model first.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model spots attacks (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model spots attacks"; builds on "Helper model"): After an answer for which a tool read outside text (web, mail, document, calendar), the panel asks the helper model in the background whether that text held an order to the assistant.

head: Speed and accuracy
title: Speed and accuracy
text: - Helper model for short texts (Features → Speed and accuracy → "Helper model for short texts"; builds on "Helper model"): Short texts in the background are written by the helper model first: the topics of remembered facts in the memory as well as reply suggestions and follow-ups on the watch.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Memory (Features → My data → "Memory"; Me → Memory): The assistant remembers things about you, such as names, preferences or where something is, and uses them later.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Memory check (Features → My data → "Memory check"; builds on "Memory"; Me → Memory): Every entry in the memory keeps where it came from (from you in a conversation, from a correction, learned automatically, changed here), which conversation and when you last confirmed it.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Memory check-back (Features → My data → "Memory check-back"; builds on "Memory check"; Me → Conversation): When an entry the check marked as maybe out of date fits your question, the Spark asks once after the answer: "Quick check: is this still right: …?" Whether and when, the panel decides with fixed rules, never the language model.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Memory topics (Features → My data → "Memory topics"; builds on "Memory check"; Me → Memory): Under Me → Memory the entries are in groups: person, home, on the move, work, health, right now, other.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Past conversations (Features → My data → "Past conversations"; Me → Conversation): You can ask about past conversations.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Own documents (Features → My data → "Own documents"; Me → Documents): You upload documents, the assistant searches them when a question fits.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Read pictures and scans (Features → My data → "Read pictures and scans"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): Photos (invoice, rating plate, whiteboard) and PDF pages without text go into your documents.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Meaning search (Features → My data → "Meaning search"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): The document search finds not only the same words but also passages with a similar meaning: "car insurance" finds "motor liability", "when do I have to cancel" finds "notice period".

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Keep originals (Features → My data → "Keep originals"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): The uploaded file stays on the Spark (photos made smaller, without location or camera data).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Read long documents at night (Features → My data → "Read long documents at night"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): By day the Spark reads only short documents (up to 10 pages) in quiet moments.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Shared documents (Features → My data → "Shared documents"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): A profile shares single documents with "For everyone", for example manuals.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Sharing with profiles (Features → My data → "Sharing with profiles"; Me → Shared): A profile shares a document with single other profiles, for example the lease with the partner.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Note on shared things (Features → My data → "Note on shared things"; builds on "Sharing with profiles"; Me → Shared): When someone shares something with you, a note comes to the device you use right now: "Anna shared something with you", without the title.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Docling server (Features → My data → "Docling server"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): A Docling server in your own network reads uploaded PDF, Word, PowerPoint and Excel files and scans a second time, in quiet moments.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - reMarkable notes (Features → My data → "reMarkable notes"; builds on "Read pictures and scans"; Me → reMarkable): You connect your my.remarkable account.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Sending to the reMarkable (Features → My data → "Sending to the reMarkable"; builds on "reMarkable notes"; Me → reMarkable): Below every answer there is "To the reMarkable"; a click puts it as a new document into the folder "Spark".

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Newest first (Features → My data → "Newest first"; builds on "reMarkable notes"; Me → reMarkable): With similar hits in your documents and reMarkable notes the assistant takes the newer one and names its date.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Morning sheet (Features → My data → "Morning sheet"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - @Spark on paper (Features → My data → "@Spark on paper"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Tasks from the reMarkable (Features → My data → "Tasks from the reMarkable"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Meeting summaries (Features → My data → "Meeting summaries"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Week in review (Features → My data → "Week in review"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Web pages and attachments to the reMarkable (Features → My data → "Web pages and attachments to the reMarkable"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Daily inbox (Features → My data → "Daily inbox"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Spark guide on the reMarkable (Features → My data → "Spark guide on the reMarkable"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): A morning sheet with appointments and lines for notes, answers to "@Spark" questions on paper, tasks from handwriting, meeting summaries, a week in review, web pages and mail attachments, one inbox per day and a Spark guide that keeps it …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Designed sheets to tick (Features → My data → "Designed sheets to tick"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): What the Spark puts on the reMarkable comes as a designed sheet exactly in your device’s format (reMarkable 1 and 2, Paper Pro, Paper Pro Move), with "Kann weg" at the top right: tick it and the Spark puts it into the trash.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Folders by kind (Features → My data → "Folders by kind"; builds on "Sending to the reMarkable"; Me → reMarkable): What the Spark puts on the reMarkable comes as a designed sheet exactly in your device’s format (reMarkable 1 and 2, Paper Pro, Paper Pro Move), with "Kann weg" at the top right: tick it and the Spark puts it into the trash.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Tidy up by itself (Features → My data → "Tidy up by itself"; builds on "Folders by kind"; Me → reMarkable): What the Spark puts on the reMarkable comes as a designed sheet exactly in your device’s format (reMarkable 1 and 2, Paper Pro, Paper Pro Move), with "Kann weg" at the top right: tick it and the Spark puts it into the trash.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Task sheet to tick (Features → My data → "Task sheet to tick"; builds on "Designed sheets to tick"; Me → reMarkable): A living sheet in the folder "Aufgaben" with what is open: tasks from your notes (remind, remove, later), memory entries that may no longer be true (true, not true) and proposals for your settings.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Creating documents (Features → My data → "Creating documents"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): On request the Spark writes a letter, report, minutes, a note, invitation, presentation or spreadsheet and puts the file under Me → Documents (Word, PDF, PowerPoint, Excel, Markdown, text or CSV).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Own templates (Features → My data → "Own templates"; builds on "Creating documents"; Me → Documents): Profiles upload own Word or PowerPoint templates (.docx, .dotx, .pptx, .potx).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Pictures from the Kiwix (Features → My data → "Pictures from the Kiwix"; builds on "Creating documents"; Me → Documents): For the title slide and "Picture and text" slides the Spark fetches a fitting picture from the Wikipedia in your own Kiwix.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Painting pictures (Features → My data → "Painting pictures"; Me → Pictures): On request the Spark paints a picture, a drawing, a logo or a colouring page, itself and without the internet, with FLUX.2 [klein] by Black Forest Labs.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Changing pictures (Features → My data → "Changing pictures"; builds on "Painting pictures"; Me → Pictures): The Spark changes an own photo or a painted picture after your sentence, itself and without the internet, with the same FLUX.2 [klein] as for painting: sky blue, as a watercolour, add or remove a thing.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Making music (Features → My data → "Making music"; Me → Music): The Spark makes a song or piece of music on request, itself and without the internet, with ACE-Step 1.5 on the model computer.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Editing music (Features → My data → "Editing music"; builds on "Making music"; Me → Music): The Spark edits a song under Me → Music, itself and without the internet, with the same ACE-Step as for making: make a section new, extend at the front or back, change the music style (rock, jazz, reggae, …, you decide how close to the o …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - AI Dungeon Master (Features → My data → "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): A role-playing game for up to five players: under Dungeon Master (its own menu entry) you start a round, pick world, tone (from 8, 12 or 16) and turn time and invite by seat link or QR code, also people without a profile.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Pictures for gear and spells (Features → My data → "Pictures for gear and spells"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every item and spell of the Dungeon Master gets a painted picture instead of only a sign: weapons, armour, jewellery, potions, spells, scrolls and tools, peoples, classes, abilities and foes too, your own catalog entries too, per world i …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Guests with e-mail (Features → My data → "Guests with e-mail"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Guests at the Dungeon Master's table can keep their heroes: they type their e-mail address, get a 6-digit code (valid 10 minutes) and with it a guest account with up to 8 heroes, also on another device.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Balance bench (Features → My data → "Balance bench"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The Spark plays fights of the AI Dungeon Master by itself, with the real rules and dice and the catalog including your own rules, without the language model: per level 1 to 10 and group size 1 to 5, 200 fights of danger "medium" each.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Narrator bench (Features → My data → "Narrator bench"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The admin plays eight fixed scenes through the running language model, with the same rules as at the table: a failed check, two heroes, a fight with dice receipts, the children's tone, a person by name, an English round, a risky and a ha …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Fix narrator errors (Features → My data → "Fix narrator errors"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): After a 👎 on the last narration a seat picks a fixed reason (for example "Action misunderstood" or "Wrong place").

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Dungeon judge (Features → My data → "Dungeon judge"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): After every turn the Spark first checks the narration with fixed rules.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Critical and fumble tables (Features → My data → "Critical and fumble tables"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a hero hits critically, the Spark rolls a d12 on the table of the kind of damage (slashing, piercing, bludgeoning, fire and the others): a fixed line such as "Tendon struck: the target limps", sometimes with a state for one to three …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Honours of the evening (Features → My data → "Honours of the evening"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a round ends (also with a chapter), the Spark gives fixed titles: Blade of the evening (most damage), Rescuer (most help for friends), Lucky one (most 20s), Quietest shadow (most Dexterity checks passed) and Hard-luck hero (from thr …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Near miss (Features → My data → "Near miss"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a check misses by only 1 or 2 (never on a 1 and never on attacks), the Spark asks the hero: give up, or make it after all and pay a price?

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Helping and group checks (Features → My data → "Helping and group checks"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a player writes in their action that they help another hero and names them ("I help Mara over the wall"), the Spark rolls Mara's first check of this turn with advantage (two d20, the higher counts).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Writings (Features → My data → "Writings"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When the heroes find something written in the story (a letter, a wanted poster, a verse, a diary page, a note, an inscription), it appears at the table as parchment with title, text (at most 600 characters) and sender and stays in the ta …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Heroes comment (Features → My data → "Heroes comment"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The narrator gives every hero who acted this turn a short line of its own: how it comments on its deed or the outcome, a feeling, a quip.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Campfire and rest (Features → My data → "Campfire and rest"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Outside a fight the host calls a rest in the game master console.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Travel stages (Features → My data → "Travel stages"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When the map leads the group along a way of two or more stages (not in a vault), it becomes a journey.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Tongues of the peoples (Features → My data → "Tongues of the peoples"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a person of the story briefly greets or cries out in the tongue of its people, the Spark turns it into foreign sounds from that people's name syllables; the same sentence always sounds the same.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Calendar of the world (Features → My data → "Calendar of the world"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every world has twelve months of 30 days, one or two moons and festivals.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Time of day by the panel (Features → My data → "Time of day by the panel"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The Spark sets the time of day by fixed rules, never the model: one half day of the world is morning and day, the next evening and night, 6 told turns each.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Guide the players (Features → My data → "Guide the players"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The narrator gets a fixed form: first what the deeds cause, then what is to be seen now, and in every narration at least two things to take up, with names (a person, a thing, a way).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Story progress (Features → My data → "Story progress"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The Spark counts by fixed rules whether the story moves on: a new place, a thread opened or closed, a new thing, an act done, a fight begun or ended, a clue shown.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Witness rule (Features → My data → "Witness rule"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): What a hero does in front of people of the scene changes their attitude by a fixed table, not by the model: attacking or robbing someone lowers the victim's attitude by two steps and that of everyone else present by one.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Read thoughts (Features → My data → "Read thoughts"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a hero casts the spell "Read thoughts" or still has its blessing or that of the "Potion of mind reading" and the action wants to hear the thoughts of a person of the scene, the panel rolls an Intelligence check instead of the model.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Persuade to come along (Features → My data → "Persuade to come along"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a hero asks a person of the map to come along, the panel decides, not the model: if the person is not at the group's place or at most neutral towards the hero, it stays.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Errands from people (Features → My data → "Errands from people"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a hero asks a person of the scene for work, the panel rolls an errand from fixed tables: bring something (a potion or a tool of the market), talk with another person or defeat a foe of the world, plus a reward in gold (times the gro …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Wandering people (Features → My data → "Wandering people"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When the group takes a long rest, the panel rolls for every person of the map not travelling with the group: with half a chance they move one way on towards their goal.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Small gestures (Features → My data → "Small gestures"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): While the round waits, a person of the scene with a strong trait shows a small gesture from a fixed list: a kind one nods, a hot-headed one drums its fingers, a fearful one glances at the door.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Chronicle book (Features → My data → "Chronicle book"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When the host closes a chapter, the Spark writes a page into the campaign's book: cover, the story so far, the heroes with people, class, level and scars, the honours of the evening, the writings for everyone and the places of the map.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Hero book to the reMarkable (Features → My data → "Hero book to the reMarkable"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): One book per hero on the reMarkable in the style of an old grimoire: contents with tabs to tap, hero sheet (values, life, armour, gold, load, gear, abilities, scars), chronicle of encounters (evenings, chapters, fights, people, levels; f …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Use the surroundings (Features → My data → "Use the surroundings"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Where a fight goes on, two to three things lie in the room or place, such as a chandelier, a powder keg, a thick pillar or a rope over the chasm.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - People catalog (Features → My data → "People catalog"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every person the group met in a round goes into the catalog when the round ends: card (looks, manner, occupation, wish, secret), traits, role, goal, voice, face and how it stands towards each hero.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Hire companions (Features → My data → "Hire companions"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): In a settlement a hero hires a companion of its world, at the children's table an animal friend: only while fewer than four heroes play, at most two, until the group counts four.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Heart's wish (Features → My data → "Heart's wish"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every hero may carry a heart's wish: one of its world's list or in own words, at most 160 characters.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Alarm and torches (Features → My data → "Alarm and torches"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): In a vault the Spark counts noise from 0 to 6: a fight, a door, a fumbled sneak or a sprung trap bring the vault closer to the alarm.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Whisper to a person (Features → My data → "Whisper to a person"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Once a turn a player whispers something to a person of the scene, such as the innkeeper who just spoke.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Foe announcements and stance (Features → My data → "Foe announcements and stance"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): After every fought turn each foe announces its next blow: it takes aim at a hero (+2 to hit), winds up (−2 to hit, double damage dice on a hit) or waits for an opening (with advantage).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Ask back on unclear actions (Features → My data → "Ask back on unclear actions"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a player sends an action that is too short ("ok"), unreadable ("asdf"), only names a pronoun while several things fit ("take it"), or holds no verb and no name of the scene (a sentence like "I search the chest" or "We rest" is clear …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Own stories (Features → My data → "Own stories"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every story card when you start a round has "⋯": Edit (title, idea, tone, acts in the story planner's form), Copy and Delete.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Scars (Features → My data → "Scars"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a hero stands up again after lying down or a foe hits it critically, the Spark rolls on a fixed d20 wound table: mostly only a scar (the look), rarely a mild consequence, −1 on a value, until a healer in a settlement takes it for gold.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Scars only (Features → My data → "Scars only"; builds on "Scars"; Dungeon Master → Settings): For "Scars": wounds then only change a hero's look, never a value.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Monster album (Features → My data → "Monster album"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every hero collects the foes its group defeated in the tab "Album" of the right column.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Adventure import (Features → My data → "Adventure import"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): A written adventure (PDF, Word, OpenDocument, Markdown, text or HTML, up to 10 MB) becomes a draft in the story planner: the panel reads the headings with the start of every chapter, the language model joins the chapters in order into 3 …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Game master dial (Features → My data → "Game master dial"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Like a good game master the Spark notices when a group only wins or keeps lying on the floor.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Heroic courage (Features → My data → "Heroic courage"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Once a game evening every hero may rise above themselves: tap "⭐ Heroic courage" before "Act".

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Lines and X-card (Features → My data → "Lines and X-card"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Everyone at the table sets what never appears in the game (lines) and what is only hinted at (veils), up to 8 short words each.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Scribe check (Features → My data → "Scribe check"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Sometimes the Dungeon Master tells that a hero finds gold or picks a thing up from the ground, and does not count it.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Random rules (Features → My data → "Random rules"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): As host you give your round up to 5 rules of your own: for example "Rockfall: every turn 10 %, 2 damage for all" or "Pickpocket: at a new place 20 % per hero, 5 gold lost".

head: My data
title: My data
text: - NPC memory and chronicle (Features → My data → "NPC memory and chronicle"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every person of the story gets a card the panel rolls from fixed tables: looks, manner, occupation, wish and secret.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Faces for NPCs (Features → My data → "Faces for NPCs"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Every person of the story you meet gets a portrait once.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Arms for group and factions (Features → My data → "Arms for group and factions"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Your group gets a coat of arms, every faction of the story its own.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Oracle (Features → My data → "Oracle"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): As host, also alone at the table, you ask the oracle: a yes-or-no question from "Certain" to "Hardly" or up to 3 tables like action and theme, place, twist, complication.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Factions with clocks (Features → My data → "Factions with clocks"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): The story's groups (guilds, gangs, orders …) pursue their goal, also without the heroes.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Quest items (Features → My data → "Quest items"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Special things of the story (a key, a map, a seal) with their own sign ✦: they weigh nothing, cannot be sold and pass from hero to hero.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Combat stages (Features → My data → "Combat stages"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): As host you choose how hard the next encounters are: easy, medium, hard or deadly.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Gold with a purpose (Features → My data → "Gold with a purpose"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Gold gets a purpose: in a settlement (village, town, tavern, harbour, bazaar, station of the map) or at a merchant there are fixed offers.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Real dice at the table (Features → My data → "Real dice at the table"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Whoever sits at the real table throws their own d20.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Bard's hero song (Features → My data → "Bard's hero song"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): When a chapter ends, the Spark sings a short song of 60 to 90 seconds about the round's heroes, in German, in the sound of the world (lute in fantasy, accordion with pirates).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Runes and sockets (Features → My data → "Runes and sockets"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): Like Diablo 2: some weapons and armour up to "rare" come from a find with sockets (weapon 2 or 3, body 3, shield and head 2, hands and feet 1).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Game master gives things (Features → My data → "Game master gives things"; builds on "AI Dungeon Master"; Dungeon Master → Settings): As admin and host of a round you give a hero at the table something from the catalog: an item up to "epic" (potions, arrows and spells too, up to 5 pieces), gold (up to 1000 at once), runes (up to 5, only with "Runes and sockets") or exp …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Document card and tags (Features → My data → "Document card and tags"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): In quiet minutes (or at night) the language model reads the beginning of each document once and notes a card: title, kind, sender, date, deadline, number and 3 to 6 keywords.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Search check (Features → My data → "Search check"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): Test questions with a known right place show how often the search in your documents finds the right thing.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Re-rank hits (Features → My data → "Re-rank hits"; builds on "Own documents"; Me → Documents): The document search mixes word search and meaning search and so finds 30 candidates.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Knowledge book (Features → My data → "Knowledge book"; builds on "Own documents"; Knowledge book → Settings): The Spark works each of your documents once into pages, such as "Car", "Insurance" or "Garage Müller", and writes short sentences there, each with its source.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Knowledge map (Features → My data → "Knowledge map"; builds on "Knowledge book"; Knowledge book → Settings): The pages of your knowledge book become points on a map, and the Spark connects them: "Golf insured with Nordstern", "parking damage raises the premium, +18 %".

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Test questions by the Spark (Features → My data → "Test questions by the Spark"; builds on "Search check"; Me → Documents): So the search check has enough questions, the language model writes, in quiet minutes, a question about a random place in your documents that only this place answers, in its own words.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Storage and NAS (Features → My data → "Storage and NAS"; Me → Storage): Under Me → Storage you connect every place once: your NAS (Synology, QNAP, Fritzbox), a cloud with WebDAV (Nextcloud, ownCloud, HiDrive, MagentaCLOUD) or an SFTP server.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Copy of my data (Features → My data → "Copy of my data"; builds on "Storage and NAS"; Me → Storage): An encrypted copy of your data at one of your places (NAS, cloud with WebDAV, SFTP, SMB share at home) or in a folder the admin mounted on the Spark (NFS, SMB, USB disk).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Knowledge folders (Features → My data → "Knowledge folders"; builds on "Storage and NAS"; Me → Storage): You pick folders on your NAS or cloud, e.g.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Household folder (Features → My data → "Household folder"; builds on "Knowledge folders"; Me → Storage): A folder on the NAS for everyone in the household, e.g.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Filing folder (Features → My data → "Filing folder"; builds on "Storage and NAS"; Me → Storage): A folder "spark_ablage" on your NAS at home is the only place the Spark writes to.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - NAS status (Features → My data → "NAS status"; builds on "Storage and NAS"): Every few minutes the Spark reads how your NAS is doing: use of the volumes, how much of the storage pool is given to volumes (that is not "full"), USB disks on the NAS, RAID, state and temperature of the disks, system temperature, fans, …

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Storage in the home network (Features → My data → "Storage in the home network"; builds on "Copy of my data"; Me → Storage): Profiles may use places with addresses in the home network for their copy (NAS, Fritzbox, Nextcloud at home).

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Folder on the Spark (Features → My data → "Folder on the Spark"; builds on "Copy of my data"; Me → Storage): Profiles put their copy in a subfolder of a folder you mounted on the Spark, e.g.

head: My data
title: My data
text: - Move originals out (Features → My data → "Move originals out"; builds on "Copy of my data"; Me → Storage): Originals of documents neither changed nor opened for 30 days live only in the copy at your place; that saves space on the Spark.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Suggesting functions by itself (Features → My day → "Suggesting functions by itself"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): At most once a week a suggestion arrives under "By itself" as a notification, e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Speaking up by itself (Features → My day → "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): The assistant speaks up when something is really up: before appointments, on your own smart-home rules, mails from chosen senders, tomorrow's weather, birthdays, parcels, a follow-up or a greeting.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Instant notes from Home Assistant (Features → My day → "Instant notes from Home Assistant"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): Your smart home rules listen to Home Assistant directly instead of looking once a minute.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - House notes on speakers (Features → My day → "House notes on speakers"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): A rule or an event from Home Assistant also says its own sentence aloud on chosen speakers, e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Home Assistant tells the Spark (Features → My day → "Home Assistant tells the Spark"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): Home Assistant sends the Spark an event, e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Smart home rule by voice (Features → My day → "Smart home rule by voice"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): "Tell me when someone is at the front door" or "Let me know when Anna comes home": the Spark finds the device, names the rule and adds it after your "yes".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Recognize important mail (Features → My day → "Recognize important mail"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; E-mail → Settings): Speaking up by itself otherwise only names new mail from senders on your list.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Describe a camera picture (Features → My day → "Describe a camera picture"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): When a rule applies, the Spark fetches a still picture of a camera from Home Assistant and lets the local language model say in a few words what is seen, e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Timers and reminders (Features → My day → "Timers and reminders"): Timers and reminders by voice.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Notes to the device in use (Features → My day → "Notes to the device in use"; builds on "Timers and reminders"): A note (reminder, by itself, job, service watch …) goes to the device you are using right now: the open page you typed or clicked on in the last two minutes, the iPhone or Android app in front, or the Spark companion on the computer you …

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Everything open in the assistant (Features → My day → "Everything open in the assistant"; builds on "Timers and reminders"; Open → Settings): What needs you comes as a card with buttons into the day's conversation: urgent finds from "For you" (bill, contract, reply, suspicion) and reminders that rang.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Lists for shopping and tasks (Features → My day → "Lists for shopping and tasks"; Lists → Settings): The page Lists in the menu: shopping, tasks and your own lists (DIY store, holiday, …).

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Share lists (Features → My day → "Share lists"; builds on "Lists for shopping and tasks"; Lists → Settings): You share one of your lists with another profile: on the page Lists at the list "⋯" → "Share …" and per person "See" or "Write along" (put on and tick off).

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Note on new entries (Features → My day → "Note on new entries"; builds on "Share lists"; Lists → Settings): You share one of your lists with another profile: on the page Lists at the list "⋯" → "Share …" and per person "See" or "Write along" (put on and tick off).

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Lists in Reminders (Features → My day → "Lists in Reminders"; builds on "Lists for shopping and tasks"; Lists → Settings): Your lists on the Spark (shopping, tasks, own lists) show in the iPhone's Reminders app, through the same access as your Spark calendars.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Write link (Features → My day → "Write link"; builds on "Lists for shopping and tasks"; Lists → Settings): A link for people without a profile, such as visitors, grandparents or the cleaner: whoever opens it puts something on one of your lists, with a name if they like.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - My status (Features → My day → "My status"; Me → My status): Under Me → My status you see what the Spark does for you in the background: reading documents, meaning search, document cards, comparing the reMarkable, tidying the inbox, fetching contacts, jobs, the morning briefing, tidying memory.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Jobs (Features → My day → "Jobs"; Me → Jobs): The assistant works longer for you: "Research …, let me know" runs in the background (search, read pages, sum up), the result comes as a notification and is listed under Me → Jobs.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Watching (Features → My day → "Watching"; builds on "Jobs"; Me → Jobs): The Spark checks the web regularly for something new (firmware, a new episode, a price below a limit) and only then tells you.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Jobs with plan, questions and proposals (Features → My day → "Jobs with plan, questions and proposals"; builds on "Jobs"; Me → Jobs): A job writes its steps as a list and ticks them off; you see it live under Me → Jobs.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Services over MCP (Features → My day → "Services over MCP"; builds on "Jobs"): Tools of outside services that speak MCP (e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Own MCP services (Features → My day → "Own MCP services"; builds on "Services over MCP"; Me → My MCP services): Every profile connects its own MCP services (e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Own MCP services in jobs (Features → My day → "Own MCP services in jobs"; builds on "Own MCP services"; Me → My MCP services): Background jobs (agent functions) may use the reading tools of your own services, never the acting ones.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Own MCP services with sign-in (Features → My day → "Own MCP services with sign-in"; builds on "Own MCP services"; Me → My MCP services): Services that want a sign-in (OAuth) instead of a key: the Spark registers at the service as a program, you sign in there, the access stays encrypted on the Spark.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Chats (Features → My day → "Chats"; Me → Conversation): Writing like in a messenger, but on your Spark: "Chats" in the menu (on a phone the "Chats" tab), the list on the left, the chat on the right.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Message to everybody (Features → My day → "Message to everybody"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): The fixed group "Alle" (everybody) in the chats: who takes part is in it, without admins; "Tell everybody we leave at eight" writes into it after your "Yes".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Group chats (Features → My day → "Group chats"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): "＋ New chat" → "New group": a name, pick the people, done.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Photos, files and voice in chats (Features → My day → "Photos, files and voice in chats"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): In the chat left of the input field: 📎 sends a photo or a file (PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, text), 🎤 records a voice message (up to 5 minutes, with what was said underneath).

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Invite into a chat (Features → My day → "Invite into a chat"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): Chats → ＋ New chat → "Invite someone": a link and a QR code for a person who has no profile yet.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Private chats (end-to-end) (Features → My day → "Private chats (end-to-end)"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): Chats → ＋ New chat → "🔒 Private" beside a person: a chat for two that only your devices can read.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Chats with other Sparks (Features → My day → "Chats with other Sparks"; builds on "Chats"): Chats → ＋ New chat → "🌐 Someone on another Spark": your Spark address (e.g.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Photos and files to other Sparks (Features → My day → "Photos and files to other Sparks"; builds on "Chats with other Sparks"): In chats with people on other Sparks photos, files (PDF, Office, text up to 25 MB) and voice messages (up to 5 minutes) go too, with the same buttons as in any chat.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Groups with other Sparks (Features → My day → "Groups with other Sparks"; builds on "Chats with other Sparks"): People on other Sparks can join a group too: the group's admins pick their contacts marked 🌐 when creating it or under "Add people".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Calls (voice and video) (Features → My day → "Calls (voice and video)"; builds on "Chats"): In a chat for two, 📞 or 🎥 at the top: every open Chats page of the other person rings, their phone says "Name is calling".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Calls when away (Features → My day → "Calls when away"; builds on "Calls (voice and video)"): An own relay (TURN) on the Spark: when one of the devices is on a mobile network or behind someone else's router, sound and picture go through it.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Calls by the assistant (Features → My day → "Calls by the assistant"; builds on "Calls (voice and video)"): Say or write to the assistant: "Call Sabine", "Video call Sabine".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Calendar (Features → My day → "Calendar"; Calendar → Settings): The assistant reads your appointments and adds new ones, but only after your "Yes".

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Share calendars (Features → My day → "Share calendars"; builds on "Calendar"; Calendar → Settings): You share one of your calendars with another profile, "See" or "See + add": Calendar → Settings → "Share" on the calendar's card, find the person in the window.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Calendar server for calendar apps (Features → My day → "Calendar server for calendar apps"; builds on "Calendar"; Calendar → Settings): Your Spark calendars show in the iPhone's calendar (or in Thunderbird, DAVx5) and can be changed there: the Spark is a CalDAV server for them.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Weather (Features → My day → "Weather"; Me → Weather): The forecast for your place: now, today, tomorrow and up to 7 days, with rain in the next hours.

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Reddit and feeds (Features → My day → "Reddit and feeds"; Me → Reddit and feeds): The Spark reads your Reddit inbox, subreddits and other feeds (blogs, YouTube, Mastodon).

head: My day
title: My day
text: - Telling news from feeds (Features → My day → "Telling news from feeds"; builds on "Speaking up by itself"; Me → By itself): The Spark reads your Reddit inbox, subreddits and other feeds (blogs, YouTube, Mastodon).

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Reading e-mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): The assistant reads your inbox of the last 30 days.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Inbox tidying (Features → Mail and contacts → "Inbox tidying"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): Advertising, newsletters and the like go into their own folders (main folder of your choice, else "Spark").

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Order mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "Order mail"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): On the E-mail page you mark a mail read or unread, flag it with ★, archive it or move it into one of your folders, also several at once ("Select", then ticks, or ⌘/Ctrl-click).

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Send mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "Send mail"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): On the E-mail page you write a new mail, answer one or forward it (with its attachments if wanted).

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Delete mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "Delete mail"; builds on "Order mail"; E-mail → Settings): On the E-mail page you delete a mail with the trash symbol, the Delete key or by dragging it onto the trash, also several ticked ones at once.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Invitations from mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "Invitations from mail"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): If a mail carries an invitation (.ics), the E-mail page shows above its text what, when, where and who invites.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - New mail at once (Features → Mail and contacts → "New mail at once"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): New mail is on the E-mail page within a few seconds, not only at the next fetch every five minutes, and your mail rules sort it at once.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Confirmation codes (Features → Mail and contacts → "Confirmation codes"; builds on "New mail at once"; E-mail → Settings): When a mail with a confirmation code arrives ("482913 is your code"), the Spark shows the code at once as a note on the device you are using, with "Copy code".

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Learn mail style (Features → Mail and contacts → "Learn mail style"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): The Spark reads your sent mails and remembers how you write: form of address, greeting, sign-off, length, tone and typical phrases, split into Private, Work and Unknown.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Parcels (Features → Mail and contacts → "Parcels"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): From the shipping mails of DHL, Hermes, DPD, GLS, UPS and Amazon of the last 14 days: what comes today, what is on its way, what waits for pick-up and what was delivered.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - For you from mail (Features → Mail and contacts → "For you from mail"; builds on "Reading e-mail"; E-mail → Settings): The Spark looks through your mails of the last 30 days and shows what needs you or is good to know: bills with amount and deadline, contracts and subscriptions that renew (with the last day to cancel), orders, offers with an end date, qu …

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - What I know about you (Features → Mail and contacts → "What I know about you"; builds on "For you from mail"; Me → What I know about you): A page under Me that shows what the Spark knows about you and where from: interests as topics with evidence (for example "Smart home & IoT" from newsletters about ESP32 and Zigbee, with the senders and up to three subjects) that count on …

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Writing help (Features → Mail and contacts → "Writing help"; Me → Writing help): Paste a text and pick what should happen: correct (only mistakes), smooth, shorter, friendlier, more formal, translate, or draft a reply to a mail you received.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Writing help in other programs (Features → Mail and contacts → "Writing help in other programs"; builds on "Writing help"; Me → Writing help): The writing help right where you write: Mac quick action (right-click → Services → "Mit Spark verbessern", in Apple Mail, Pages, Word, Excel …), Windows program for x64 and ARM (mark text, Ctrl+Alt+S), Office add-in with a button in Outl …

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Contacts (Features → Mail and contacts → "Contacts"; Contacts → Settings): The assistant knows phone numbers, e-mail addresses and birthdays from your address book.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Edit contacts (Features → Mail and contacts → "Edit contacts"; builds on "Contacts"; Contacts → Settings): On the page Contacts you change a card like on Apple: "Edit", a minus per field to remove it, an "+ add" per kind for phone, e-mail, address and website, "Done" saves.

head: Mail and contacts
title: Mail and contacts
text: - Contacts for contacts apps (Features → Mail and contacts → "Contacts for contacts apps"; builds on "Contacts"; Contacts → Settings): The address book "On the Spark" shows in the iPhone's Contacts app (or Thunderbird, DAVx5 on Android), both ways when "Edit contacts" is on; otherwise read only.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Home Assistant (Features → Home → "Home Assistant"; Me → Smart home): Control lights, devices and heating by voice and ask for values.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Room mode (Features → Home → "Room mode"; Me → Room mode): For a chosen time the assistant listens to the conversation in the room and helps in a pause: answers open questions, suggests appointments or shopping items, gives the real value on "cold" or "dark".

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Ignore TV voices (Features → Home → "Ignore TV voices"; builds on "Room mode"; Me → Room mode): In room mode only voices the Spark knows count: TV, radio and visitors trigger no questions or suggestions.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Room mode for Home Assistant (Features → Home → "Room mode for Home Assistant"; builds on "Room mode"; Me → Room mode): Home Assistant sees on which device room mode listens right now and until when, and can end it, e.g.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Own speakers (ESP32) (Features → Home → "Own speakers (ESP32)"; Me → Speakers): A small ESP32-S3 board with a microphone and speaker becomes a voice assistant in the room.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Stop while it speaks (Features → Home → "Stop while it speaks"; builds on "Own speakers (ESP32)"; Me → Speakers): While an own speaker talks its microphone stays on.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Start room mode from afar (Features → Home → "Start room mode from afar"; builds on "Room mode"; Me → Room mode): You say or type "Raummodus im Wohnzimmer an" on one device and your living room speaker listens.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Announcements on speakers (Features → Home → "Announcements on speakers"; builds on "Chats"; Me → Conversation): "Announcement in the living room: dinner is ready": the speaker plays a tone and says it.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Home Assistant Assist (Wyoming) (Features → Home → "Home Assistant Assist (Wyoming)"): Home Assistant uses the Spark's speech recognition and voice.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Phone (Features → Home → "Phone"; Me → Phone): Call the Spark from a phone in the house (DECT handset, IP phone) and talk to it like to a speaker: ask, "Stopp" or # interrupts, "Tschüss" or hanging up ends.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Phone: take guests (Features → Home → "Phone: take guests"; builds on "Phone"): A handset without a profile and, with "Calls from outside", an unknown or hidden number get questions and answers as a guest.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Phone: calls from outside (Features → Home → "Phone: calls from outside"; builds on "Phone"): Call the Spark from on the go: a number confirmed under Me → Phone picks its profile.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Phone: the Spark calls (Features → Home → "Phone: the Spark calls"; builds on "Phone"; Me → Phone): The Spark calls by itself: wake-up call and reminder by call a profile orders itself, and the call back for callers from outside with an unsure voice.

head: Home
title: Home
text: - Phone: call on outages (Features → Home → "Phone: call on outages"; builds on "Phone: the Spark calls"): If a service of the service watch is gone 10 minutes or longer, the Spark calls the admin besides the note, at most once an hour.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Bus and train (Features → On the go and devices → "Bus and train"; Me → Bus and train): The next departures at your stop and connections to a destination, with delays and platform.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Telegram (Features → On the go and devices → "Telegram"; Me → Telegram): You write to the assistant through your own Telegram bot or send a voice message, from anywhere.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Android app (Features → On the go and devices → "Android app"; Me → Android app): An app for Android phones, without the Play Store: it shows the Spark like the page on the phone and can also show notes while closed, start as the assistant app and share text from other apps to Spark.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Android: notes at once (Features → On the go and devices → "Android: notes at once"; builds on "Android app"; Me → Android app): Without a Google service notes on Android come every 15 minutes.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Android: update in the app (Features → On the go and devices → "Android: update in the app"; builds on "Android app"; Me → Android app): When the Spark has a newer Android app, the app shows a strip "Update now" at the top.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Android: Spark as assistant (Features → On the go and devices → "Android: Spark as assistant"; builds on "Android app"; Me → Android app): Spark becomes the phone's assistant: long-press the power or home button and a sheet with the face lies over the open app.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Android: fingerprint for admins (Features → On the go and devices → "Android: fingerprint for admins"; builds on "Android app"; Me → Android app): When a profile with an admin role or the panel password is signed in to the Android app, the app shows the Spark only after the fingerprint, face or screen lock: when opened and again after 5 minutes in the background.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Spark companion on PC and Mac (Features → On the go and devices → "Spark companion on PC and Mac"; Me → Companion): A small program in the Windows taskbar (x64 and ARM) and the Mac menu bar.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Companion may act on the PC (Features → On the go and devices → "Companion may act on the PC"; builds on "Spark companion on PC and Mac"; Me → Companion): The Spark may open a page or a released program on your paired computer, bring a program to the front, close, minimize or full-screen the front window, press fixed keys (next, previous, space, undo, copy, paste, save …), type your own wo …

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Write along in meetings (Features → On the go and devices → "Write along in meetings"; builds on "Spark companion on PC and Mac"; Me → Companion): The Spark companion writes along in a meeting when you click "Besprechung mitschreiben" in the companion (or Ctrl+Alt+R, Mac ⌥⌘R): the microphone and the computer's sound go to speech recognition in pieces.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Show and operate the screen (Features → On the go and devices → "Show and operate the screen"; builds on "Spark companion on PC and Mac"; Me → Companion): You see the screen of your own PC or Mac in the panel or in the iPhone or Android app and, when the person at the computer picks "Allow", operate it with mouse and keyboard: a tap is a click, dragging moves the mouse, text and fixed keys …

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Spark operates the computer (Features → On the go and devices → "Spark operates the computer"; builds on "Spark companion on PC and Mac"; Me → Companion): On your word the Spark does a task on your own PC or Mac step by step: it looks at the screen and proposes one click, scroll, key or text at a time.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Pebble watch (Features → On the go and devices → "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): The "Spark" watch app for Pebble Time 2, Core 2 Duo and Pebble Round 2 gets address and key from a setup code instead of typing both on the phone.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: follow-ups to tap (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: follow-ups to tap"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): Under an answer on the Pebble watch there are up to three fitting follow-up questions, e.g.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: quick commands (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: quick commands"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): Your own fixed sentences on the Pebble watch, e.g.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: reminders and timers on the wrist (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: reminders and timers on the wrist"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): Your next 8 reminders and timers are kept as wake-ups on the Pebble watch and vibrate on time, even when the phone is away.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Spark watchface (Features → On the go and devices → "Spark watchface"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): A watchface of its own for the Pebble watch: time and date, below your next appointment, the next reminder, the weather and a hint.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: my day and my week (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: my day and my week"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): At the top of the watch list (hold UP) are "Mein Tag" and "Meine Woche".

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: notes for admins (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: notes for admins"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): When a service does not answer (language model, speech recognition, Home Assistant …), the admins' Spark watchface shows a red bar on top and vibrates once.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: quick notes (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: quick notes"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): In the watch list (hold UP) pick "Merken" and say a sentence, e.g.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: place with a note (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: place with a note"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): When noting, the phone adds the place to the sentence, rounded to about 100 metres, e.g.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: messages (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: messages"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): The watch list (hold UP) has „Nachrichten“: the latest 8 chats with the number of unread ones.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: reply suggestions (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: reply suggestions"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): When the last message came from somebody else, the language model suggests up to three short replies; they come below the fixed sentences.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: remote (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: remote"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): „Fernbedienung“ in the watch list shows up to 12 devices you picked under Me → Pebble watch, and your own speakers.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Watch: steps, pulse and sleep (Features → On the go and devices → "Watch: steps, pulse and sleep"; builds on "Pebble watch"; Me → Pebble watch): When the app opens, the watch sends its numbers of the day: steps, last pulse and sleep.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Terminal client (Features → On the go and devices → "Terminal client"; Me → Terminal): The "spark-tui" program brings the Spark into a terminal, e.g.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Device updates (Features → On the go and devices → "Device updates"; Me → Conversation): The Spark fetches new firmware for the speakers, the Android app and the Spark companion from GitHub, checks every file by checksum and tells you once when a new version is ready.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Update speakers at night (Features → On the go and devices → "Update speakers at night"; builds on "Device updates"; Me → Conversation): The speakers fetch new firmware only when they start.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Note on a new XiaoZhi version (Features → On the go and devices → "Note on a new XiaoZhi version"; builds on "Device updates"): The speaker firmware builds on XiaoZhi (github.com/78/xiaozhi-esp32) at a fixed point.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Spark as MCP server (Features → On the go and devices → "Spark as MCP server"; Me → Spark as MCP server): Other programs (Open WebUI, n8n, Home Assistant, Claude …) use the Spark over the Model Context Protocol: speech to text, text to speech, Wikipedia and Kiwix, own documents, appointments, reminders and "Ask Spark".

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - MCP server from outside (OAuth) (Features → On the go and devices → "MCP server from outside (OAuth)"; builds on "Spark as MCP server"; Me → Spark as MCP server): Programs on the internet like claude.ai or ChatGPT connect to the Spark through your reverse proxy.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - MCP: acting with confirmation (Features → On the go and devices → "MCP: acting with confirmation"; builds on "Spark as MCP server"; Me → Spark as MCP server): A program may switch the smart home, enter appointments and set reminders, but only as a proposal.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - iPhone app (Features → On the go and devices → "iPhone app"; Me → iPhone app): An own app for the iPhone: press the button, ask, the answer comes in the Spark voice, also with the screen locked.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Push to the iPhone app (Features → On the go and devices → "Push to the iPhone app"; builds on "iPhone app"; Me → iPhone app): Reminders, the morning briefing and notes come to the iPhone even when the app is closed.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Panel areas in the iPhone app (Features → On the go and devices → "Panel areas in the iPhone app"; builds on "iPhone app"; Me → iPhone app): The iPhone app shows parts of the panel itself: memory, the next appointments, the Spark's reminders and conversation settings.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Apps keep the last state (Features → On the go and devices → "Apps keep the last state"): The iPhone and the Android app keep the last state of some pages on the phone: the conversations (the 20 newest with 50 messages each), the chats, the own settings and functions and in the iPhone app the numbers on the tiles of "My thing …

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Review access for the iPhone app (Features → On the go and devices → "Review access for the iPhone app"; builds on "iPhone app"): For Apple's App Store review: instead of the pairing link that works only 10 minutes, the reviewer gets your panel's address and a code of twelve letters and digits.

head: On the go and devices
title: On the go and devices
text: - Spark update from the iPhone app (Features → On the go and devices → "Spark update from the iPhone app"; builds on "iPhone app"): Chosen profiles get a notification when a new version with green tests is ready and see in the app under Settings → Spark version what changes.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Speaker recognition (Features → Access → "Speaker recognition"; Me → Speaker identification): The assistant recognises you by voice, even on someone else's device, and then answers with your memory and settings.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Code word at a speaker (Features → Access → "Code word at a speaker"; builds on "Speaker recognition"; Me → Speakers): A speaker in a room gives personal things only to your clearly recognised voice.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Second sign-in step (Features → Access → "Second sign-in step"; Me → Security): Signing in with name and PIN also needs a code from an authenticator app.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Reporting problems (Features → Access → "Reporting problems"; Me → Reporting problems): Something does not work?

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Tell admins about reports (Features → Access → "Tell admins about reports"; builds on "Reporting problems"; Me → Reporting problems): When a profile sends a report to GitHub or keeps it on the Spark only, the assistant tells the admin profiles (role Admin, the main admin first): in the assistant when the page is open, else as a note on the device.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Usage counter (Features → Access → "Usage counter"; Me → Usage): The Spark counts how much its models work: tokens read and written at the language model (of them from the cache), questions to the classifier, seconds of listening and speaking, texts of the meaning search, re-ranked hits and pictures.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Quota (Features → Access → "Quota"; builds on "Usage counter"; Me → Usage): Every profile has a language model limit for the day, the week (from Monday) and the month (from the 1st), each on its own, 0 means none.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Service watch (Features → Access → "Service watch"; Me → Conversation): The Spark looks by itself whether its services answer: language model, listening, speaking, the internet, the web search (SearXNG), the own Kiwix archive, Home Assistant, the mail and calendar servers and the NAS of the backup, each only …

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Round-trip check (Features → Access → "Round-trip check"; builds on "Service watch"): Every few minutes the Spark makes a real test run: Speaking says a fixed sentence, Listening writes it down again, and the language model answers a fixed question in at most three words.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Sentry (Features → Access → "Sentry"): The Spark tells its admins by itself when something happens at the doors: a lockout after wrong sign-ins, a new way in (trusted browser, passkey, program over MCP, paired Spark, used invitation), changed protection (admin password, secon …

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Maintenance pause (Features → Access → "Maintenance pause"): Before you put a new language model (own or qwen38), speech recognition or speech output in place, you pause the Spark for a while.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Maintenance pause on restart (Features → Access → "Maintenance pause on restart"; builds on "Maintenance pause"): The Spark notices by itself when the language model (own or qwen38), the speech recognition or the speech output restarts or switches, and pauses just that part for up to 30 minutes, like with the button.

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Emergency mode with Parakeet (Features → Access → "Emergency mode with Parakeet"): When the panel runs on a computer of its own (Spark split) and the DGX is gone, the Spark otherwise answers every question with "The Spark is taking a break right now." With this switch the panel computer hears by itself: Parakeet recogn …

head: Access
title: Access
text: - Case (Features → Access → "Case"): If the panel computer sits in a SunFounder Pironman 5, the Spark drives its parts itself, without SunFounder's software: the small display shows the admin status and numbers in turn (Spark, services and maintenance, Pi, DGX gone or pause …

head: Access
title: Access
