With *Settings → Security → Lautsprecher-Updates auch über http* switched off (on by default so existing speakers keep updating; changing it needs a code), a speaker that reaches the Spark over http gets no update over Wi-Fi (diagnosis: "nicht über http angeboten"), and the night round skips it; updating over USB in the browser always works. A known board id from another board (different MAC) gets nothing, the key after the code goes only to the address that showed the code, and a wrong challenge at activation is refused. - Companion: the Windows and Mac companions load updates only over https. A Mac companion signed with a Developer ID takes only an update from the same team (codesign -R with the Team ID from its own signature); an ad-hoc signed one checks size, SHA-256, bundle id and a valid signature as before. - iPhone app: a pairing link to another Spark asks explicitly "Switch to another Spark?" with both addresses; unsent messages do not go along when switching. - root and units: install.sh a

text: nd update.sh read config.json, the update progress, the engine signatures and update-target only as the service user (as_svc cat). The API watchdog (speech-spark-watch) has MemoryMax=1G and PrivateTmp=yes; the vLLM engines deliberately have no MemoryMax (shared GPU memory). - Speech services without an API key: with an empty api.key, ASR and TTS answer only the Spark itself. An old configuration that listens in the network without a key gets a new one at the update. - ffmpeg and speech recognition: every ffmpeg call reads only files and pipes (-protocol_whitelist file,pipe); a playlist fetches nothing from the network. The ASR service waits at its gate before it reads a recording (up to 200 MB) into memory; Parakeet decodes one recording at a time, with two threads and a time limit. - Telegram voice messages are downloaded like photos: streamed, cut off after 5 MB, the file path from Telegram checked. - Spark update: if /etc/speech-spark-signers exists but is not a plain file of root (a link, another owner, writable by others), the update stops instead of quietly skipping the check. Without the file the update log says "Signature check off". To switch it on: sign commits with an SS

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: The red "Notaus" button (bottom of the sidebar, on phones at the top of Manage) stops the Spark in three stages. Triggering needs no code and only goes up; lifting is for admins only.

head: Kill switch (Notaus)
title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: - Who triggers: only admins (panel password, profiles with the role Admin or Manager), also from their iPhone app and on the way (since V01.0.338; before, a switch could allow it for every profile). Ordinary profiles see neither the button nor the band nor the Status card; only in stage 3 or from outside a page "The Spark is stopped right now" without a name or reason. Never guests, MCP or the language model; Telegram, voice, Home Assistant and the Android tile only as described under *Other ways* below (since V01.0.360). - Lifting: only the panel password or a profile with the role Admin, only in a browser (no app key, no HTTP Basic), only in the home network, with a fresh code (without a second step: the panel password again). Choice: back to stage 1 or off; held jobs then run on or are cancelled (default). - Home network means a direct connection from a private network. Through a reverse proxy only what a listed proxy (Settings → Security → Reverse proxy) passes on as a home address counts; a listed proxy without that counts as outside. So list the proxy there. - Kept across restart and update (state/notaus.json). A damaged file counts as stage 3, never as off. Way out without t

title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: he panel: sudo rm /var/lib/speech-spark/state/notaus.json. - Visible: red band on every page, a card under Status (kinds and counts since it was triggered, never contents), a push to the admin profiles when triggered and lifted, an entry in the admin log. Status → Live and the live monitor /live show a red band with stage, time, channel and per kind "held" with a count (never the reason or a name) and keep running in stage 3 (reading only; pairing a new monitor waits). - ESP32 speakers (firmware build 6 and later, since V01.0.364): hold the BOOT button for 5 seconds. The firmware then sends the fixed wake word "spark-notaus" (only the button sends it, never speech recognition). Only a speaker of an admin profile triggers the big emergency stop, stage 2, and announces it; otherwise it says "only for an admin's speaker". Never *My kill switch*: a button press does not say who pressed it. - Pebble watch (watch app 1.6.0 and later, since V01.0.364): hold SELECT for 3 seconds until it buzzes long, then let go. The watch sends the fixed sentence "Spark, Notaus" (as above: the big one only for admin profiles). "Spark, Mein Notaus" works by dictation. - iPhone app (since V01.0.370, with th

title: Kill switch (Notaus)
text: e next TestFlight build): emergency stop button behind a question and the Siri shortcut "Spark Notaus"; without an admin role only *My kill switch*, never lifting in the app. - Emergency stop by itself (since V01.0.364, switch under *Settings → Security*, off; changing it needs the admin code): the guard switches on stage 1 "Outside closed" by fixed rules, never higher: 20 wrong sign-ins, PINs, codes or emergency stop keys from outside in 10 minutes; an MCP flood from outside (30 MCP requests turned away by the rate limit in 10 minutes); 15 connections refused by netguard in 10 minutes (such as 169.254.x, home addresses or the Spark's own services, where outside text tries to steer the Spark; refusals by the emergency stop itself do not count). Counted in memory only. Channel "Wächter" in the push, the admin log and Status → Live; lifting as always.

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: All of these only switch on, never off; lifting stays in the browser. The panel always decides by fixed rules, never the language model and never text from outside.

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: - Telegram: /meinnotaus stops the own profile (like *My kill switch*; afterwards Telegram only answers "Mein Notaus ist an"). /notaus (stage 2) or /notaus 1–/notaus 3 only for profiles with an admin role; forwarded messages never count as a command. From stage 1 on Telegram itself rests. - Fixed sentence in the chat, by voice on the phone, in the app or at a speaker that recognised the voice: "Spark, Mein Notaus" for every profile, "Spark, Notaus" (stage 2) or "Spark, Notaus Stufe eins/zwei/drei" only for admin profiles. Only the whole sentence, no question about it ("Was ist der Notaus?" triggers nothing). Never over MCP, never for a voice the speaker does not recognise as the profile. - Home Assistant: *Settings → Security → Emergency stop from outside* creates a key (fresh admin code, at most 5, only the hash in state/notaus-keys.json, plain text shown once) with ready text for configuration.yaml: rest_command.spark_notaus (POST /api/notaus/ha, Authorization: Bearer …, {"level": 1–3}, default 2) and a REST sensor on /api/notaus with the stage. Home network only; the key reads nothing, lifts nothing and is no device key. Wrong keys lock like wrong logins, rate limit notausha. - A

head: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
title: Other ways to the emergency stop (since V01.0.360)
text: ndroid tile (Android app 1.1.0 and later): add "Notaus" in quick settings. It uses the login of the app's page; admins choose "Ganzer Spark" (stage 2) or "Mein Notaus", everyone else only "Mein Notaus", always behind a question. The tile shows the stage. - The channel shows in the admin log, the push and on Status → Live (telegram, sprache, ha, android).

head: My kill switch (own profile only)
title: My kill switch (own profile only)
text: Since V01.0.338 every signed-in profile has its own, weaker kill switch under *Me → Security → My kill switch* (admins have it besides the big one). It stops only this profile; the others notice nothing:

head: My kill switch (own profile only)
title: My kill switch (own profile only)
text: - Ways in closed: every other browser login ends (the browser that triggered it stays signed in); the profile's device keys (iPhone and Android app, Siri, watch, speakers, Home Assistant events) only get "locked", as do MCP keys, OAuth access and Telegram. - Nothing in its name: smart home, mail drafts and tidying, messages and announcements, appointments, lists, reMarkable, MCP actions; no "yes" carries anything out; jobs wait in the queue; "on its own", Home Assistant notes and briefings of the profile stay silent. - Reading stays (Dominik's choice 3b): in its own browser the profile still asks and may read mail, calendar, memory and documents. - Lifting: the profile itself, only in the browser (no app key), with its PIN (wrong tries lock like at sign-in) and a fresh code when its second step is on; or an admin under *Status → Profiles' own kill switch* (same rules as the big one). The admin profiles get a push with the name, never a reason. - File: state/notaus-mine.json. A damaged file holds every profile, and only an admin lifts that. Status → Live shows only how many profiles, never which.

head: Reporting problems
title: Reporting problems
text: Since V01.0.386. Something does not work? Every profile describes it briefly under Me → Reporting problems and gets a draft; guests never. Admin switch: Features → Access → "Reporting problems", plus the target repository (default db9979/spark-meldungen, private). It opens everywhere: "Report a problem" at the bottom of the panel, Status → Logs, Ctrl/⌘ K, Me → Reporting problems, in the Android app (panel), in the iPhone app under Settings, in the Spark companion (Windows: the icon's menu; Mac: settings), by Telegram /melden text and by voice (also watch and speakers) with the fixed sentence "Spark, Problem melden: …". Telegram and voice only make a draft; sending always comes after a look at the preview.

head: Reporting problems
title: What goes along
text: What goes along: the description, if wanted the own last requests (only ways, tools, times from Logs → Requests), the system state (version, services, memory), from the iPhone app the sound log, and for admins only diagnose log lines of the area (10, 30 or 60 min).

head: Reporting problems
title: Anonymizing
text: Anonymizing: fixed rules on the Spark, no language model. First the log redaction, then secrets (everything in the vault, tokens, passwords) become [GEHEIM], contents in log lines (quotes, subject, question, search, appointment, file name …) [INHALT], addresses [URL], [MAIL], [IP-LAN], [IP], [HOST], places [ORT], phone numbers [TELEFON], long identifiers [ID], profile, device and account names [PERSON-1], [GERÄT-1], [KONTO-1] (same number for the same name). Code blocks and @ cannot trigger anything. Only the anonymized version is stored, 14 days.

head: Reporting problems
title: Preview and sending
text: Preview and sending: the Spark shows title and text exactly as they go out; lines can be unticked. Only what matches the preview is sent (a signature over the text); a leak check blocks sending while a known name, a mail address, an address or a secret is still in it. Three ways: "Send to GitHub" (issue via api.github.com), "Open in the browser" (GitHub with the text filled in, works without a token) and "Keep locally only". Limits: per profile 20 open drafts and 10 new a day, 3 sent per profile and 10 per day, one minute apart. Who sees other drafts: every profile only its own; all drafts (with names, view, send, delete) only the admin and the admin role, since V01.0.544 no longer the Verwalter (manager) role (review pruefung/kontext-trennung-2026-10-14.md).

head: Reporting problems
title: Token
text: Token: a fine-grained token for the report repository only with "Issues: Read and write", 90 days. Only the main admin saves it with a fresh code (Features → Reporting problems), sealed in the vault, never shown, never logged; classic ghp_ tokens are refused. "Check" shows the expiry date and warns when the repository is public; 14 days before expiry a hint shows on Status → Live.

head: Reporting problems
title: Admin view
text: Admin view: admins see every report of every profile, for sent ones the state on GitHub (open or done), the number of answers and the answers themselves as plain text with a link; a profile sees only its own. Answers from GitHub never go to the language model.

head: Reporting problems
title: Tell the admin through the assistant
text: Tell the admin through the assistant (since V01.0.386, sub-switch, off): when a profile sends or keeps a report, the assistant tells the admin profiles (role Admin, the main admin first), in the assistant when the page is open, else as a note. Only profile name, area, way and number, never the text; the reporting profile itself gets nothing. Every admin profile turns it off for itself under Me → Reporting problems; during the Notaus it stays silent.

head: Reporting problems
title: Live
text: Live: Status → Live shows GitHub (reports) with the number of drafts and of those sent today, never contents.

head: Stability
title: Stability
text: - Backups: every day, before every update, before going back to the previous version and before every restore the panel backs up profiles (memory, conversations, documents, calendars, mail accounts, smart home, speaker ID), cloned voices, settings, the panel password and the shared state of the Spark (the admin's second login step, iPhone push key and devices, Telegram bot, browser push key, ESP32 speakers, agent services, own test questions) to /var/lib/speech-spark/backups. Counted separately, the newest seven daily or manual ones and the newest five from before an update, rollback or restore are kept. *Settings → Update and backup → Backup* downloads, restores or deletes each one and restores a downloaded file. A restore checks the settings like the settings page does, caps the size and swaps all parts or none; the current state is backed up first. Passwords and tokens are in the backup encrypted, the key is not: on another Spark they have to be entered again. An admin second login step the Spark cannot read is then not taken over (the current one stays). For a move there is the move backup: it also carries the key, encrypted with a password you type (at least 12 characters, scr

title: Stability
text: ypt + Fernet). It restores only with the same password; a wrong one changes nothing, and after five wrong ones in an hour the panel waits. The Spark's login keys are in no backup, so after a move everyone signs in again. Whoever has the file and the password can read all stored credentials: keep them apart. - Backup to the outside (since V01.0.286, plan "Bedienung gesamt" D4, off): *Settings → Backup → Sicherung nach außen* (main admin only, changes with the admin code). Once a day a move backup goes over WebDAV into a folder (NAS, Nextcloud, Synology; https only, through netguard, home network allowed), first encrypted as a whole with the backup password (scrypt as for the move backup, AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB pieces, each numbered and the last one marked: cutting, swapping or changing shows when decrypting). The NAS only sees encrypted data. Restore: download the file (…-offsite.tar.gz.enc) from the NAS and load it under *Aus Datei wiederherstellen* with the backup password, also on a new Spark; wrong passwords count as for the move backup (5 per hour). Without the password the copy is lost: write it down. WebDAV password and backup password are sealed in the vault (state/offsite.jso

text: n, part of the backup), never in a log; a new address needs the WebDAV password again. The last 7 copies stay there; only what this Spark sent itself is deleted. Runs like the daily backup only in speech pauses (vorrang.py), after a failure the next try after 6 hours; *Jetzt senden* right away. Logs: offsite_backup, offsite_failed. - The NAS certificate (since V01.0.487, zertpin.py): when the certificate does not fit the address (self-made, or made for a name such as nas.local while the address is an IP), checking is never switched off. "Check certificate" shows fingerprint (SHA-256), names and expiry; the admin compares it with the one in the NAS and accepts exactly that certificate (with a fresh code; only what the NAS shows at that moment is accepted). From then on it is the only trust anchor in the TLS handshake, the name is not compared; any other certificate gets neither password nor copy. A new address or "Forget" removes it. The error names the way instead of CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED; the Dienst-Wächter checks with the same certificate. Better where possible: the address with a name from the certificate. - Copy of my data (formerly "Own storage", since V01.0.453, plan plae

title: Stability

The Spark mounts nothing itself and always works locally; the storage is only the target of a copy every 30 minutes in speech pauses that sends only what changed (at most 2 GB per run, 2 runs at once). - What may go there is a fixed list (areas to choose): conversations, memory, tasks/reminders, documents (text, search, originals), created documents. Never: keys, sign-in, the second sign-in step, passwords of other services, settings, voice prints. The search database goes as a consistent copy (SQLite backup). - Encryption: every file an object of its own under a random name, AES-256-GCM in 1 MiB pieces (numbered, the

title: Stability
text: - Service watch (chat.svc_watch, below it chat.svc_watch_users, all off; released for every profile, never guests; each admin profile can switch the note off under Me → Conversation → Services (svc_note, on from the start), V01.0.440; dienstwacht.py, plan plaene/dienst-ausfall-melden.md): the panel looks by itself whether its services answer, only what is switched on: language model (/models of the stored address), listening and speaking (/health), internet (three fixed public addresses, www.google.com, www.microsoft.com and cloudflare.com, gone only when none answers; since V01.0.452 never api.github.com, because every question there counts against GitHub's 60 per hour the update check needs), SearXNG (/healthz), Kiwix, Home Assistant, mail servers, calendar servers and the NAS of the backup. Every minute, mail, calendar and NAS every 5 minutes (after a failed try every minute). - Without login: an HTTP answer below 500 (401 too) counts as "answers", for the mail server its TLS greeting on the IMAP port. Tokens and passwords are not opened for it. Since V01.0.601 Home Assistant is asked for /manifest.json, which it answers without a token; before, every probe of /api/ counted ther

Addresses only from the settings, through netguard at each module's level (Kiwix, Home Assistant, NAS: home network; mail, calendar: user rules; internet: public), 5 seconds, 64 KB. These checks are not on the live view's Wächter list and never start the automatic kill switch (netguard.QUIET). While the internet is gone, the services behind it (public address) get no note of their own; "internet gone" names them and the functions that need the internet. Everything from one round is one note per admin. - Round-trip check (since V01.0.699, chat.rundlauf below the service watch, off; spacing chat.rundlauf_mi

Every step with the stage „hinten“ (people go first), with Spark split through the TLS-Tor and the LLM-Tor like every request. Every step is measured in ms, and the whole way. text: teps, the whole way with the curve of the last 24 runs, today ok and errors), *Status → Live* (target „Rundlauf“ with the times, a hint at the step that fails), the control centre and the iPhone app from the same data. Only times and fixed words are kept (rundlauf.json, stays on this device). Logs: rundlauf: ok tts 420 asr 310 llm 280 ms, rundlauf: fehler asr falsch, rundlauf: stoerung asr, rundlauf: wieder ok. - Who hears it: the admin profiles (notaus.admin_uids: role Admin, the main admin first), unless they switched it off, through push.send (tag svc) on the device they pick under *Me → Conversation → Services* (svc_device: used last, iPhone, Android, companion, Telegram, browser or all; not set up: as usual). "Only collect at night" (svc_night): nothing from 10 pm to 7 am, one summary at 7. A note that does not get out (without internet the push does not reach the iPhone) waits at most 12 hours and is tried again every 5 minutes or with the next note, then with times ("was gone from 06:00 to 06:43"). Notes name only the service, the time and what does not work; never an address, a host, a profile name or an error text. - Shown: on top of every admin page and in the iPhone app

head: Stability
title: Stability
text: under "Manage Spark" "Restricted right now: …" (health.alerts); *Status → Services* lists every service with its state, since when, outages today and the outages of the last 7 days; removing a tick takes a service off the list (PUT /api/admin/svcwatch/{id}), "Check now" looks at once (POST /api/admin/svcwatch/check, rate limit svcwatchnow 4 per minute). The live view shows a dot per service, the target "Internet" and outage and all-clear under "Events". head: Self-test
title: Self-test
text: Every install and update runs the panel's self-test (app/tests) against fake LLM, TTS and Home Assistant servers in a throw-away directory: login and access, that profiles never see each other's memory, documents, conversations, mailboxes or Home Assistant, the chat tools, learning from conversations, calendar and text cleaning. It runs before the new version goes live. In an update a failure stops the update and the old version keeps running; on a first install it is only reported. The result is in the update log. It includes the security checks (test_hardening.py, one test per guard) and a scanner (test_scanner.py) that refuses new code using shell=True, eval or the like, a route without a login, an upload read without a size limit, values in onclick not escaped for JavaScript, or an assistant tool not sorted as "reads outside text / changes something / own data only". By hand: cd /opt/speech-spark/app && sudo /opt/speech-spark/venv-panel/bin/python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .

head: Self-test
title: Gentle updates
text: Gentle updates (from V01.0.379): when the update installs exactly the version whose GitHub test run passed, the Spark only runs a smoke test (tests/test_rauchtest.py, a few seconds: every module loads with this Spark's packages, the panel starts and answers). Since V01.0.643 a panel computer without models of its own (Spark teilen, e.g. a Raspberry Pi 5) always runs only the smoke test; the whole self-test ran past its 900 s there, and GitHub's "Tests" run the whole one for every version. Otherwise the whole self-test still runs on a first install, with --newest, --to and when going back to the previous version. Both run with the lowest CPU and disk priority (nice 19, ionice class 2/7), so an answer being spoken keeps its speed. An update asks apt only when a package is missing, pip only when the package list or the lock file changed (.pkgs or .locked in the environment), and downloads models only when other ones are chosen (/opt/speech-spark/.models). The ASR and TTS services restart only when something they run from changed: their files per app/restart-map, their systemd unit, the settings or their Python packages; a service the list does not know always restarts, and the smoke t

text: est checks the list against the imports. VoiceDesign, like the engines, restarts only when its settings changed. The panel restarts on every update (about 8 s).

head: Self-test
title: A red main does not go unnoticed
text: A red main does not go unnoticed (V01.0.822): when the newest state on GitHub failed the tests, *Settings → Update* says since when ("Red since Mon 23:44"), and the update line in the Live box says the same. The "Tests" run then opens the issue "main rot" on GitHub with the names of the red tests (GitHub tells the repository's owner), adds every further red run and closes it with the next green one. Tests that pass only the second time go as a comment to the issue "Wackelnde Tests". Before every push tools/vorpush.py stops while main is red (only the ROT-FIX passes, with --rotfix) and runs every test, not only those of the changed files.

head: Self-test
title: Install overnight
text: Install overnight (Settings → Update, off): a new tested version is installed at night between 3 and 5 am, at most once a night, with a backup first. If somebody is talking with the Spark (within the last two minutes) it waits for the next pause; if GitHub cannot be reached it asks again after 15 minutes. Nothing starts during the kill switch. Turning it on needs the second sign-in step when that is on. The "Install update" button asks once more when a conversation is going on. The live view shows a running update under "Running now" with its step and share, its outcome for an hour, and whether "overnight" is on.

head: Self-test
title: Hands-on test
text: Hands-on test (since V01.0.697, admin only, not for managers): *Status → Hands-on test* shows what is new and should still be tried out in daily use, the newest first. The check points are one list in the repository (app/panel/praxistest.json: number, version, title, steps, thread); every new feature adds its point with the next number, numbers never change. Per point „Works“, „Problem“ or „Later“; „Problem“ shows the way to *Status → Logs → Diagnosis* to give the excerpt with the number to the thread. Points before V01.0.600 that nobody marked are folded away as „old, probably done“, with one button „All old ones done“. Only the word per number is kept (praxistest-stand.json, stays on this device), never a text. „Needs you“ names the open points as a quiet line (never red); the iPhone app shows the page under „Manage Spark“. Logs: praxistest: klappt|problem|spaeter|offen P123, praxistest: alt erledigt N. The steps are written in German.

head: Logs
title: Logs
text: All speech services log into their own journal (journalctl --namespace=speech-spark -u 'speech-spark-*'), capped at 500 MB and 14 days; journald deletes older entries automatically. Adjustable under Settings → Operation, effective after the next update. The panel's constant status polls are not logged at all.

head: Logs
title: Without profile names
text: Without profile names (since V01.0.443): journal lines name a profile only if it agreed under Me → Conversation → Privacy (the same switch as for Logs → Requests); otherwise they say "Profil" and the end of its id, e.g. "iphone: paired for Profil 3f2a". The admin log still names who changed something.

head: Logs
title: Diagnostic filters in the panel
text: Diagnostic filters in the panel (since V01.0.141): *Status → Logs → Diagnostic filters* replaces journalctl … | grep -E "room:|esp32:" | tail -30 on the console. Tick chat:, web search (chat: web search), homeassistant:, room:, esp32:, update and self-test (unit speech-spark-update) and errors (error, Fehler, traceback, failed, warn); several ticks mean "or", none shows every line. Time range 10 min to 24 h, 30 to 1000 lines (newest kept); "Copy" takes the output including a header with filter and hit count. Admin only, at most 60 requests per minute. Filtering runs in Python against a fixed list; only numbers from fixed lists reach journalctl. Bot tokens, bearer keys, password=/token=/key= values and logins inside URLs are blacked out before display.

head: Logs
title: Logs page "overview first"
text: Logs page "overview first" (since V01.0.212): tabs Diagnosis, Services, Update and Changes. Under Diagnosis tiles show the error count and the three busiest areas with a small history over the time range (tap to filter), below the newest error with a fixed hint (e.g. HTTP 401 from Home Assistant → token expired). Filter buttons with counts: conversation, web search, router, Home Assistant, room, speakers, Telegram, mail and "errors only". Each line shows time, area and message; errors red, warnings yellow (fixed word list in the panel), repeated lines as "×n", pauses from 2 min as a divider. Search runs in the browser over the loaded lines only. "Live" reloads every 10 s (services every 3 s) and pauses while you scroll up or select text. "Copy for thread" takes version, filter and the raw lines in a code block.

head: Logs
title: Complete log lines
text: Complete log lines (since V01.0.493, Dominik: "Why does an announcement from the chat not show up in the log?"): until then an announcement wrote a line only when it was said; when it was refused (switch off, no speaker allowed, hourly limit, Notaus, quiet time) nothing was written anywhere. The Changes tab missed every Chats path, because the exception /api/chat as a prefix also matched /api/chats/…. Now every action writes one line for every outcome, fixed words and numbers only, the profile only as profiles.log_name. - Announcement (filter "Messages and chats"): messages: announcement sent|refused <reason> | via chats|assistant|house | N speaker(s) picked, N now, N at next wake word, N quiet time | N chars, at the wake word messages: announcement said at wake word or too old, dropped. Also refused messages of the assistant, chat messages read on the speaker (at once or at the wake word), a sentence stopped at the speaker, every refusal of the Chats page (chats: refused | why … | http …) and "delete chat for me". - Tools (new filter "Tools"): chat: tool <name> ok|not ok|not offered | N ms for every call; the name only when the tool was offered. - Lists, appointments, reminders (n

head: Logs
title: Complete log lines
text: ew filter): entry added, ticked off or deleted (with count, Notaus or kind of error), handed to the iPhone, appointment saved or not, reminder played on a device, deleted or dropped after more than 6 h. - Notifications (new filter): every notification with its kind (job, reminder, chat …), devices and ways reached, held by "Do not disturb"; browser push without the outside server's text. - Computer, own services, documents (new filter): acting on the PC (done, declined, no answer), own MCP service (done, declined, error), document sent or refused. - Memory: fact saved (with its source) or forgotten (count); mail: confirmed sorting, undo, cleanup or draft done, refused or failed; Telegram: document sent or refused. - Changes tab: announcement, groups, members, invitations, keys and "who may write to me" are in it now; writing, reading and typing in chats stays out.

head: Logs
title: A log for everything, checked by tests
text: A log for everything, checked by tests (since V01.0.504, Dominik: "Why is the log so inconsistent? … Always put everything new into the log."): - What Status → Live shows under Events is in the journal too now, whether Live is on or not: ereignis: <area> | <text> (new filter "Events (as in Live)"). So companion, documents, Spark help, writing help, Notaus, service watch, device updates, reMarkable sync, speaker recognition, logins and everything else with a Live line are in the log. What the Spark does by itself with a service (update check, NAS backup, device updates) shows as ereignis: Von selbst | … ok|nicht ok while Logs → Requests is off. - Every line has a filter area. New: reMarkable, Apps, By itself, Improve, System and security, Events; existing areas also take related words now (e.g. conversation also Spark help and writing help, storage also backup). Lines without a fixed word at the start ("memory low", "learned …", "github token", "sealing secrets" …) now start with their area. - "faelle: melder" now names the detector, its fixed sentence (e.g. "12 Fehler in den letzten 24 Stunden") and the case under Status → Improve. - Confirmed action through the MCP server: mcp-ser

head: Logs
title: A log for everything, checked by tests
text: ver: confirmed action <tool> done|fail|no. - Three self-tests turn a new gap red: every line needs a word of logfilter.AREAS; every function behind a Notaus gate writes a line or names where its line comes from; every exception of the admin log has a reason (guard.QUIET_WHY).

head: Logs
title: Logs without contents
text: Logs without contents (since V01.0.513): old lines that still held text now name only fixed words and numbers. Home Assistant writes the length of the spoken command and the number of device words instead of the command, and only the HTTP code instead of the server's answer (device ids like light.wohnzimmer stay, so a wrongly switched device can be found). A note the Spark did not say by itself names its reason and length instead of its text, "hamelden" names the profile via log_name instead of the raw id and, for a rule by voice, only the kind of condition. A fourth self-test turns every new log line red that shows what was said or written, a foreign server's answer or a raw profile id.

head: Logs
title: Errors with a reason instead of "error"
text: Errors with a reason instead of "error" (since V01.0.505, Dominik: log excerpt): requests "by itself" (update check, offsite backup, device updates) name a fixed reason in their line on *Logs → Requests* instead of a bare error: github_limit (60 questions per hour), github_http_401 (GitHub refuses, e.g. the read token), git_ls_remote (GitHub not reachable), keine_gruenen_tests, ohne_git; for the backup http_401 (user or password of the WebDAV folder wrong), zertifikat or the kind of error; for device updates the part that failed (esp32, android, xiaozhi). The lines update check failed: …, esp32: firmware check failed, android: app check failed and geraeteupdate: XiaoZhi check failed now also show under "Errors only". - Device updates reported every check as "not ok" while the Android app was on, even when everything worked (the Android check returns a pair that always counted as an error). Fixed; "no app in the repo yet" is no error. - Settings assistant: a finding that does not change (e.g. "5 errors in the last 24 hours") is no longer counted up every 30 minutes (faelle: melder | - | fehler | 9×); only a changed finding is a new entry. - Meaning search: docembed: no vector for th

head: Logs
title: Errors with a reason instead of "error"
text: e question: names a fixed reason (not running, not enough free memory, model did not start, model files changed, timeout (model busy or slow) …) instead of a bare RuntimeError. A ride along without waking (search locally first, creating documents) while the model sleeps is no error: the journal then says docembed: question without meaning search (model asleep …) and the full text search answers.

head: Logs
title: Telegram: one poller only
text: Telegram: one poller only (since V01.0.214): Telegram hands new messages to one getUpdates at a time. Up to V01.0.213 the panel's startup tasks ran twice (the https server ran them again), and the two Telegram pollers kicked each other out every 15 s ("Conflict: terminated by other getUpdates request"). Now the https server starts without its own startup tasks, and a second poller in the same process is not started. If Telegram still reports a conflict, another program uses the same bot token: the Spark then waits 5 s, 30 s, 1, 2, 5 and at most 10 min, logs only the second and every 20th time (without the token) and shows a hint under Status and Features → Telegram to use the token in one place only or get a new one from @BotFather. A single conflict right after a restart is normal (the old poll runs for up to 25 s).

head: Logs
title: Weather service briefly down
text: Weather service briefly down (since V01.0.214): when Open-Meteo answers the weather note with 5xx or 429 or not at all, the log shows a warning ("retry in 10 min") instead of an error, and the Spark tries again every 10 min within the time window.

head: Logs
title: Web requests in the logs
text: Web requests in the logs (since V01.0.215): for web server lines ("GET /api/… 200 OK") only the status code makes a line red (500 and up), never words in the address. The panel no longer writes the log page's own requests to the journal at all. Update lines quoting a version text ("Available: 46fb0e8 …", "Update finished: …") get no colour (since V01.0.216). The time may read "+0200", "+02:00" or "Z" (since V01.0.217; before, "+02:00" left every area at 0).

head: Logs
title: Detailed diagnosis per area
text: Detailed diagnosis per area (Logs → Advanced): room mode, speakers, Home Assistant and conversation can be switched on for 15 min, 1 h or 4 h; afterwards and on every restart they are off again. They add … detail … lines with numbers and decisions only (recognition time, answer time, word count, duration of a Home Assistant call, history size, offered tools), never heard or written text, names or secrets; redaction still runs. Admin only, rate limited.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
title: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
text: Normally everything runs on the DGX Spark: models, APIs and the panel with the assistant. That stays the default. If you like, the panel and the small services (chats, reminders, speakers, Telegram, logs) move to a small computer of their own, for example a Raspberry Pi 5. The DGX then only serves the models: speech recognition, speech output, pictures and the own language model.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
title: What for
text: What for: the DGX may restart, switch models or be switched off, and chats, calls, reminders, announcements and logs keep running. Voice questions get the fixed sentence "The Spark is taking a break right now." meanwhile (emergency mode), and the Dienst-Wächter reports the outage. With Features → Emergency mode with Parakeet the panel computer then hears by itself and understands a few fixed commands without a language model: lights and devices through Home Assistant, the time and your own reminders. Speakers hear sentences recorded beforehand.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: What you need
title: What you need
text: - Computer for the panel: Raspberry Pi 5 with 8 GB, an NVMe SSD instead of an SD card, wired LAN and a fixed IP address in the router. As the system Raspberry Pi OS Lite 64-bit in the current version (Trixie, Python 3.13), booting from the NVMe. A case like the SunFounder Pironman 5 brings the M.2 slot along; then without an extra NVMe board. Other 64-bit computers with Debian or Ubuntu and Python 3.11 or newer work the same way. - The own language model on the DGX: Spark split reaches the language model through the LLM-Tor. qwen38 cannot be reached from the panel computer, so first sudo speech-spark modelle llm uebernehmen (see Installation). - Both computers in the same home network.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: New install, split
title: New install, split
text: 1. On the DGX: bash sudo ./install.sh --mode api --teilen This installs the models, the TLS-Tor, the Wärter and the firewall and shows a pairing code at the end (6 characters, valid 10 minutes, one use). A new code any time with sudo speech-spark teilen code. 2. On the panel computer: bash git clone https://github.com/db9979/speech-on-dgx-spark cd speech-on-dgx-spark sudo ./install.sh --mode panel --modelle <IP-of-the-DGX> It asks for the code, pairs, installs only the panel (without torch, vLLM or CUDA) and then runs the round trip: speech output speaks a sentence, speech recognition has to understand it.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Moving an existing Spark
title: Moving an existing Spark
text: The panel with all profiles, memory, chats, voices and settings moves in one go.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Moving an existing Spark
title: Moving an existing Spark
text: 1. On the new panel computer install the panel as in step 2 above, but only once the DGX shows the code. 2. On the DGX: sudo speech-spark umziehen --code. It makes a move backup with the vault key (sealed with a random password) and the panel's https certificate and shows the code. 3. While pairing, the new computer fetches the move, restores it, counts the profiles and reports "fertig". On a panel computer that is already installed this also works with sudo speech-spark umziehen --von <IP-of-the-DGX>. 4. Only after this "fertig" does the DGX switch its panel off and run on as the model computer. If something breaks off, the DGX stays as it was. No step deletes anything. 5. By hand afterwards (also listed under Settings → Update for 14 days): - in the router the forward of 31443 and the ports for calls (Features → Chats → "Calls when away") to the new computer, - in Home Assistant Wyoming to <new-computer>:31003, - on every ESP32 speaker the new server address (http://<Pi IP>:31080, over USB under speaker setup; if the board still has the DGX address, the diagnosis and "Check network" say so and name the right one), - the reverse proxy (real certificate for the iPhone app, Android

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Moving an existing Spark
title: Moving an existing Spark
text: app and passkeys) to the new computer; if it runs on another device its address under Settings → Security → Reverse proxy stays right, if it ran on the DGX itself enter the new address there. Otherwise the iPhone app names the certificate in its "Spark not reachable" note.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Moving an existing Spark
title: Moving an existing Spark
text: The apps stay signed in because the panel's certificate moves along. What is changed in the old panel between the backup and the switch does not move; best move while nobody is talking.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Taking it back
title: Taking it back
text: On the panel computer sudo speech-spark umziehen --code, on the DGX sudo speech-spark zurueckholen --von <IP-of-the-panel-computer>. The same way in the other direction; afterwards everything runs on the DGX again, and the panel computer only switches its panel off (its data stays).

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: How the connection is protected
title: How the connection is protected
text: - Nothing crosses between the computers in plain text: the TLS-Tor on the DGX speaks only TLS 1.3 with its own certificate, and the panel computer trusts exactly that one (remembered at the pairing). - The pairing code proves while pairing that both see the same certificate. Whoever stands in between shows another one and gets nothing. - The DGX's firewall lets only the panel computer reach the door's ports. Every command to the Wärter is signed with a key of its own, carries a time stamp and counts only once. - Which version the DGX installs is decided by its own rules, never by the panel computer.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
title: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
text: When the Raspberry Pi sits in the Pironman 5 case, the small display shows the state, the four LEDs light in the status colour and the fans run by temperature. Switch it on under Funktionen → Gehäuse (admin only, shown only on a split Spark): pick "Pironman 5", "Set up" (admin code), then "Restart". Or at install time sudo ./install.sh --gehaeuse pironman5 and restart the Pi afterwards.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
title: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
text: - Set up writes a marked block into /boot/firmware/config.txt (I2C, SPI, fan on GPIO 6 with on and off threshold), loads i2c-dev and gives the service user the groups i2c, spi, gpio. A copy of the old file stays as config.txt.speech-spark-alt. Remove takes only this block out again. - Display (SSD1306, 128×64) changes every few seconds between fourteen pages: Spark, Services and maintenance, Pi (temperature, load, memory), DGX gone or paused, Network, DGX in detail (GPU temperature, free memory, loaded language model), Security (wrong logins and connections the Wächter blocked today, while Live is on, Notaus level), Devices (speakers and apps connected, Verbund), House (Home Assistant, Synology, Kiwix, search as the service watcher sees them), Power (the Pi's under-voltage and throttling, uptime), Version (Pi and DGX the same or different) and Active 10 min (how many people asked something in the last 10 minutes, as one big number, profiles and guests beside it; a profile counts once, also on several devices, a guest per device; what the Spark does by itself never counts; in memory only, without names, also while Logs and Live are off). Also "Pi" and "TARS": CPU and RAM load in per

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
title: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
text: cent as two big numbers, CPU left, RAM right (the TARS page only when the models run on a second computer; on TARS the RAM counts the memory shared with the loaded models, so it often reads 70 to 90 %). The number of active people also shows under Status → Summary ("Active (10 min)"), in Status → Live, in the Steuerzentrale and in the iPhone app's status. When the DGX is gone or paused its page comes first; on a problem the services. While the language model switches or starts, the Spark page comes first and shows the step at the bottom, such as "LLM wechselt (4/6)". Under Funktionen → Gehäuse all pages show as small pictures with the values of now, drawn exactly as on the display: a tap switches a page on or off, dragging or ◀ ▶ changes the order, the big picture shows what is on the display right now. The picture can be turned by 180° (the preview stays upright), "only on problems" keeps it dark otherwise. While an update runs, the display stops its rotation and shows only "Update TARS" or "Update Pi" with a big percentage, a bar and the step (one bar for both: TARS up to 30 %, then the Pi up to 100 %), also at night and with "only on problems", dimmed at night; the LEDs are blue

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
title: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
text: meanwhile. Near the end the panel restarts, so the last picture stays for a few seconds. Then "Update fertig" or "Fehler" stays for a minute before the rotation goes on. Night mode: off, dim or fully off between two hours. Against burn-in the content moves by one or two points every 3 minutes, and a picture that does not change for 10 minutes gets darker. - LEDs: green = all running, yellow = pause, a hint, a service missing or the language model switching, red = DGX not reachable. - Fans are driven by the kernel itself (overlay gpio-fan); the thresholds apply after the next setup and restart.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
title: Case of the panel computer (Pironman 5)
text: The panel never writes system files itself: it leaves a wish and starts the fixed unit speech-spark-gehaeuse, which checks the wish again and writes the block itself from two numbers. Check with sudo speech-spark gehaeuse status; the Live box "Gehäuse" shows display, LEDs and page, the logs are in the area "gehaeuse".

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Both computers in the summary
title: Both computers in the summary
text: When the panel and the models run apart, Status → Summary shows both computers as equals: a tile each on top (the model computer with free memory, GPU and CPU; the panel computer with used memory, CPU, temperature and disk) and below, under "Computers", two cards side by side with curves of the last 20 minutes:

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Both computers in the summary
title: Both computers in the summary
text: - Model computer: GPU with temperature and power, unified memory with the 8 GiB limit, CPU, disk, network, the running language model and its services. The Wärter sends the values with its status. - Panel computer: CPU, memory (used, available, cache), temperature and fan, SD card or SSD, network, power (the Raspberry Pi's under-voltage and throttling) and its services, plus "Panel stalled": how often the hang guard saw the panel stand still in the last 24 hours, and the longest (Security and operation).

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Both computers in the summary
title: Both computers in the summary
text: When the model computer does not answer, its card stays, red with "not answering for …" and its last values grey. Under "Braucht dich" the panel speaks up by fixed rules: the panel computer from 80 °C, throttled or short of power, less than 0.5 GiB memory free; on either computer less than 10 % disk free; the model computer not answering. Each note leads to the cards. The same shows in Status → Live (box "Panel computer", the panel computer's CPU next to the model computer's), in the iPhone app under Überblick (Summary) and in the Android app through the panel view. Only numbers and fixed words, never addresses or processes; on a single Spark the page stays as before. Logs in the area "system" (rechner: hinweis …).

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Control centre on the screen
title: Control centre on the screen
text: A screen on the panel computer's HDMI output shows the control centre: everything on one display, as plain text without a desktop or browser (about 20 MB). Switch it on under Features → Control centre on the screen; then it starts at every boot by itself on the first screen, without signing in. Switching it off ends it, and the normal sign-in comes back.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Control centre on the screen
title: Control centre on the screen
text: - Top: overall state, running requests, notes, maintenance and version, below it the day's numbers (answers, first sound, Wächter, entrance, backup, the screen's times). - Middle: the stages Hören, Weiche, Sprachmodell, Werkzeuge and Sprechen in the frame of the computer they run on; with Spark split tars and the Pi side by side with CPU, GPU, memory, temperature and a 20-minute curve. Every running request has its own colour and visibly jumps between the computers; the ways run underneath the boxes, and a finished answer stays with "fertig in … s" as in the Live view. The Werkzeuge box names every tool in use in the colour of its request, with ▶ running, ✓ done or ✗ failed; on Full HD one name and "+N" for the others. While nothing runs, it shows the tools used last with ✓ or ✗ (on 4K with the time). Every box has a dark surface in its colour and round corners (the console's own palette, reset on exit); the frames of the two computers stay dark. - Left the devices with a request, the connected devices and access over the internet; right the services and targets of the Live view that are in use right now (the others in one line "+ N ready" and "+ N quiet", as in Status → Live), the

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Control centre on the screen
title: Control centre on the screen
text: internet behind the Wächter, "Braucht dich", models and services, the last events, security and maintenance. - Bottom the last 20 minutes as curves (GPU, CPU, free memory, temperature) and the answers per hour.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Control centre on the screen
title: Control centre on the screen
text: The size follows the screen: at the start and whenever the resolution changes, the screen program picks a Terminus font for at least 160 × 45 characters (Full HD about 160 × 45, 4K with a font twice as big about 240 × 67); "smaller" or "larger" takes the next font. A very small screen gets a short list without the flow. Characters the font lacks are replaced by plain ones. Between "Screen off from" and "Screen on from" (default 23 to 7 o'clock, the same hour twice means always on) it turns the screen dark and the monitor sleeps. Against burn-in the picture moves by one or two characters every 3 minutes.

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Control centre on the screen
title: Control centre on the screen
text: Only kind, place, time and numbers are shown, never questions, answers or names: everyone in the room sees it. The screen program asks only the panel on the same computer (127.0.0.1) once a second, with a key of its own that only the service user can read; the panel does not answer other computers or a proxy. A slow answer (up to 8 seconds) or a short hiccup keeps the last picture; only after five failed questions in a row it shows "panel gone". New services of the Live view appear by themselves. Status → Live shows in the box "Control centre" whether it shows right now; the service watch reports when it stops asking. Logs in the area "system" (schirm: …).

file: Spark split: the panel on a computer of its own
head: Checking and finding faults
title: Checking and finding faults
text: The Live box "Model computer" shows whether the DGX is reachable, how many services run, its version and a pause. Technical details: Security and operation and Architecture.

head: What gets installed
title: What gets installed
text: All services run as the system user speech. A sudoers rule lets the panel start, stop and restart the speech services and engines and trigger the update, nothing else.

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance
text: In the panel under Status → Checks → Measure performance, or on the console:

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance
text: Since V01.0.163 every value gets a level (very good, good, tight, too slow) and a sentence saying when it is good; an overall verdict sits on top, and the last run is shown next to each value. The borders are fixed rules in bench.rate():

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance
text: "Words understood" is missing with --audio (the text of your own recording is unknown). The last ten runs' key numbers are kept in bench-history.json.

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance
text: The benchmark goes through the public ports, so it measures what apps see. The last result is stored in /var/lib/speech-spark/state/bench-latest.json. The memory shares of the engines (configuration) are starting values: set them to fit after the measurement.

head: Measuring performance
title: Measuring performance
text: Since V01.0.800 speech output measures several at once three times: the long test text with the set number (--parallel, default 4) and with 2, and when streaming one short answer sentence with the set number, like the first sentence of a real answer. Each request brings along how long it waited in the TTS service (X-Spark-Wait-Ms from common.PrioGate); "Davon in der Warteschlange" (of it in the queue) thus separates waiting for a slot (tts.engine_max_seqs) from the engine's computing. The console shows engine_max_seqs with it.

head: Several voices at once
title: Several voices at once
text: Three settings under Settings → Speech output → Advanced are meant to make the first audio faster when several answers run at once. All are off (as before); switch each on alone and measure performance before and after.

head: Several voices at once
title: Several voices at once
text: - Shorten the reference of your own voice (tts.ref_max_s: off, 8, 10 or 15 s): with a Base model every sentence carries the cloned voice's whole reference recording, and the engine reads all of it before the first audio. When the recording is more than 2 s longer than the limit, the TTS service cuts it once at the quietest point between 60 % of the limit (at least 3 s) and the limit (kurzref.cut_at), has speech recognition on this computer write the piece down and keeps as many words of the voice's own text as it heard (kurzref.keep_words, at least 70 % alike). When it does not fit, the whole recording stays. The piece is kept with its text in voices/kurz/ and applies until the recording or the limit changes; the recording itself stays unchanged. Every result writes a line tts: referenz … to the speech output's log (shortened with seconds, already short, format, speech recognition, does not fit, error), without names or text. - Several voices at once (tts.engine_decode_batch: 1, 2 or 4): the decoder (Code2Wav) computes up to 2 or 4 voices together, with CUDA graphs for 1 to n voices (decode_batch_max_size, decode_cudagraph_batch_sizes, like vllm-omni's profiles for many requests).

head: Several voices at once
title: Several voices at once
text: Takes a little more memory and time at start. - Remember the same beginning (tts.engine_prefix_cache): the talker remembers the part of the prompt that is the same in every sentence of the same voice (enable_prefix_caching for stage 0).

head: Several voices at once
title: Several voices at once
text: engine.sh writes both engine values into the deploy file (state/tts-deploy-main.yaml) and the stage values; a change restarts speech output. vllm-omni 0.30 already bounds the decoder's reference context to 72 frames itself (ref_code_context_frames follows codec_left_context_frames).

head: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
text: The language model runs either as the own vLLM behind the LLM-Tor (sudo ./install.sh --llm, then sudo speech-spark modelle llm uebernehmen, back with … zurueck) or, as before, from dgx-spark-qwen38. With the Spark split only the own one works, because the panel computer cannot reach qwen38. The points below about lanes and the cockpit only apply while qwen38 runs.

head: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
text: - Ports: qwen38 uses 30000 to 30099 (engine 30000, proxy 30001, image 30020, video 30022, cockpit 30090/30091). Speech uses 31001 (ASR), 31002 (TTS), 31003 (Wyoming), 31005 (pictures), 31006 (LLM-Tor), 31080 and 31443 (panel over https), plus UDP 31060 and 31062–31068 for the phone; the engines on 31011, 31012, 31013, 31015, 31016 and 31017 listen on 127.0.0.1 only, as do the Wärter (31007) and the emergency mode (31009). The full list is in the architecture. The panel rejects ports in qwen38's range, and the installer stops if a port is taken. - Memory: the GB10 has one 128 GB pool shared by CPU and GPU. The qwen38 lanes reserve a fixed share of it: 50 % with stock/fp8, 76 % in 1M mode and 85 % with flash. According to the qwen38 docs only ~16.6 GiB stay free at idle with flash, and below ~8 GiB DGX OS's earlyoom kills processes. Therefore: - If the installer detects a flash or 1M lane, it picks the 0.6B models. - Before a service loads its model it checks that the reserve stays free afterwards (default 10 GiB). If not, it does not load and the panel shows blocked with the reason. - If memory still runs short, the system kills the panel first (OOMScoreAdjust=900), then the speech

head: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
text: services (500), not the LLM lane and not sshd (see "Speech first"). - Speech starts after the qwen38 lanes, so they take their fixed share first. - Engines start one after another, because vLLM measures free memory at start-up and parallel starts take each other's share. Order: own language model, speech recognition, speech output, VoiceDesign, image understanding. Each waits while one before it stops, restarts or loads, at most an hour (engine.sh). install.sh restarts an engine only when its settings changed or it is not running, also on a run by hand, and the language model first (since V01.0.680). Before, a run such as install.sh --musik 2b restarted every engine, the language model last. It then loaded while speech output measured its memory, and speech output failed every 30 seconds with "No available memory for the cache blocks". To restart one on purpose: sudo systemctl restart speech-spark-<engine>. Since V01.0.775 every engine also waits while a model measurement has its engine running (speech-spark-messen-engine): on tars speech output restarted while the measured engine broke off, counted the memory freed meanwhile as its own and took 83 instead of 5 GiB; the language mo

head: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
title: Language model: own or dgx-spark-qwen38
text: del then found no room (self-test test_no_start_next_to_a_measurement). - Lane switch: if you switch to flash in the cockpit, already loaded speech models stay in memory. With 1.7B models that can get too tight. Stop ASR and TTS in the panel first or switch them to 0.6B. - GPU time: ASR and TTS share the GPU with the LLM. During a transcription or speech request the LLM gets a little slower.

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: Speech recognition and speech output always come first (fixed rule without a switch, since V01.0.225, plan plaene/vorrang-sprache.md).

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: - When "speech is running": while an answer of /api/chat streams (browser, app, speakers, Telegram, Siri) and while ASR or TTS handle a request from anyone (Open WebUI and Wyoming too). The services report it through common.SpeechMark: every POST /v1/audio/... request that passed the size limit and API key touches state/speech-active. 20 seconds after that still count (follow-up question). - Background work waits during that time; its running request to the language model is cancelled (vLLM stops it when the connection closes) and repeated in the next pause, at most three times. Only one background request runs at a time. Connected: learning from conversations, memory tidy, agents, proactive notes, daily briefing, mail sorting, quality test, reading documents and meaning search (wissen.quiet()), backup (also with low CPU priority). - New hint in health.alerts: add it to live.hints too, with its place in the picture and fixed words. - New event in the audit log (guard.log): a fixed word in guard.LIVE_WORDS, then it shows under events. A line from anywhere: live.mark(area, text); something the Spark does by itself with a service: live.job(why, tool, t0, ok). - Interface for new backg

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: round work (app/panel/vorrang.py): - r = await vorrang.post(c, "Name", url, json=..., headers=...): one request to the language model (httpx client c): waits, runs alone, is cancelled on speech and repeated; gives up with vorrang.Busy after three cancellations. - await vorrang.run("Name", lambda: coroutine()): the same for any other coroutine. - await vorrang.quiet("Name"): only wait for a pause. - await vorrang.in_thread("Name", fn, *args): CPU work (e.g. an embedding model) after a pause in its own thread with nice 15. - vorrang.hold("Name"): inside a worker thread, wait between two steps while speech runs (never call it on the event loop). - vorrang.speaking(): whether speech is running. - Operating system: the ASR and TTS services and their engines run with Nice=-5, CPUWeight=1000, IOWeight=1000. When memory runs out, the system ends the panel first (OOMScoreAdjust=900), then the speech services (500), not the LLM lane and not sshd. - GPU: the GB10 has no priorities between processes. The speech engines' memory is reserved from their start. The language model's own answer runs at the same time as the speech output and sometimes slows it down ("tts behind … inside the piece"). S

head: Speech first
title: Speech first
text: ince V01.0.430 the panel therefore sends the next piece to the speech output at 5 s of audio in stock while the answer is still being written (times the speaking rate, so 6 s at 1.2; chat.WRITE_LEAD), afterwards at 2 to 3 s as before. The iPhone app collects 0.4 s of audio after it ran dry before it plays on, and starts with a 5 ms fade-in after silence. - Checking: Status → Checks → "Speech first" speaks a sentence alone, under load without priority and under load with priority, and shows first audio, real-time factor and recognition time, above it today's counters. Status → Logs shows the lines in the area "Priority" (vorrang: … wartet, … abgebrochen, … wartete N s).

head: Priority for people
title: Priority for people
text: When several people talk at once, chosen profiles get their answer first (since V01.0.282, plan plaene/vorrang-personen.md). Off by default.

head: Priority for people
title: Priority for people
text: - Switching on: Funktionen → Gespräch → "Vorrang für Personen" (chat.person_priority, feature register vorrang). Only the admin sets the stage per profile under People and devices, at the profile under Rights "Priority": "Vorrang" (three profiles at most), "normal" or "hinten anstellen" (last in line). Stored in state/personen-vorrang.json (in the backup), changes in the admin log (person_priority). Under Me the profile sees the function as on or "off for you". - Who asks: only from the sign-in (browser, app, device key), never from the text. Guests and programs without a profile (Open WebUI, Wyoming) are always normal. At a shared speaker the stage counts only when the speaker recognition heard the profile's voice; the recording itself goes to the recognition as normal there, because the voice is known only afterwards. - Speech output and recognition: both services let only as many requests go to the engine at once as it takes (tts.engine_max_seqs, asr.engine_max_seqs); the rest wait in the service (common.PrioGate) by stage, then by arrival. A running request is never stopped. Every 4 s of waiting move a request one stage up, so nobody starves. At most 64 wait, else 503. A slot c

title: Priority for people
text: omes back after 90 s at the latest, even when a device dropped the connection before its stream began. - Language model (since V01.0.284): while an answer with priority has no first sentence yet, new rounds of other people wait at most chat.person_priority_wait seconds (0–5, default 2) before they go to the language model (stufe.wait_turn). Running answers are never stopped; an answer without a first sentence holds others for 30 s at most. Logs → Anfragen shows "waited … for an answer with priority" at the round, journal vorrang: Antwort wartete N s auf eine Antwort mit Vorrang. - Early notice: the browser and the iPhone app send POST /api/vorrang/spricht when a recording starts (profile or device key, at most 60 per minute). If the profile has priority, background work stops at once and the language model gate closes for 15 s at most, until the question arrives. The answer is the same for everybody, so it does not tell who has priority. Shared speakers do not send it. - Who may say the stage: only the panel. It sends X-Spark-Stufe (0, 1, 2) together with the key from state/vorrang-key (made once by the panel, mode 0600, not in the backup). The services believe it only from 127.0.0

title: Priority for people
text: .1 and only with that key; everybody else is normal, even with the API key. - Seeing it: Status → Logs → Anfragen shows "with priority" at the arrival and, at speech output, how long the sentences queued and how many they overtook. Journal: vorrang: Stufe 2 überholt N wartende Anfrage(n). The services' /health shows slots, waiting requests and counters under queue. - Measuring: Status → Checks → "Speech first" also measures the case "two people at once": the speech output is full with sentences of others (all slots plus two waiting), then one more sentence comes, once normal and once with priority. It shows the first audio of both. - Limits: the language model knows no order; Open WebUI and other programs that ask it directly are not held back. With one person talking nothing gets faster.

head: Why the installation looks like this
title: Why the installation looks like this
text: - PyTorch from the cu130 index: the aarch64 torch on PyPI has no CUDA, so a plain pip install qwen-tts would run on the CPU. torch and torchaudio must come from the same index, otherwise libtorchaudio.so does not load. - No flash-attn: there is no ARM wheel, and it reportedly does not build for sm_121. Both models use PyTorch SDPA instead. - Separate venvs for the transformers backends: qwen-asr needs transformers==4.57.6, qwen-tts transformers==4.57.3. - ASR with vLLM: vLLM 0.30 supports Qwen3-ASR natively, with /v1/audio/transcriptions, streaming and concurrent requests. It shares the environment with the TTS engine. qwen-asr[vllm] is not needed (it would force vllm 0.14). - TTS with vllm-omni: qwen-tts cannot stream. The Qwen team points to vllm-omni for streaming. vllm 0.30.0 and vllm-omni 0.30.0 have ARM wheels on PyPI (CUDA 13) and are installed natively, without Docker. - Engine memory: vLLM reserves a fixed share of the *whole* memory pool at start-up, for TTS per stage (talker and code2wav). The defaults (ASR 1.7B 0.06, 0.6B 0.035; TTS 0.04 + 0.025) are kept small so speech fits next to the qwen38 stock lane. If a share is too small, the engine stops at start-up with "No a

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: How the parts work together, the way of a request and every storage place are in Architecture and data flow and in the panel under Status → Architecture. In the picture every box has a colour bar on the left for its kind (legend top right: devices, access and protection, conversation, knowledge, mail and contacts, operation, models, storage, outside) and a symbol before its line; arrows show the direction, a tab marks what exists only with the Spark split (V01.0.915, technik.FARBE, SYMBOL, NUR_BEI). test_technik checks that every text fits its box and no line runs across a box.

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: One answer of the assistant runs through three files in app/panel/:

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: - chat_turn.py (prepare): who is speaking and what they may use (profile, recognized voice, device key, Telegram, iPhone app), the system prompt, answers to waiting proposals ("yes" to an appointment, mail change, correction ...), the tools on offer and the locks after outside text. The result is a Turn with all values. - chat_tools.py (run): what a tool call does (web search, Home Assistant, mail, calendar, reminders ...). Only offered tools run; the locks are checked here again. - chat.py (_answer): asks the language model in rounds, runs tool calls through chat_tools.run, checks the answer and streams text and sound. Tool definitions and lock lists (READS_OUTSIDE, LOCKED_OUTSIDE ...) stay in chat.py.

head: How the chat is built
title: How the chat is built
text: New rights or hints go into chat_turn.py, new tools into chat_tools.py (definition and lock list in chat.py).

head: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
title: Keeping the live overview current (live.py)
text: - New tool: a target in live.TOOLS (an existing one or a new one in live.TARGETS with zone spark, lan or net) and a word in live.RETURNS. tests/test_live.py turns red when a tool from chat.py or an extra service is missing. - New kind of device: a word in live.CLIENT (the test compares with tracelog.CLIENTS). - New channel (WebSocket, long poll): a line in live._conns. - Request without a conversation (only hearing or only speaking, e.g. Wyoming): rec = live.begin(client, device), then rec.step("asr"|"tts", …) and live.end(rec, ok); refused senders with live.door(...). - Something the Spark does by itself (rule, reminder, task): live.begin(client, "", uid=…, auto=True, why="fixed word") and the steps below it inside with live.within(rec): (no way back to a device). Notes are reported by push.send itself (live.note, targets Web Push, Apple Push, Android app, Telegram); a new tag gets a word in push.WHY. - Background work runs through vorrang.run/post/in_thread/quiet/hold with a fixed name; that reports it to live.bg itself (no contents in the name). - New entry check or guard level: guard.failed and netguard.resolve already report to live.refused and live.outgoing; add new words the

head: Tests
title: Tests
text: app/tests/ holds the self-tests that run on every update (cd app && python -m unittest discover -s tests). All services are faked (tests/helpers.py); no test talks to real models or Home Assistant. tests/test_ui_browser.py also opens the panel in Chromium (Playwright) at computer and phone width: every page without script errors and without sideways scrolling, the settings search, the Me window. Without Playwright (as in the self-test on the Spark) it is skipped; on GitHub it runs in the "Tests" workflow on every push. There everything runs in four parts at the same time (python selftest.py discover -s tests --part K/4, cut by test module and its duration in tests/dauer.json, the long browser test test by test); the job "Ergebnis" checks that every part reported and counts the failures over the whole run.

head: Troubleshooting
title: Troubleshooting
